  - article:
    - heading "Rail vehicle model Historic and domestic bus manufacturers" [level=1]:
      - img "Rail vehicle model"
      - text: Historic and domestic bus manufacturers
    - paragraph: What Taipei's buses actually were before the current import-and-electrify era — two dated 1970s/80s fleet purchases, and the domestic coachbuilders that bodied imported chassis after privatisation.
    - region "Quick facts":
      - text: Historic and domestic bus manufacturers
      - term: First air-conditioned route
      - definition:
        - text: 中1路 (later 601), 1 July 1976, Mercedes-Benz L508D × 30
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - term: 1980 "self-strengthening" purchase
      - definition:
        - text: Hino BM400 × 60, plus Hino BY420 on new routes
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - term: Metropolitan Bus's post-privatisation body-builder
      - definition:
        - text: 日盈機械, later 國際山霖汽車
        - superscript:
          - link "[2]":
            - /url: "#ref-2"
      - term: 國際山霖汽車 closure — conflict, see body
      - definition: TBC
    - navigation "On this page":
      - paragraph: On this page
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - link "The two dated purchases anyone has found":
            - /url: "#the-two-dated-purchases-anyone-has-found"
        - listitem:
          - link "The oldest specific model still findable at operator level":
            - /url: "#the-oldest-specific-model-still-findable-at-operator-level"
        - listitem:
          - link "Domestic coachbuilders, after privatisation":
            - /url: "#domestic-coachbuilders-after-privatisation"
        - listitem:
          - link "What this site searched and found nothing":
            - /url: "#what-this-site-searched-and-found-nothing"
        - listitem:
          - link "What remains open":
            - /url: "#what-remains-open"
        - listitem:
          - link "References":
            - /url: "#references"
    - paragraph:
      - text: "This site's existing bus-model pages cover the current era: electric buses since roughly 2019, and the imported diesel/coach chassis (Hino, Isuzu, Mercedes-Benz, Volvo, Scania, MAN) on the market now. What"
      - link "Taipei":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
      - text: "'s fleets actually were in the 1970s through the 1990s is barely documented anywhere in Mandarin or English, and this page reports exactly how little survives rather than filling the gap with a plausible guess."
    - heading "The two dated purchases anyone has found" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: zh.wikipedia's article on public minibuses names two specific fleet purchases for Taipei
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: ", and this site checked directly that no other source repeats either one, including a sibling Wikipedia article on the same general topic. Both figures are carried at Medium confidence for that reason."
    - paragraph:
      - strong: 1 July 1976
      - text: ", Taipei's first air-conditioned bus route, predecessor of today's 601, began service using 30 Mercedes-Benz"
      - strong: L508D
      - text: small air-conditioned buses
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - strong: 6 September 1980
      - text: ", the city added 60 Hino"
      - strong: BM400
      - text: small air-conditioned buses, described as marking a "self-strengthening year" (自強年) after the 1979 US–Taiwan derecognition — the same year saw Hino
      - strong: BY420
      - text: large air-conditioned buses (11.55 m) introduced on new routes
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: ". Quoted directly:"
    - blockquote:
      - paragraph:
        - text: 1980年9月6日起，添購60輛[日野]BM400型小型冷氣巴士
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: Route renumbering (中1 → 601 and others) is dated to the same September 1980 changeover
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . This site found nothing naming a manufacturer, model or operator for any Taipei bus before 1976, or for the years between these two purchases and the mid-1990s.
    - heading "The oldest specific model still findable at operator level" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Enthusiast fleet-tracking pages (zh.wikiversity, uncited, treated as leads rather than sources) name a 1995-model-year Hino
      - strong: LRG2KRB
      - text: at 光華巴士 as the oldest specific vehicle record this site found surviving for any of the 14 聯營 operators, alongside two retired Hino models,
      - strong: LRK2JMA
      - text: (fully retired) and
      - strong: LRK2JMB
      - text: (transferred to 基隆客運). None of this is independently corroborated against a primary source and is reported here only as the practical limit of what this site could trace.
    - heading "Domestic coachbuilders, after privatisation" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Once Metropolitan Bus (大都會客運) was formed by privatising the municipal operator in 2004, its early vehicle purchases paired
      - strong: imported Isuzu large-bus chassis with bodies built by a domestic coachbuilder, 日盈機械
      - text: ", later renamed"
      - strong: 國際山霖汽車
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . That coachbuilder went on to acquire shares in Metropolitan Bus from former employees — becoming a shareholder in the operator whose buses it was bodying
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - strong: When 國際山霖汽車 closed is not settled.
      - text: zh.wikipedia's Metropolitan Bus article gives "late 2009" for a bankruptcy that ended the chassis-body pairing and shifted subsequent purchases to Daewoo vehicles distributed by 成運汽車
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . An independent company-registry mirror gives a formal dissolution date of
      - strong: 23 October 2013
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: . Both are published; neither source explains the four-year gap, and this page does not pick one — it may be the ordinary difference between ceasing to trade and a company's legal dissolution, but no source says so.
    - paragraph:
      - text: "Other domestic body-builders surface in enthusiast operator-fleet pages (zh.wikiversity, uncited, Medium confidence at best):"
      - strong: 健益
      - text: ", bodying 大有巴士's Mitsubishi Fuso RK127JL;"
      - strong: 豐榮
      - text: ", bodying 大南汽車's Hino ERK2JRL/ERK2JML and, separately, a Daewoo BC211MA for 指南客運;"
      - strong: 柏昇車體
      - text: ", a body variant for 指南客運's Mitsubishi Fuso RM11FN2XC."
      - strong: 成運
      - text: (成運汽車) appears repeatedly across several operators as both a Daewoo-brand distributor and a body-builder in its own right. None of these was independently verified beyond the single uncited fleet page naming it.
    - paragraph:
      - strong: 中興巴士's own general characterisation
      - text: "of its historic fleet, quoted directly and undated: 「中興巴士採用的車輛廠牌以日本製造的日野及三菱扶桑為主」 — Hino and Mitsubishi Fuso, mainly"
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: .
    - heading "What this site searched and found nothing" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "This site read China Motor Corporation (中華汽車工業)'s own Wikipedia history, covering 1969 onward: trucks, light commercial vehicles, cars, vans and electric motorcycles — no bus or bus chassis anywhere in the article. Ford Liuho (福特六和/六和汽車)'s history, from 1969, covers Toyota-then-Ford passenger and light-commercial vehicles, and this site found no bus connection. San Fu (三富汽車), often mentioned as a candidate domestic manufacturer, assembled Isuzu Trooper, Isuzu Panther and Hyundai Accent under contract before closing in 1999 — this site found no source connecting it to bus bodies. Two 7car.tw articles that appeared, by title, to cover early Taiwan-made coaches and the domestic body-building process could not be reached at all (see below), so their content is not reported here."
    - heading "What remains open" [level=2]
    - paragraph: This site found nothing naming a manufacturer for any Taipei bus before 1976. The fifteen years between the 1980 Hino purchase and the 1995 光華巴士 record have no source at all — not a search failure to retry, a genuine absence across zh.wikipedia, zh.wikiversity, Taiwanese news archives (聯合報 and 中國時報's 1980s archives require paid access, not checked), and the Taipei Public Transport Office's own history page, which returned HTTP 404 at the URL found. Yulon (裕隆汽車)'s own corporate history names "flat-nose large coaches" (平頭大客車) as an early product line with no date, model or customer — whether this reached Taipei city-bus service is unconfirmed. This site's search surfaced two 7car.tw articles describing early domestic coachbuilding by title, but could not fetch either — the whole domain returned a connection failure on every attempt.
    - region "References":
      - heading "References" [level=2]
      - paragraph: 0 of 4 sources on this page are primary — published by the operator, the builder or government.
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - link "Public minibuses":
            - /url: https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/公共小型巴士
          - text: "公共小型巴士 secondary 維基百科 (Chinese Wikipedia) accessed 2026-08-28 The only source found for either 1970s/80s claim; carries no footnote for either sentence and is not corroborated by a sibling Wikipedia article on the same general topic (空調巴士, checked directly and found to contain neither claim). Quoted directly: 「1980年9月6日起，添購60輛[日野]BM400型小型冷氣巴士」."
        - listitem:
          - link "Metropolitan Bus":
            - /url: https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/大都會客運
          - text: 大都會客運 secondary 維基百科 (Chinese Wikipedia) accessed 2026-08-28 Fetched twice, consistent both times; the article itself carries a "missing sources" banner for this passage. Supports the Isuzu-chassis/日盈機械-body pairing after 2004 privatisation and the operator/shareholder relationship that followed.
        - listitem:
          - link "國際山霖汽車股份有限公司 company registry entry":
            - /url: https://www.twincn.com/27781611
          - text: 國際山霖汽車股份有限公司 secondary 台灣公司網 (Taiwan company registry mirror) accessed 2026-08-28 A registry-mirror site, not the Ministry of Economic Affairs' own portal directly. Supports the company's Banqiao address and a 23 October 2013 dissolution date, which conflicts with zh.wikipedia's "late 2009" bankruptcy claim — see the conflict below.
        - listitem:
          - link "Zhongxing Bus":
            - /url: https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/中興巴士
          - text: "中興巴士 secondary 維基百科 (Chinese Wikipedia) accessed 2026-08-28 Quoted directly for its one-sentence brand characterisation: 「中興巴士採用的車輛廠牌以日本製造的日野及三菱扶桑為主」. Undated, no footnote."

    - heading "An unreconciled delivery record for Capital Bus Group" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "Two company news items give different cumulative delivery counts to the same operator, Capital Bus Group, and neither is picked over the other:"
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - strong: 139 buses purchased cumulatively since 2022 (民國111年), plus a further 92 tendered for Q4 delivery
        - text: — from a dedicated announcement of the 92-bus order
        - superscript:
          - link "[5]":
            - /url: "#ref-5"
        - text: .
      - listitem:
        - strong: 26 buses delivered in January 2025, plus 70 more "within the year"
        - text: — from the March 2025 trade-show coverage above
        - superscript:
          - link "[4]":
            - /url: "#ref-4"
        - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: These do not obviously combine into one running total from what either source states, and neither article cross-references the other's figures
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: .
    - heading "Fleet-scale figures, published separately" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "Three different production/fleet figures appear across sources measuring different things:"
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - strong: 400+ electric buses delivered nationwide
        - text: ", an undated figure from the manufacturer's own site"
        - superscript:
          - link "[2]":
            - /url: "#ref-2"
        - text: .
      - listitem:
        - strong: 350 electric buses operating nationwide
        - text: ", dated to the 2024 trade show"
        - superscript:
          - link "[3]":
            - /url: "#ref-3"
        - text: .
      - listitem:
        - strong: 6,000+ buses produced all-time
        - text: ", including non-electric models, with a reported diesel-era peak of over 800 buses sold in one year and revenue above NT$4 billion — a different, broader measure than the electric-only figures above, not comparable to them directly"
        - superscript:
          - link "[8]":
            - /url: "#ref-8"
        - text: .
    - heading "Technical gaps" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: No source establishes chassis/body-builder division of labour, door count for the intercity model, or a floor-type claim for the intercity model (unlike the three urban models, none of which is named "low-floor" on the manufacturer's own page)

      - text: . The Erlin (彰化二林) plant's planned annual capacity is stated by the company's own profile page only as "20,000 KD units"

    - paragraph:
      - text: This page lists 1500 static TDX station rows in Kaohsiung's Unclassified group, with a published capacity total of 30382 docks. TDX's Station/City feed supplies identity, bilingual names, addresses, coordinates and capacity; that feed does not carry current occupancy
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The rail column is a nearest-coordinate join against the committed TDX rail station registry. It is shown only for a unique result within 200 metres; station names are not used to create a match
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . The feed did not expose a usable district for these rows, so they remain in an explicit Unclassified group rather than being assigned from a guessed address or station name
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - heading "Snapshot detail" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Kaohsiung's Unclassified group section is a build-time view of 1500 returned TDX Station/City records, not a live occupancy display
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . The normalized rows retain 1500 English station names, 1500 Traditional Chinese station names, and 1500 valid coordinate pairs; the source response also supplies station identifiers, addresses, service type, capacity and source-update timestamps
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The published capacity values in this group range from 10 to 99 docks per row, with the total shown above calculated by summing the returned BikesCapacity fields
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: ". The observed ServiceType distribution is 2: 1500, so a missing or null service value is not converted into an assumed operating category"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The TDX records used for this page carried UpdateTime value(s) 2026-08-25T23:38:06+08:00
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . Those timestamps date the source response, while the page frontmatter records the retrieval date; neither timestamp is presented as a prediction of future station availability
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: Representative rows in this group are station ID 501216070 (17 docks; YouBike2.0_阿公店柳橋西路口), station ID 501228004 (16 docks; YouBike2.0_阿公店森林公園) and station ID 501228003 (39 docks; YouBike2.0_阿公店水庫停車場)
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . They remain rows in a browse index because the source provides a compact identity, address, coordinate and capacity record; creating a separate article for every dock would repeat the same source fields without adding a sourced history or design record
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The nearby-rail column is conservative: 0 rows have a confirmed coordinate join in this group"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . A match is retained only when one nearest candidate is within 200 metres and not tied at the one-metre ambiguity threshold, and the calculation compares coordinates rather than station names
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . Current available bikes and return docks are deliberately outside this static page because TDX publishes those values through a separate availability feed
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .

  - heading "Network" [level=1]
  - paragraph: The joint-operation system — one brand, one fare structure, many private companies — and the route numbering that encodes more than it appears to.
  - paragraph:
    - text: "The page this folder exists for is an explainer, not a listing: how 聯營公車 works — who sets fares, who owns the buses, what the city controls and what the companies do — and how the route numbering system encodes direction suffixes, short-workings, branches, trunk routes and minibus services in ways no English source explains."
    - strong: One of those pages is now written
    - text: — see
    - link "the joint-operation network":
      - /url: /bus/network/joint-operation/
    - text: ". Writing it cost this section most of what it thought it knew. Several claims that had been sitting in research notes did not survive their first check against the regulator: the numeric bands turned out to have a competing and better-sourced explanation, the feeder-colour table was missing a line, and the revenue-pooling model that was supposed to be the whole point of the page is not described by the office that runs the system. What is published is what survived those checks."
  - paragraph:
    - text: "A second page covers the national programme reshaping what those buses run on:"
    - link "the 2030 electrification programme":
      - /url: /bus/network/electric-bus-programme/
    - text: ", a NT$64.3 billion plan"
    - superscript:
      - link "[1]":
        - /url: "#ref-1"
    - text: the Legislative Yuan's own oversight documents record as running well behind its own interim targets
    - superscript:
      - link "[1]":
        - /url: "#ref-1"
    - text: ". A third covers how the joint-operation committee decides who runs the routes it has just described:"
    - link "operator service ratings":
      - /url: /bus/network/operator-ratings/
    - text: ", a twice-yearly graded evaluation running since 1992"
    - superscript:
      - link "[2]":

    - text: that ties directly into the route-points mechanism above

      - link "[2]":
        - /url: "#ref-2"
    - text: .
  - paragraph: 3 entries
  - list:
    - listitem:
      - link "The joint-operation network Around 280 routes, fourteen private companies and one brand. Four city regulations set out how the money actually moves — and the central revenue pool everyone repeats is in none of them.":
        - /url: /bus/network/joint-operation/
    - listitem:
      - link "Operator service ratings Twice a year since 1992, Taipei has graded its bus operators 優/甲/乙/丙/丁 on 26 indicators — and the grade can cost an operator its routes. It is a national requirement, not a Taipei quirk — New Taipei, Taoyuan, Taichung, Kaohsiung and Tainan each run their own separate scheme.":

    - listitem:
      - link "The 2030 electrification programme A NT$64.3 billion, seven-year national programme to convert Taiwan's bus fleet to electric — and the Legislative Yuan's own record of it running well behind target.":

    - paragraph:
      - text: This page lists 1567 static TDX station rows in New
      - link "Taipei":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
      - text: "'s Unclassified group, with a published capacity total of 47489 docks. TDX's Station/City feed supplies identity, bilingual names, addresses, coordinates and capacity; that feed does not carry current occupancy"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The rail column is a nearest-coordinate join against the committed TDX rail station registry. It is shown only for a unique result within 200 metres; station names are not used to create a match
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . The feed did not expose a usable district for these rows, so they remain in an explicit Unclassified group rather than being assigned from a guessed address or station name
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - heading "Snapshot detail" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The New Taipei's Unclassified group section is a build-time view of 1567 returned TDX Station/City records, not a live occupancy display
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . The normalized rows retain 1567 English station names, 1567 Traditional Chinese station names, and 1567 valid coordinate pairs; the source response also supplies station identifiers, addresses, service type, capacity and source-update timestamps
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The published capacity values in this group range from 8 to 99 docks per row, with the total shown above calculated by summing the returned BikesCapacity fields
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: ". The observed ServiceType distribution is 2: 1567, so a missing or null service value is not converted into an assumed operating category"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The TDX records used for this page carried UpdateTime value(s) 2026-08-25T23:37:06+08:00
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . Those timestamps date the source response, while the page frontmatter records the retrieval date; neither timestamp is presented as a prediction of future station availability
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: Representative rows in this group are station ID 500205047 (10 docks; YouBike2.0_國慶學成路口), station ID 500233030 (15 docks; YouBike2.0_鷺江國中(長興路298巷)) and station ID 500231042 (25 docks; YouBike2.0_柑園五里聯合活動中心)
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . They remain rows in a browse index because the source provides a compact identity, address, coordinate and capacity record; creating a separate article for every dock would repeat the same source fields without adding a sourced history or design record
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The nearby-rail column is conservative: 135 rows have a confirmed coordinate join in this group"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . A match is retained only when one nearest candidate is within 200 metres and not tied at the one-metre ambiguity threshold, and the calculation compares coordinates rather than station names
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . Current available bikes and return docks are deliberately outside this static page because TDX publishes those values through a separate availability feed
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .

- main:
  - navigation "Breadcrumb":

  - article:
    - heading "The 2030 electrification programme" [level=1]
    - paragraph: A NT$64.3 billion, seven-year national programme to convert Taiwan's bus fleet to electric — and the Legislative Yuan's own record of it running well behind target.
    - region "Quick facts":
      - text: The 2030 electrification programme
      - term: Programme
      - definition:
        - text: 2030年客運車輛電動化推動計畫
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - term: Approved
      - definition:
        - text: 26 May 2023
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - term: Period
      - definition:
        - text: 民國113–119年 (2024–2030)
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - term: Total budget
      - definition:
        - text: NT$64.327 billion
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - term: Highway Bureau share
      - definition:
        - text: NT$45.0835 billion
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - term: Ministry of Environment share
      - definition:
        - text: NT$19.2432 billion
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - term: Vehicle target, 2030
      - definition:
        - text: 14,500 buses
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - term: City bus target, 2030
      - definition:
        - text: 11,700 buses
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - term: Intercity/national coach target, 2030
      - definition:
        - text: 2,800 buses
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
    - navigation "On this page":
      - paragraph: On this page
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - 'link "The Legislative Yuan''s own record: running behind target"':
            - /url: "#the-legislative-yuans-own-record-running-behind-target"
        - listitem:
          - link "Registered fleet — several figures, several scopes":
            - /url: "#registered-fleet--several-figures-several-scopes"
        - listitem:
          - link "Gaps":
            - /url: "#gaps"
        - listitem:
          - link "Specifications":
            - /url: "#specifications"
        - listitem:
          - link "References":
            - /url: "#references"
    - paragraph:
      - text: 行政院 approved MOTC's 2030年客運車輛電動化推動計畫 on 26 May 2023, running 民國113–119年 (2024–2030) with a total budget of NT$64.327 billion, split between the Highway Bureau (公路局, NT$45.0835 billion) and the Ministry of Environment (環境部, NT$19.2432 billion)
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . The target is 14,500 electric buses by 2030 — 11,700 city buses and 2,800 intercity, general highway and national-coach vehicles
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: ". A government-linked testing foundation frames the programme in three phases: a completed pilot phase (民國109–111年/2020–2022), the current rollout phase (112–115年/2023–2026), and a universalisation phase (116–119年/2027–2030) — a breakdown not found on any MOTC or Executive Yuan primary page checked for this page"
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: .
    - 'heading "The Legislative Yuan''s own record: running behind target" [level=2]'
    - paragraph: Three Legislative Yuan committee review documents, all read in full, give a consistent picture of a programme behind its own interim targets.
    - paragraph:
      - text: As of August 2024, city electric buses stood at 1,817 (17.31% penetration) against a stated 2024 target of 3,300 buses at 25%
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . First-half 2024 manufacturing output was just 50 vehicles against an annual target of 1,070, with full-year capacity estimated at only 1,700–1,900 vehicles nationally
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . Purchase-subsidy execution for the year stood at NT$412.411 million — 17.2% of the annual budget
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . Several counties, including Keelung,
      - link "Hsinchu":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/hsinchu/
      - text: City,
      - link "Miaoli":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/miaoli/
      - text: ", Nantou and Penghu, showed close to 0% penetration"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: A separate committee review, covering the same period from a different angle, gives the 2024 target as 3,400 buses at 25% — the same percentage as the figure above but 100 vehicles apart, with no source explaining the difference
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: . The same document sets the FY2025 (114年度) budget at NT$6.8575 billion, split into vehicle-purchase subsidy (NT$5.92 billion), operating subsidy (NT$797.2 million), route-network optimisation (NT$130.8 million) and maintenance-system support (NT$9.5 million), with a 2025 target of 5,000 city buses at 35% penetration
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: .
    - heading "Registered fleet — several figures, several scopes" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Published as separate measurements rather than one series, because they mix different scopes (national vs. city-only) and bases (plated-and-operating, registered, subsidy-approved, or domestically-manufactured only)
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: ", and no source bridges them:"
    - table:
      - rowgroup:
        - row "Date Figure What it measures":
          - columnheader "Date"
          - columnheader "Figure"
          - columnheader "What it measures"
      - rowgroup:
        - row "Nov 2024 1,926 buses nationally plated National, all electric buses[4]":
          - cell "Nov 2024"
          - cell "1,926 buses nationally plated"
          - cell "National, all electric buses[4]":
            - text: National, all electric buses
            - superscript:
              - link "[4]":
                - /url: "#ref-4"
        - row "Oct 2024 1,876 actual, ~4,000 projected by end-2025 National, domestically-manufactured subset only[5]":
          - cell "Oct 2024"
          - cell "1,876 actual, ~4,000 projected by end-2025"
          - cell "National, domestically-manufactured subset only[5]":
            - text: National, domestically-manufactured subset only
            - superscript:
              - link "[5]":
                - /url: "#ref-5"
        - row "Dec 2025 4,261 buses, 40.8% penetration National[6]":
          - cell "Dec 2025"
          - cell "4,261 buses, 40.8% penetration"
          - cell "National[6]":
            - text: National
            - superscript:
              - link "[6]":
                - /url: "#ref-6"
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The most recent figure, from December 2025, quotes MOTC on charging infrastructure: 13,482 public chargers nationally, an overall vehicle-to-charger ratio of 8.8:1 and a fast-charge ratio of 35:1, both stated as exceeding EU-recommended ratios of 10:1 and 80:1 respectively"
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: .
    - heading "Gaps" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Whether the December 2025 figure of 4,261 buses/40.8% covers city buses only — matching the "35% target" language used for that category elsewhere — or the full range of bus categories the 14,500-vehicle 2030 target spans
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: ", is not stated by its source"
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: and remains an open scope question. A government statistics-portal query for a clean year-by-year registered-fleet series was not run for this page; only the ad hoc figures above, from news reports and Legislative Yuan documents, are available.

    - heading "Company history and legal identity" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The MOEA record identifies Capital Bus as 首都客運股份有限公司, with the English charter name CAPITAL BUS TRANSPORTATION Co., LTD. It gives unified business number 34049262, registered address in
      - link "Sanchong":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/o15/
      - text: ", paid-in capital of NT$530 million, representative Li Bowen and a registration date of 14 August 1975"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . The same record lists city bus, intercity bus, tour-bus, vehicle-repair and related activities among the approved business categories
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The operator’s own company profile gives a different dated milestone: it says the company was founded on 1 July 1976"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: .
      - link "Taipei":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
      - text: PTO’s history places the predecessor called San Chung City Bus among the five private operators entering the city’s joint-operation system on 30 April 1977, and labels that predecessor as today’s Capital Bus
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: . Those dates are kept as separate registration, founding and network-transition events rather than silently chosen as one origin date.
    - heading "Operating sites and network" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The current TDX snapshot associates 61 routes with the Taipei CapitalBus record
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . The page’s route section is generated from those associations, so it can change with the committed data pull without turning this profile into a hand-maintained route list
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: Capital’s profile names 21 operating sites, including Sanchong, Erchong, two
      - link "Xinzhuang":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/o18/
      - text: sites,
      - link "Sanxia":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/lb06/
      - text: ","
      - link "Neihu":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br19/
      - text: ", Dongyuan,"
      - link "Shilin":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/r16/
      - text: ", Nangang, Jingmao, two Xizhi sites, Shezi, Luodong, Ankeng, a second Sanchong site, Minsheng, Banqiao Front, Badouzi, Hualien and Banqiao"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: . It separately lists a maintenance plant and inspection teams at Sanchong, Erchong, both Xinzhuang sites, Neihu, Shilin, Xizhi, Ankeng and Wujie
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: . The source does not state opening dates, vehicle capacity or route allocation by site, so those fields remain TBC rather than being inferred from the route list
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":

      - text: .

      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . The page therefore reports the fleet-model and propulsion roster as TBC; route count is not a fleet proxy

        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: New Taipei’s 111(2) evaluation report records Capital Bus at 94.01 points, grade 優等 and second place in that period; its comparison table also records 優等 for 110(2) and 111(1)
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: . That result is useful evidence of dated public oversight, but it does not establish that every route, site or vehicle had the same result
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: .
    - paragraph: The page can therefore say something specific about Capital’s legal record, geographic operating footprint and facilities, while leaving its complete fleet and contract history open. A model-level fleet register, procurement/subsidy table and depot register would be needed to fill those gaps.

    - paragraph:
      - text: This page lists 1790 static TDX station rows in
      - link "Taipei":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
      - text: "'s Unclassified group, with a published capacity total of 50761 docks. TDX's Station/City feed supplies identity, bilingual names, addresses, coordinates and capacity; that feed does not carry current occupancy"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The rail column is a nearest-coordinate join against the committed TDX rail station registry. It is shown only for a unique result within 200 metres; station names are not used to create a match
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . The feed did not expose a usable district for these rows, so they remain in an explicit Unclassified group rather than being assigned from a guessed address or station name
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - heading "Snapshot detail" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Taipei's Unclassified group section is a build-time view of 1790 returned TDX Station/City records, not a live occupancy display
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . The normalized rows retain 1790 English station names, 1790 Traditional Chinese station names, and 1790 valid coordinate pairs; the source response also supplies station identifiers, addresses, service type, capacity and source-update timestamps
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The published capacity values in this group range from 5 to 99 docks per row, with the total shown above calculated by summing the returned BikesCapacity fields
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: ". The observed ServiceType distribution is 2: 1790, so a missing or null service value is not converted into an assumed operating category"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The TDX records used for this page carried UpdateTime value(s) 2026-08-25T23:37:06+08:00
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . Those timestamps date the source response, while the page frontmatter records the retrieval date; neither timestamp is presented as a prediction of future station availability
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: Representative rows in this group are station ID 500101023 (87 docks; YouBike2.0_第二學生活動中心), station ID 500111014 (54 docks; YouBike2.0_中研公園) and station ID 500111010 (30 docks; YouBike2.0_研究院舊莊街口)
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . They remain rows in a browse index because the source provides a compact identity, address, coordinate and capacity record; creating a separate article for every dock would repeat the same source fields without adding a sourced history or design record
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The nearby-rail column is conservative: 208 rows have a confirmed coordinate join in this group"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . A match is retained only when one nearest candidate is within 200 metres and not tied at the one-metre ambiguity threshold, and the calculation compares coordinates rather than station names
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . Current available bikes and return docks are deliberately outside this static page because TDX publishes those values through a separate availability feed
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .

    - paragraph:
      - text: To a passenger,
      - link "Taipei":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
      - text: "has one city bus network: one brand, one fare structure, one route numbering scheme, one app."
      - strong: It is fourteen private companies
      - text: ", and it has been a negotiated arrangement between them since 1977"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The regulator's own summary is unglamorous and worth stating exactly: around"
      - strong: 280 routes
      - text: ","
      - strong: 14 operators
      - text: ", about"
      - strong: 3,500 vehicles
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . Nothing about that is visible from a bus stop, which is the point of the arrangement.
    - heading "Where it came from" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The city's buses began as a municipal monopoly. 臺北市公共汽車管理處 ran
      - strong: 51 routes with 651 vehicles
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . Private operation was opened up in part from 1969, when 欣欣, 大有, 大南 and 光華 joined in succession and the network grew to
      - strong: 90 routes and 847 vehicles
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: Joint operation proper began on
      - strong: 30 April 1977
      - text: ", when five more private operators — 中興, 指南, 台北,"
      - link "三重":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/o15/
      - text: and 三重市公車, today's 首都客運 — came in
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: ". The regulator's account:"
      - strong: 149 routes were allocated
      - text: ", 2,325 vehicles were planned for joint operation, and"
      - strong: 1,984 actually ran
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - heading "How many routes it started with — two official answers" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The operators' own body describes the same year differently. It says the first phase opened with
      - strong: 33 routes
      - text: ", and that three further phases during 1977 opened"
      - strong: 50, 31 and 16
      - text: more
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: —
      - strong: "130"
      - text: in all.
    - table:
      - rowgroup:
        - row "Routes at the start Source Kind":
          - columnheader "Routes at the start"
          - columnheader "Source"
          - columnheader "Kind"
      - rowgroup:
        - row "149, 「當時分配路線149條」 Public Transport Office[1] Primary":
          - cell "149, 「當時分配路線149條」":
            - strong: "149"
            - text: ", 「當時分配路線149條」"
          - cell "Public Transport Office[1]":
            - text: Public Transport Office
            - superscript:
              - link "[1]":
                - /url: "#ref-1"
          - cell "Primary"
        - row "33, then 50 + 31 + 16 across four 1977 phases 臺北市公車聯營管理委員會[5] Primary":
          - cell "33, then 50 + 31 + 16 across four 1977 phases":
            - strong: "33"
            - text: ", then 50 + 31 + 16 across four 1977 phases"
          - cell "臺北市公車聯營管理委員會[5]":
            - text: 臺北市公車聯營管理委員會
            - superscript:
              - link "[5]":
                - /url: "#ref-5"
          - cell "Primary"
    - paragraph:
      - text: One figure may count routes
      - emphasis: allocated
      - text: on day one and the other routes
      - emphasis: opened
      - text: across the year.
      - strong: Neither source says so
      - text: ", both are the bodies' own numbers, and this page publishes both rather than picking."
    - heading "Afterwards" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Through the late 1980s and 1990s many intercity routes run by the former 臺灣省公路局 were absorbed into joint operation, either renumbered outright or taken in as 區段聯營, joint operation over a section
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: ". The municipal operator itself stopped being municipal: on"
      - strong: 1 January 2004
      - text: 臺北市公共汽車管理處 was corporatised and renamed
      - strong: 大都會汽車客運
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "A recent and easily missed change: some journeys on low-demand routes have been moved to a"
      - strong: booking system
      - text: rather than a timetable — 「針對部分路線班次搭乘需求低且不固定之班次納入預約制」
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - heading "Who decides" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The
      - strong: 臺北市公車聯營管理委員會
      - text: is formed by the participating operators themselves, with the Public Transport Office as the supervising authority, and it describes itself as the 「決策及業務執行單位」 — the body that both decides and executes
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: ". Its stated duties are narrower than the name suggests: maintaining and managing bus stop signs, public relations, liaison between passengers, regulator and operators, and"
      - strong: review of joint electronic-ticketing business
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "Ten participants founded it: the municipal 臺北市公共汽車管理處, the four operators admitted from 1969 (欣欣客運, 大有巴士, 大南汽車, 光華巴士) and the five admitted in 1977 (中興巴士, 指南客運, 臺北客運, 三重客運 and 三重市公車, now 首都客運)"
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - strong: One body or two?
      - text: zh.wikipedia describes a two-tier structure — the committee as the decision body and a separate 臺北市公車聯營管理中心 as the executive one
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . The committee's own page describes a single body doing both
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: . Published as the disagreement it is.
    - paragraph:
      - text: "A standing city committee sits above all this and reviews costs, fares and subsidies: seventeen members convened by the head of the Department of Transportation, with seats for the Ministry of Transportation and Communications, its Institute of Transportation, the Consumers' Foundation and — notably — the operators' own 臺北市公車聯營管理委員會, whose tasks include 「定期檢討聯營公車營運成本及票價事項」"
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: .
      - strong: The version of that rule read here is marked repealed
      - text: ; a successor exists and has not been read, so treat the structure as indicative rather than current.
    - heading "How the money moves" [level=2]
    - paragraph: The arrangement is usually described in one sentence about a central revenue pool. No opened primary source establishes that sentence. The city's own regulations instead set out a different and more specific machine, in four parts.
    - heading "Routes are allocated, not owned" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: An operator does not own a route. The city allocates them, and it does so on
      - strong: points
      - text: ": when the Public Transport Office allocates a joint-operation route or reallocates a revoked one,"
      - strong: the operator with the most accumulated route points chooses first, and is docked ten points for doing so
      - text: — 「得由累計獲有路線積分分數最多之聯營公車業者優先選線 1條，並扣除路線積分10分」
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: ". The alternative path is open tender: the city canvasses operators' interest and a review committee, the 臺北都會區市區及公路客運路線審議委員會, selects the operator"
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - strong: The city can also take a profitable route away.
      - text: The rule carries a heading that says so outright — 「本處收回業者高營收路線接駛原則」, principles for recovering high-revenue routes from operators. The successor operator gets
      - strong: five years
      - text: ", must apply to continue one year before that expires, and can be extended by at most three more; it must run the original alignment and may not apply to adjust it for a year"
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "That single provision does more to explain the shape of the network than any account of pooling:"
      - strong: a route that earns well is a thing the regulator can move between operators.
    - heading "Vehicle counts are constrained, not centrally set — and evaluation scores the operator, never the route" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: "No general \"buses per route\" formula exists. The route-allocation regulation constrains vehicle counts only in two specific situations: when a route changes hands, the incoming operator's proposed vehicle count may not exceed what the route had before,「接駛業者以維持原輸運能量及 不得高於原有配車數下，提出該路線需配置車輛數」"
      - superscript:
        - link "[14]":
          - /url: "#ref-14"
      - text: ; and a designated 服務性路線 — a route an operator cannot refuse — is capped at 20% of that operator's own highest-revenue route's vehicle count, 「指定接駛之服務性路線配車數以接駛最高營收路線配車數之百分之20（四捨五入）為 上限」
      - superscript:
        - link "[14]":
          - /url: "#ref-14"
      - text: . Outside those two administrative cases, no source found sets vehicle counts by route length, frequency or ridership.
    - paragraph:
      - text: The
      - link "operator service-rating scheme":
        - /url: /bus/network/operator-ratings/
      - text: scores the
      - strong: operator
      - text: ", never the individual route"
      - superscript:
        - link "[15]":
          - /url: "#ref-15"
      - text: ". The regulation says so directly: 「路線積分，係指交通局依各期評鑑成績及評鑑項目成績所給予之評分」 — route points are the score the Department of Transportation assigns from each period's"
      - emphasis: operator-level
      - text: evaluation, not a score computed for a route
      - superscript:
        - link "[15]":
          - /url: "#ref-15"
      - text: . Those points stay valid for two years
      - superscript:
        - link "[15]":
          - /url: "#ref-15"
      - text: . No published route-level service-quality metric exists on this site's evidence.

    - heading "Losses are subsidised route by route, on a published formula" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Operating-loss subsidy is made under a
      - emphasis: central
      - text: "regulation, not a city one: 「特依交通部令頒大眾運輸事業補貼辦法訂定本作業規定」"
      - superscript:

          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: . An operator may apply where a route it still ran at the end of the previous December earned
      - strong: less per bus-kilometre than its reasonable operating cost
      - superscript:

          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: ". The formula is stated:"

      - strong: This is the load-bearing point on the whole money question.
      - text: The subsidy is computed against 每車公里實際營運收入 — actual operating revenue per bus-kilometre,
      - emphasis: on that route, for that operator
      - superscript:

    - heading "Concessionary fares are reimbursed monthly, per operator" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Where a passenger pays a concessionary fare, the difference between that and the single tariff is budgeted and paid by government — 「票價與單一運價間之差額， 由政府編列預算補貼之金額」, under 發展大眾運輸條例 第九條

        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: . The recipients are named as 「經營本市聯營公車路線之公車業者」, the operators, individually
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The cycle is
      - strong: monthly
      - text: — 「價差補貼款之審核核撥週期：每月1次」 — with operators filing by the twentieth of the following month, and the claims are audited against the
      - strong: card issuers'
      - text: records via a route-by-route subsidy application, an operating detail return and a card-tap record. Payments are docked for abnormal taps, over-age vehicles, lapsed insurance, missing announcement equipment and wage non-compliance
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: .

      - superscript:

      - text: . That is a compatibility, not a corroboration.

    - paragraph:
      - text: There is
      - strong: no route 8
      - text: ", and"

    - paragraph:
      - text: "The four is the ordinary homophone taboo. The eight is not superstition at all: 八路軍, the Eighth Route Army, was a Chinese Communist formation, and a bus route numbered 8 was avoided for that reason"

    - heading "The six categories" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The regulator's own list, which is the closest thing to an official taxonomy: 一般路線 general routes, 幹線公車 trunk buses, 捷運接駁公車 metro feeders, 山區公車 hill routes, 休閒公車 leisure routes, and 市民小巴 community minibuses"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Trunk buses are the interesting category.
      - text: "They were assembled in 2017–18 from existing joint-operation routes running on major arterials, rebranded as 類捷運 — \"metro-like\" — and named after the streets they run along rather than numbered: 信義幹線, 敦化幹線"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . The network is called
      - strong: 八橫八縱
      - text: ", eight horizontal and eight vertical"
      - superscript:

          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: .
    - heading "Trunk buses, and the colour collision" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The trunk network was not conceived on its own. The Public Transport Office's January 2017 release sets out a
      - strong: four-tier hierarchy
      - text: "for the whole bus network: 快速 express, 幹線 trunk, 支線 branch, 微循環 micro-circulation"
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "Phase one was five corridors, named in the release — 「南北向敦化、松江新生2線，東西向之民生、仁愛2線及內湖等共計5線幹線路廊」: Dunhua and Songjiang–Xinsheng running north–south, Minsheng and Renai running east–west, plus"
      - link "Neihu":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br19/
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: . The same release gives peak headways of
      - strong: 4–6 minutes
      - text: and off-peak
      - strong: 5–10 minutes
      - text: ", though those figures came back only in an English summary of the page and are carried at lower confidence"

No route-level scoring methodology is stated anywhere in the regulation."

It resolves to 唯真，〈關心話題 正本清源談公車票證〉，聯合報，1981-04-13, which this project has not read: the 聯合報 archive is not openly fetchable. This is a lead toward the revenue question, not an answer to it."

    - heading "TDX record" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The committed TDX pull identifies this page as the operator record for
      - link "Taipei":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
      - text: Bus Co., Ltd. (臺北客運), with source municipality NewTaipei
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: TDX publishes the record ID bus-operator-taipeibus-1m9ums8, operator code TaipeiBus, operator number 1407, phone 0800-003-307 and URL
      - link "http://www.tpebus.com.tw":
        - /url: http://www.tpebus.com.tw
      - text: for this record
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: This is a data record, not a claim that every TDX record with the same company name is a separate legal entity
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - heading "Company history and legal identity" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: 臺北客運's own website traces the business to 1954, when it was called 文山輕便客運社; it says the business was reorganised as 文山汽車客運股份有限公司 in 1956 and took the name 臺北汽車客運股份有限公司 in June 1962
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The current legal record is more precise than the public trading name: the Ministry of Economic Affairs registry identifies 臺北汽車客運股份有限公司 under unified business number 35505603, with registered offices at 新北市三重區重新路2段78號8樓 and 李博文 as representative"
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: . The same record gives paid-in capital of NT$390 million and 39 million issued shares, and lists urban and highway passenger transport, vehicle repair and related transport-equipment activities among its registered businesses
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: . The registry lists the board's corporate representatives and share blocks, but it does not label a parent company
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The public label 首都客運集團 is narrower than a legal ownership chart. A 2024 New Taipei police release describes that group as 首都客運、臺北客運、大都會客運 and 三重客運, in the context of a traffic-safety publicity partnership
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: . That establishes the four-company membership stated by the government release; it does not, by itself, establish that Capital Bus is Taipei Bus's statutory parent
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: .
    - heading "Operating character and facilities" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The operator describes its business as urban public-bus, highway-bus and national-route passenger transport serving Greater Taipei and parts of Keelung and
      - link "Taoyuan":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taoyuan/
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: . Its company profile publishes an operating snapshot of 20 Taipei joint-operation routes, 63 New Taipei routes, four highway or road passenger routes, 877 vehicles and 1,381 employees
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: ". The numbers are retained as the operator's own snapshot because the committed TDX record measures route associations differently: this page's 126 NewTaipei records are generated from the structured pull rather than substituted with the website's three-category count"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The profile names station sites including 板橋後站、四海站、三峽一站、三峽二站、南雅站、歡仔園站、樹林站、中和站、新店站、木柵站、中華站、五福站 and 三重二站, and names 冷水坑保養總廠 plus repair units at several operating sites
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: . The separate station page publishes addresses, phone numbers and route allocations for the facilities it details; examples include 四海站、南雅站、中和站、新店站、木柵站 and 三峽一站
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: . Neither page gives a depot capacity or opening date, so those remain TBC rather than being inferred from route assignments
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The fleet evidence is specific but incomplete. New Taipei's February 2023 release records 26 electric buses entering service on Taipei Bus route 656 and says the operator received NT$182 million to replace those 26 vehicles; the same release describes the route as the city's first fully electrified route at that point
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: . It does not identify the buses' manufacturer, chassis, body or passenger capacity, and TDX has no model field for this operator record
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . The page therefore describes the electric transition without inventing a model roster.
    - heading "Service record and incidents" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: New Taipei's 2025 service-quality announcement lists 臺北客運 among four 優等 operators for the 113 second-period evaluation and says Taipei Bus and Capital Bus had each reached 16 consecutive years at that level
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: . This is an evaluation result, not a claim that every route or facility performed identically
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The record also includes a serious documented incident. New Taipei's transport bureau says a Taipei Bus 667 bus failed to yield to a pedestrian at the 壽德街 and 民德路 intersection in
      - link "Zhonghe":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/y12/
      - text: on 19 August 2023, causing a fatality; the bureau says it imposed a NT$90,000 fine, suspended the vehicle plate and deducted service-evaluation points
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: . The release says the driver lost the licence and quotes the general manager acknowledging that the driver had not followed the company's stop-before-moving rule
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: . Separately, a Taipei audit report records three labour-law penalties against Taipei Bus in ROC years 111–113, totalling NT$270,000, with the source data compiled from the Ministry of Labor employer-penalty query system
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: .

      - text: The list below is generated from the committed route pull’s operatorIds associations, so it records the current data snapshot rather than a hand-maintained route roster

        - link "[1]":

    - heading "Terminals and stop sequences" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The route-detail response supplies a direction label, a run identifier and the published departure string. The separate
      - code: GetRoadLine
      - text: response returns an ordered list whose records include a stop name, stop identifier and latitude/longitude.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: The data layer therefore records the first and last stop in that ordered response as the direction's terminal summary, while retaining the whole stop sequence for checking. “Terminal” here means the boundary of the portal's ordered run data; it does not imply that the city has designated every boundary as a bus terminal facility.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
    - paragraph:
      - text: That distinction matters on circular and short-working services. For example, the portal's route 10 detail labels the outward direction 總站→成德高中, while its return stop sequence ends at 火車站 in the retrieved run data.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: The data layer preserves both the published direction label and the returned stop boundary instead of forcing them into one English terminal pair.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: Route 2 similarly exposes 火車站→陽明交大 in the detail response; its direction lists seven outward departures and six return departures in the snapshot.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
    - heading "Published departures and fares" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The portal publishes departure strings such as 0805,0845,1225,1310,1425,1640,1805 for route 2's outward run, and it exposes separate return runs where they exist.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: Across the retrieved direction records, the committed layer preserves 970 departure values. That is a count of published timetable values, not a headway calculation and not a promise that every trip operates on every day.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: "The portal's current-notice stream shows why the retrieval date belongs beside the data: it carried a dated Green Line summer-timetable notice and temporary stop-adjustment notices during the same period."
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The detail response provides a linked 票價 page for routes, but it does not include a fare amount in the response used here.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: Fare values therefore remain TBC. A later fare layer needs to fetch the linked route-level fare records, identify the effective date and concession rules, and preserve any conflict with a city or operator notice; the presence of a link is not evidence of a current numeric fare.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
    - heading "Boundary, history and gaps" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The national Highway Bureau timetable is kept separate because its catalogue describes a static nationwide export with its own operator, route, stop, date and departure fields.
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: A Hsinchu route appearing in both systems would be a cross-layer relationship to verify, not a reason to merge the two route identities. This page does not use the Highway Bureau's national route count or monthly aggregate statistics as Hsinchu figures.
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
    - paragraph:
      - text: No ridership series, vehicle roster, depot allocation, contract history, accessibility inventory or stable historical route-change series is asserted here. Those fields need primary records from Hsinchu City, Hsinchu County, operators or the Highway Bureau, fetched at full length. A 2024 Hsinchu transport-department PDF route-summary lead was checked on 25 August 2026 but returned HTTP 403, so it is recorded as a failed lead in the research file and is not used to fill the current snapshot.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - heading "Operators, and one unsettled question about scope" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: 新竹客運 (Hsinchu Bus), the region's oldest operator, traces to 台灣軌道 株式會社, founded 29 September 1919
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: .
      - strong: Whether it still runs Hsinchu city buses is not settled.
      - text: zh.wikipedia's own article states the company currently operates only Hsinchu city buses and two intercity routes
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: . A separately fetched news account reports that 新竹客運 exited
      - strong: regional highway-bus routes
      - text: across Hsinchu-Miaoli (竹竹苗) entirely on 1 November 2024, citing falling ridership from demographic decline, pandemic effects and rising private-vehicle ownership
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: — but that article's own framing is about intercity/highway routes, not explicitly about the city network the route catalogue above draws from, which still lists 新竹客運 as an operator label. This site does not resolve the two readings against each other; the catalogue above, dated 25 August 2026, is the more recent primary evidence and leans toward "still operating city routes."
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The city's own two trunk lines have different operators: the"
      - strong: Blue Line
      - text: (formed 25 December 2015 from former routes 1 and 15) is run by 新竹客運, while the separately-formed
      - strong: Green Line
      - text: ", from the same date, is run by"
      - strong: 苗栗客運
      - text: (
      - link "Miaoli":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/miaoli/
      - text: Bus) — originally a highway route, 5809
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: . A newer, fully electric
      - strong: 先導公車
      - text: (pilot bus) route is run by
      - strong: 國光客運
      - text: ": ten electric buses, funded by a NT$52 million Highway Bureau subsidy, merging the former 紅線/橘線 circular shuttles and linking the railway station, two universities, the Science Park and HSR Hsinchu Station"
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: . Hsinchu's route catalogue is therefore run by at least four distinct companies across its different lines, not one dominant city operator.
    - region "Specifications":

      - paragraph: 6 of 10 sources on this page are primary — published by the operator, the builder or government.

          - text: 新竹市幸福巴士公共運輸資訊 primary Hsinchu City Government ( 新竹市政府 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The full route selector and category labels used to define the 68-entry Hsinchu snapshot; it also links city bus, national highway bus, regional highway bus, HSP shuttle and rail/bike information.

    - heading "Kaohsiung regional buses" [level=1]
    - paragraph: Kaohsiung's TDX snapshot exposes 316 route records, 617 direction runs, 19,191 ordered stops and 30 operator records; the municipal route index separately reports 197 routes.
    - region "Quick facts":
      - text: Kaohsiung regional buses
