      - paragraph: On this page
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - link "Current structured coverage":
            - /url: "#current-structured-coverage"
        - listitem:
          - link "Fares and service categories":
            - /url: "#fares-and-service-categories"
        - listitem:
          - link "Accessibility and ridership boundary":
            - /url: "#accessibility-and-ridership-boundary"
        - listitem:
          - link "Operators and ownership":
            - /url: "#operators-and-ownership"
        - listitem:
          - link "Electric buses — three citywide counts, three different dates":
            - /url: "#electric-buses--three-citywide-counts-three-different-dates"
        - listitem:
          - link "Conflicts and gaps":
            - /url: "#conflicts-and-gaps"
        - listitem:
          - link "Specifications":
            - /url: "#specifications"
        - listitem:
          - link "References":
            - /url: "#references"
    - paragraph:
      - text: "Kaohsiung's regional bus layer is a dated structural snapshot, not a live departure board. The official municipal route index is the first boundary: its full route list displayed 197 routes when fetched on 25 August 2026."
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: The separate operator index displayed the same total while grouping route labels under operators, including taxi-fleet entries and labels marked for reservation service.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: Those pages are useful for the city's public-facing route taxonomy, but they do not expose the same record schema as TDX.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
    - heading "Current structured coverage" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The live TDX Route response contained 316 route records, each with a route UID and ID, a Traditional Chinese and English name, terminal labels, operator objects, sub-route records, map URL where supplied, version ID and source update time.
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: The response had 316 distinct route-name values in this retrieval, so the page does not silently deduplicate branches or labels that TDX publishes as separate route records.
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: Its route data is joined to the full StopOfRoute response by the exact route UID.
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The StopOfRoute response supplied 617 direction-level records and 19,191 ordered stop objects.
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: Each retained stop has the source stop UID and ID, name, sequence, boarding flag where present, and latitude/longitude values from the TDX object.
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: This makes the committed JSON useful for stop-level joins and static route inspection, while the source
      - code: UpdateTime
      - text: remains the date of the underlying record rather than a promise about the next vehicle.
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The operator response supplied 30 operator records with names, phone numbers, URLs, provider IDs, operator numbers and update times.
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: "That is a count of TDX operator records, not a count of companies currently running a passenger route: the route response attaches operators to its own route records, and the municipal index uses a different grouping and publication scope."
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: The official catalogue also describes route-stop data with route IDs, stop IDs, coordinates, direction and order fields, and identifies the municipal static-data service as its source boundary.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - heading "Fares and service categories" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The current official fare PDF states that the section-fare schedule applies from 1 July 2026 to section-priced city buses, including medical buses, 公車式小黃 and 幸福巴士.
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: Its basic table gives NT$15 cash or electronic full fare, NT$10 for the specified student-card electronic fare, and NT$8 half fare; cash payment is exact change.
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: The same document requires electronic passengers to tap or scan on and off, and states that an incomplete transaction locks the electronic ticket until a later NT$15 unlock charge is paid.
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The bureau's full Q&A describes a one-section fare through 8 kilometres and a two-section fare above 8 kilometres, with the fare depending on passenger category.
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: It also documents a 60-dollar maximum self-pay rule for mileage-priced highway and JOY routes, separate social-card point rules, MenGo products and the 399/999 commuter products.
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: The fare page's title says “from 1 July 2026”, while an internal heading on the same fetched page says “from 1 March 2026”; both are retained as a page-level date conflict rather than silently corrected.
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
    - paragraph:
      - text: Kaohsiung's 公車式小黃 plan explains that taxi vehicles substitute for bus service where low demand or geography makes a conventional route inefficient.
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: The full plan records a 2014 trial, expansion from 2015, night service from 2017, wider rural deployment from 2019 and further route additions in 2021.
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: It lists fixed routes operated by 中華大車隊 and 福倫車隊, while the municipal operator index also includes reservation-labelled entries; those labels should not be interpreted as ordinary fixed-timetable stops without reading the linked operator schedule.
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
    - heading "Accessibility and ridership boundary" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Transportation Bureau maintains a separate accessibility index listing a dated low-floor-bus route and reservation-information file, a rehabilitation-bus service and facility information.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: The linked low-floor-bus PDF did not return successfully in the full fetch, so this regional page does not invent a route-level accessible-bus list or claim that every TDX route is step-free.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The official open-data catalogue for Kaohsiung MRT feeder-bus operations lists annual route mileage, vehicles, trips, operated kilometres, passenger count, passenger-kilometres and revenue fields.
      - superscript:
        - link "[13]":
          - /url: "#ref-13"
      - text: Its linked JSON and CSV resources both failed direct fetch in this environment, so current passenger totals and a historical ridership series remain TBC.
      - superscript:
        - link "[13]":
          - /url: "#ref-13"
      - text: The bureau's statistical-publications index confirms that transportation reports exist for Minguo 104 through 113, but the 113 report link returned 404 in the full fetch; no table value is substituted from a search result.
      - superscript:
        - link "[21]":
          - /url: "#ref-21"
    - heading "Operators and ownership" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Two operators dominate the network by history rather than by TDX record count.
      - text: 高雄客運 (Kaohsiung Bus) traces to a Japanese-era predecessor, 高旗自動車株式會社
      - superscript:
        - link "[14]":
          - /url: "#ref-14"
      - text: — a date this site could not independently confirm on the operator's own history page, which states eleven named business stations (including one at
      - strong: 岡山
      - text: ", Gangshan) and 63 maintenance staff without giving an explicit founding year in the text fetched"
      - superscript:
        - link "[15]":
          - /url: "#ref-15"
      - text: . It has been owned by
      - strong: 三地集團
      - text: (Santi Group) since roughly 2016 (an approximate date — the source gives only "five years before" a 2021 article), whose other holdings include 府城客運 (
      - link "Tainan":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/tainan/
      - text: ), 普悠瑪客運 (Taitung), and, more recently, 嘉義客運 (2019) and 苗栗客運 (2024)
      - superscript:
        - link "[14]":
          - /url: "#ref-14"
      - superscript:
        - link "[16]":
          - /url: "#ref-16"
      - text: .
      - strong: 港都客運
      - text: "(Gangdu Bus) is a different company: formed 1 January 2014 by privatising the former municipal operator, 高雄市公共汽車管理處, which itself traces to a business operating from 1937 under Japanese rule"
      - superscript:
        - link "[17]":
          - /url: "#ref-17"
      - text: . Ownership splits roughly 42% Kaohsiung City Government and 58% former public-bus-office employees
      - superscript:
        - link "[17]":
          - /url: "#ref-17"
      - text: — the same city-minority/employee-majority shape as
      - link "Taipei":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
      - text: "'s 大都會客運, formed the same way a decade later."
    - paragraph:
      - strong: A name-collision check, run directly against this evidence
      - text: ": no operator called 大都會客運 or 岡山客運 exists in Kaohsiung. 高雄客運's own page names a Gangshan (岡山) service"
      - strong: station
      - text: ", not a separate company"
      - superscript:
        - link "[15]":
          - /url: "#ref-15"
      - text: ", and the only 大都會客運 this site has found anywhere is"
      - link "Taipei's":
        - /url: /bus/operators/metropolitanbus-h3iwov/
      - text: — see the
      - link "operator ratings page":
        - /url: /bus/network/operator-ratings/
      - text: for the fuller account.
      - strong: 屏東客運

The same 2022 publication profiles a Foxtron"

    - region "References":

      - paragraph: 16 of 21 sources on this page are primary — published by the operator, the builder or government.
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - link "Kaohsiung bus route and stop dataset":
            - /url: https://data.nat.gov.tw/dataset/43822
          - text: 高雄市公車各路線去回程公車站點資料 primary Kaohsiung City Government Transportation Bureau ( 高雄市政府交通局 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The official catalogue describes route-stop data, coordinates, direction and stop order, and identifies the municipal XML endpoint; the committed snapshot uses the current TDX equivalent.
        - listitem:
          - link "Kaohsiung bus route overview by route":
            - /url: https://www.tbkc.gov.tw/Service/PublicTransport/NewBusRoute
          - text: 公車路線總覽(依路線別) primary Kaohsiung City Government Transportation Bureau ( 高雄市政府交通局 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The full municipal route index displayed 197 routes when fetched; its count is retained as a separate publication scope from TDX's 316 route records.
        - listitem:
          - link "Kaohsiung bus route overview by operator":
            - /url: https://www.tbkc.gov.tw/Service/PublicTransport/BusRouterTrader
          - text: 公車路線總覽(依業者別) primary Kaohsiung City Government Transportation Bureau ( 高雄市政府交通局 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The full operator index displayed 197 routes and operator-grouped route lists, including separate taxi-fleet and reservation-labelled entries.
        - listitem:
          - link "Kaohsiung city-bus route response":
            - /url: https://tdx.transportdata.tw/api/basic/v2/Bus/Route/City/Kaohsiung?$format=JSON
          - text: 高雄市公車路線資料（TDX Route） primary Taiwan Ministry of Transportation and Communications TDX ( 交通部運輸資料流通服務 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The full live response supplied 316 route records, route names, terminal labels, operator objects, sub-routes, route-map URLs, version IDs and source update times.
        - listitem:
          - link "Kaohsiung bus stop-order dataset":
            - /url: https://data.nat.gov.tw/dataset/43822
          - text: 高雄市公車各路線去回程公車站點資料 primary Kaohsiung City Government Transportation Bureau ( 高雄市政府交通局 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The official catalogue defines the route ID, stop ID, longitude, latitude, direction and stop-order fields used by the structured stop layer.
        - listitem:
          - link "Kaohsiung TDX ordered bus stops by route":
            - /url: https://tdx.transportdata.tw/api/basic/v2/Bus/StopOfRoute/City/Kaohsiung?$format=JSON
          - text: 高雄市公車路線站序資料（TDX StopOfRoute） primary Taiwan Ministry of Transportation and Communications TDX ( 交通部運輸資料流通服務 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The full live response supplied 617 direction-level records and 19,191 ordered stop objects with names, sequence values, boarding flags and coordinates.
        - listitem:
          - link "Kaohsiung bus operators":
            - /url: https://tdx.transportdata.tw/api/basic/v2/Bus/Operator/City/Kaohsiung?$format=JSON
          - text: 高雄市公車業者資料（TDX Operator） primary Taiwan Ministry of Transportation and Communications TDX ( 交通部運輸資料流通服務 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The full live response supplied 30 operator records with names, contacts, websites and update times; not every operator record is attached to a route in the route response.
        - listitem:
          - link "Kaohsiung bus fare information":
            - /url: https://www.tbkc.gov.tw/Service/PublicTransport/gogo123?id=5599cc66-4ca8-4d82-9532-9f123a361b59
          - text: 公車票價資訊(2026年7月1日起調整) primary Kaohsiung City Government Transportation Bureau ( 高雄市政府交通局 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The full fare page states the section-fare scope, card and cash rules, concession-card boundary and the 15/10/8 basic fare table; its heading says 1 July 2026 while an internal heading says 1 March 2026.
        - listitem:
          - link "Kaohsiung section-fare explanation, 1 July 2026 edition":
            - /url: https://www.tbkc.gov.tw/FileOutput/Page/%E9%AB%98%E9%9B%84%E5%B8%82%E5%B8%82%E5%8D%80%E5%85%AC%E8%BB%8A%E6%AE%B5%E6%AC%A1%E7%A5%A8%E5%83%B9%E8%AA%AA%E6%98%8E115.7.1%E7%89%88.pdf?id=c8b30f33-c69f-4e1a-969c-9acf1a620810
          - text: 高雄市市區公車段次票價說明 primary Kaohsiung City Government Transportation Bureau ( 高雄市政府交通局 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The full two-page official PDF states implementation from 1 July 2026 and gives cash, electronic-payment, student, half-fare and social-card rules.
        - listitem:
          - link "Kaohsiung mileage-section bus fare Q&A":
            - /url: https://www.tbkc.gov.tw/Service/PublicTransport/gogo123?id=cb7f57d2-317a-4172-8a92-d01491de5057
          - text: 高雄市市區公車里程段次收費Q&A primary Kaohsiung City Government Transportation Bureau ( 高雄市政府交通局 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The full Q&A explains the 8-kilometre one/two-section boundary, card tap-on/tap-off lock fee, mileage-route cap, MenGo and TPASS-related products.
        - listitem:
          - link "Kaohsiung 公車式小黃 service plan":
            - /url: https://www.tbkc.gov.tw/Service/PublicTransport/Taxis?id=db7194a9-88c3-4277-9343-6e080d7493e8
          - text: 公車式小黃服務計畫簡介 primary Kaohsiung City Government Transportation Bureau ( 高雄市政府交通局 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The full page describes the taxi-bus rationale, development from 2014, fare treatment from 2019 and the current fixed-route lists for 中華大車隊 and 福倫車隊.
        - listitem:
          - link "Kaohsiung public-transport accessibility service index":
            - /url: https://www.tbkc.gov.tw/Service/PublicTransport/Accessibility
          - text: 無障礙服務 primary Kaohsiung City Government Transportation Bureau ( 高雄市政府交通局 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The full page lists a dated low-floor-bus route and reservation information file, plus separate rehabilitation-bus and facility entries; the linked low-floor PDF itself failed fetch and is not expanded here.
        - listitem:
          - link "Kaohsiung MRT feeder-bus operations":
            - /url: https://data.gov.tw/dataset/159665
          - text: 高雄市捷運接駁公車營運情形 primary Kaohsiung City Government Budget Office ( 高雄市政府主計處 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The full catalogue lists annual fields including route mileage, vehicles, trips, passenger count, passenger-kilometres and revenue; its linked JSON and CSV resources failed direct fetch, so no values are asserted.
        - listitem:
          - link "Kaohsiung Bus Co., Ltd.":
            - /url: https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/高雄客運
          - text: 高雄客運 secondary 維基百科 (Chinese Wikipedia) accessed 2026-08-28 Traces to 高旗自動車株式會社 (Japanese era, 1941 by this article's account, not independently confirmed on the operator's own primary page). Names parent 三地集團 (Santi Group) and subsidiaries 府城客運, 普悠瑪客運, 嘉義客運 (2019) and 苗栗客運 (2024).
        - listitem:
          - link "Kaohsiung Bus — company history":
            - /url: https://ksbus.com.tw/about.asp?id=2
          - text: 高雄客運-歷史沿革 primary 高雄汽車客運股份有限公司 accessed 2026-08-28 The operator's own page (fetched without the www. subdomain, which fails a certificate check). States eleven business stations by name, including one at Gangshan (岡山) — direct evidence against a separate "岡山客運" company — and 63 maintenance staff. Does not state an explicit founding year in the text this site could extract.
        - listitem:
          - link "Quietly taking control of Guai Guai and Nanren Lake — Kaohsiung's land-consolidation magnate revealed":
            - /url: https://www.mirrormedia.mg/story/20210705fin005
          - text: 低調入主乖乖南仁湖 高雄百億土地重劃大王揭祕 secondary 鏡週刊 (Mirror Media) accessed 2026-08-28 Investigative feature naming 高雄客運 as 三地集團's first acquisition/turnaround target roughly five years before the 2021-07-05 article (so approximately 2016, not exact), quoting group CEO 鍾育霖.
        - listitem:
          - link "Gangdu Bus":
            - /url: https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/港都客運
          - text: 港都客運 secondary 維基百科 (Chinese Wikipedia) accessed 2026-08-28 Formed 1 January 2014 privatising 高雄市公共汽車管理處 (predecessor operating from 1937 under Japanese rule). Ownership roughly 42% Kaohsiung City Government, 58% former public-bus-office employees. The operator's own site (gdbus.com.tw) could not be fetched — a TLS configuration error — so every claim here rests on this secondary source.
        - listitem:
          - link "Kaohsiung's new good-life progress, No. 05":
            - /url: https://takao.kcg.gov.tw/article/760
          - text: 高雄新好生活進行式 No.05 primary Kaohsiung City Government Information Bureau ( 高雄市政府新聞局 ), 高雄畫刊 accessed 2026-08-28 Published 2026-05-06. States a citywide figure of 195 electric low-floor buses out of roughly 1,000+ total city buses (19%), and profiles a Foxtron "Model T" bus in service on Route 24 with a stated 2-hour 80% charge time.
        - listitem:
          - link "Green electric bus era arrives — Kaohsiung buses roll out further and further":
            - /url: https://168.motc.gov.tw/theme/fullsized/post/1906121103392
          - text: "綠色電動巴士時代來臨 高雄公車愈開愈遠 secondary MOTC Traffic Safety Portal ( 交通部 168 交通安全入口網 ) accessed 2026-08-28 Dated 2018-04-10. States a citywide total of 77 electric buses across seven private operators: 港都客運 50, 南台灣客運 14, 高雄客運 11, 漢程客運 2 — a much smaller figure than the 2022 195-bus count, from an earlier date."
        - listitem:
          - link "Pingtung Bus":
            - /url: https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/屏東客運
          - text: 屏東客運 secondary 維基百科 (Chinese Wikipedia) accessed 2026-08-28 Founded 1931, current name from 1947. Runs routes 9117, 9127, 9188, 9189 jointly with 高雄客運 into Kaohsiung, with a Kaohsiung station established 2001.
        - listitem:
          - link "Kaohsiung transportation statistical reports index":
            - /url: https://www.tbkc.gov.tw/AboutUs/Accountant/Journal
          - text: 統計刊物專區 primary Kaohsiung City Government Transportation Bureau ( 高雄市政府交通局 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The full index lists transportation statistical reports for 104 through 113, but the linked 113 report URL returned 404 when fetched directly here; no table value is copied from a search result.
    - paragraph: "Last updated: 2026-08-28"

    - paragraph:
      - link "Tainan":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/tainan/
      - text: "'s public-bus data has several official layers, and they are not interchangeable. The Government Data Open Platform describes the route and stop datasets as Tainan Transportation Bureau data sourced through TDX, while the live TDX responses expose the route identities and ordered stop records used here."
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: The
      - link "committed Tainan route JSON":
        - /url: /data/tainan-bus-routes.json
      - text: "keeps that distinction visible: route metadata, sub-routes and source update times are separate from the direction-level stop arrays."
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
    - heading "The city-bus route layer" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The route response supplies route names, route IDs, operator references, sub-route directions, terminal labels, fare descriptions and official route-map links.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: A route can contain more than one sub-route, including extensions or direction-specific labels, so the data layer retains the source's sub-route UID and name rather than flattening every branch into a bare route number.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: The stop response then joins by route and sub-route UID; each stop keeps the source stop ID, sequence, boarding flag and coordinate where published.
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
    - paragraph:
      - text: This is a structure for navigation and comparison, not a live arrival board. The Tainan portal separately advertises dynamic information, route maps, stop information, transfer queries, fare queries and timetable/download functions.
      - superscript:
        - link "[14]":
          - /url: "#ref-14"
      - text: The route JSON's
      - code: UpdateTime
      - text: values are the source timestamps for the snapshot, while the page retrieval date is 25 August 2026; those dates should be read together when routes are used for a journey.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
    - table:
      - rowgroup:

    - heading "Operators, fares and transfers" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The operator response publishes ten records with names, phone numbers, websites and update times.
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: "That count is a count of TDX operator records, not an independent legal-company audit: route records can name a bus company, a taxi fleet or a small-bus operator in the same city catalogue."
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The fare page describes a fare system with several layers. For 2026, Tainan residents using the City Card receive the stated urban-route weekday half-fare and weekend-free treatment, while the page gives a basic-mileage-free rule for main and branch routes when an electronic card is tapped on and off.
      - superscript:
        - link "[15]":
          - /url: "#ref-15"
      - text: The same page states a two-hour TRA-to-bus transfer discount and a separate rule for HSR express routes, including the condition that HSR passengers travel free.
      - superscript:
        - link "[15]":
          - /url: "#ref-15"
      - text: These are network and eligibility rules, not a route-by-route historical fare series; that series remains TBC in this page.
      - superscript:
        - link "[15]":
          - /url: "#ref-15"

    - paragraph:
      - text: "The sharp fall between 109 and 110 is visible in the source-derived sum, but this page does not assign a cause to it: the ridership dataset supplies counts and categories, not an explanatory series."
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: The 114 resource was available when the catalogue metadata was last updated on 11 August 2026, and the page identifies the publication cadence as annual.
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
    - heading "小黃公車" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Tainan describes 小黃公車 as city-bus service operated with taxi vehicles, with fixed routes, stops and timetables plus a reservation mode for trips within one kilometre of a route stop when booked by 17:00 the day before.
      - superscript:
        - link "[16]":
          - /url: "#ref-16"
      - text: The official Q&A also describes reservation stops in places without a fixed route or fixed timetable, so a stop listed in that part of the page must not be treated as a normal scheduled stop.
      - superscript:
        - link "[16]":
          - /url: "#ref-16"
      - text: Its current route table names 52 unique routes across 32 administrative districts and identifies 台一大車隊 or 中華衛星大車隊 for the grouped services.
      - superscript:
        - link "[16]":
          - /url: "#ref-16"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The city has continued to change the service model. A recent official notice describes 黃3 and 黃16 as joint bus-and-taxi services, adds 黃23 between 西寮代天府 and 柳營奇美醫院, and states a reservation window from 06:00 to 22:00 for qualifying bookings.
      - superscript:
        - link "[17]":
          - /url: "#ref-17"
      - text: The JSON preserves the grouped route table and unique route names, but leaves individual departure times to the official portal's timetable layer rather than copying a dynamic or image-only schedule into a static claim.
      - superscript:
        - link "[16]":
          - /url: "#ref-16"
      - superscript:
        - link "[14]":
          - /url: "#ref-14"
    - heading "Operators — a network that keeps changing hands" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Tainan's city-bus operator roster has been actively reshaped by tender through the 2020s, unlike
      - link "Taipei":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
      - text: "'s stable joint-operation group"
      - superscript:
        - link "[23]":
          - /url: "#ref-23"
      - text: .
      - strong: 興南客運
      - text: (Shing Nan Bus) is the oldest, tracing to 台灣輕鐵株式會社 (1921) and a 1941 merger into 興南乘合自動車株式會社
      - superscript:
        - link "[18]":
          - /url: "#ref-18"
      - text: .
      - strong: 新營客運
      - text: (Xinying Bus), formally established January 1950, joined the Tainan system in a first batch of 44 transferred highway routes — sources disagree on whether that was 2011 or 2012
      - superscript:
        - link "[19]":
          - /url: "#ref-19"
      - text: .
      - strong: 府城客運
      - text: "(Fucheng Bus) is younger and structurally distinct: founded 2013 as a subsidiary spun off from"
      - strong: Kaohsiung Bus
      - text: (高雄客運, also documented on this site's
      - link "Kaohsiung page":
        - /url: /bus/regional/kaohsiung/
      - text: ) specifically to give Tainan a dedicated city-bus brand, after the original, differently-owned 台南客運 stopped running city routes in 2003
      - superscript:
        - link "[20]":
          - /url: "#ref-20"
      - text: .
      - strong: 漢程客運
      - text: (Han-Cheng Bus), founded 2013 in Kaohsiung as part of the same 台灣愛巴士 交通聯盟 alliance as 巨業交運/巨業交通, expanded into Tainan in December 2019 as its fourth operator
      - superscript:
        - link "[21]":
          - /url: "#ref-21"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Route 77 traces a small chain of hand-offs that is itself informative.
      - text: Launched 2016 as Tainan's first electric-bus route, it passed from its original operator to 府城客運 and then, from 10 April 2023, to 漢程客運 — the same 40 daily trips and alignment carried through each transfer
      - superscript:
        - link "[22]":
          - /url: "#ref-22"
      - text: . A
      - strong: 2024-08-21 network reorganisation
      - text: awarded 巨業交通 nine routes (existing and new, first batch targeted for Q4 2024) and 統聯客運 ten routes, making 統聯客運 Tainan's sixth operator from
      - strong: 3 January 2025
      - superscript:
        - link "[23]":
          - /url: "#ref-23"
      - text: — after the TDX snapshot above was retrieved, so that operator may not yet appear in the committed route/operator records.
    - heading "Conflicts" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: 新營客運's own zh.wikipedia article and the separate 大台南公車 overview article disagree on the year it joined the Tainan network — 2011 in one, 2012 in the other, describing what appears to be the same 44-route transfer
      - superscript:
        - link "[19]":
          - /url: "#ref-19"
      - text: . Neither is independently corroborated against a Tainan city government primary source; both are published rather than picked.
    - heading "Gaps and conflicts" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The route and stop datasets provide current structure, but not a historical route-change log, reliability series, depot allocation, vehicle assignment or accessibility inventory.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: TDX provides route and stop update timestamps, while the ridership catalogue provides annual route totals; neither is a complete timetable history.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: The city portal and the 小黃公車 Q&A are therefore retained as the service-information boundary, and any timetable or route change should be refreshed from those sources before publication.
      - superscript:
        - link "[14]":
          - /url: "#ref-14"
      - superscript:
        - link "[16]":
          - /url: "#ref-16"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The official sources disagree on the current 小黃公車 count. The Q&A page says 52 routes across 32 administrative districts, while the 5 August 2026 expansion notice says that adding 黃3, 黃16 and 黃23 increased the total from 46 to 49 routes across 31 districts.
      - superscript:
        - link "[16]":
          - /url: "#ref-16"
      - superscript:
        - link "[17]":
          - /url: "#ref-17"
      - text: These may be different publication snapshots or scopes, but the fetched sources do not explain the difference. The data layer preserves the Q&A table's 52 unique route names and reports the notice's 49 separately; it does not average them or choose a winner.
      - superscript:

    - paragraph:
      - text: The confirmed stop sequence runs 44 stops from 泰山站一(泰山路), past 黎明技術學院, then 捷運泰山站(泰林路), then 中原路一, then 莊敬中學(復興路), then
      - link "七張":

      - text: (北新路), then 中正國宅, ending at 崇光中學.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: "8 confirmed interchanges are recorded in the curated stop-ID join set:"
      - link "Taishan Station":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/a5/
      - text: ","
      - link "Xinpu":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/bl08/
      - text: ","
      - link "Xindian District Office":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/g02/
      - text: ", Qizhang, Dapinglin, Touqianzhuang,"
      - link "Xinpu Minsheng":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/y17/
      - text: and
      - link "Xingfu":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/y19/
      - text: .
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: The route runs 12 subroutes under two operators, 指南客運 and 中興巴士.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: "The TDX record files 7 distinct stop-pattern names under this identity: 918、918三民路、918返程不繞黎明與三民路、918三民路不繞黎明、918不繞黎明和三民路、918去(車機)、918返(車機)."
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: "The committed record carries 12 direction/variant sequences, 77 distinct stops in total: 39 stops (outbound, 918); 33 stops (return, 918); 44 stops (outbound, 918三民路); 33 stops (return, 918三民路); 39 stops (outbound, 918返程不繞黎明與三民路); 32 stops (return, 918返程不繞黎明與三民路); 43 stops (outbound, 918三民路不繞黎明); 32 stops (return, 918三民路不繞黎明); 38 stops (outbound, 918不繞黎明和三民路); 32 stops (return, 918不繞黎明和三民路); 39 stops (outbound, 918去(車機)); 33 stops (return, 918返(車機))."
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: The published fare is charged over 2 Segment; the published route length is 45.7 km; weekday service runs from 05:30 to 22:30, with a published peak headway of 0608 minutes and 1015 minutes off-peak; holiday service follows the same published span.

        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"

      - text: "The committed record carries 8 direction/variant sequences, 137 distinct stops in total: 64 stops (outbound, F102); 65 stops (return, F102反向經鄒厝崙); 58 stops (outbound, F102經淡水商工); 61 stops (outbound, F102經淡水商工、鄒厝崙); 67 stops (outbound, F102經鄒厝崙); 66 stops (outbound, F102經市民農園); 69 stops (outbound, F102經鄒厝崙、市民農園); 67 stops (return, F102反向經鄒厝崙、市民農園)."

  - paragraph: Every English-language source we could find has Taiwan's metro line colours wrong. Not badly wrong — most are within a few percent — but not one of the 11 matches what the operators actually publish. These are the official values, taken from Taiwan's Ministry of Transportation and Communications, with the working shown.
  - 'link "Official line colours All 11 lines: hex values, swatches, contrast against white and black, and where each one was read. Plus a reconciliation against the Wikipedia and Wikidata values — including one case where a citation to an official route map was further from correct than the value it replaced, and one line the platform does not carry at all. 11 lines · 10 from MOTC TDX"':
    - /url: /data/line-colours/
  - link "Station records All 210 stations across 10 lines — codes, Chinese and English names, coordinates where published, interchanges and running order. TDX-backed records are downloadable as JSON; Sanying's twelve records cite the operator on their station pages. 210 stations · mixed provenance":
    - /url: /data/stations/
  - link "Bibliography Every source cited anywhere on this site, marked primary or secondary, with the pages that rest on it and the date each URL was read. The primary-to-secondary ratio is the honest summary of how much of this site is first-hand. Cited sources · primary vs secondary":
    - /url: /data/sources/
  - link "Provenance What came from official data, what is hand-researched, what is still unknown, and how current any of it is. Including the staleness caveat that applies to everything on this site. Retrieved 2026-08-24":
    - /url: /data/provenance/
  - link "Network growth A dated station-opening timeline from the researched station records, with every missing opening date left as TBC and grouped by line for checking. Opening chronology · 1996 to now":
    - /url: /data/network-growth/
  - link "Comparisons Lines by length and stations, operators by documented fleet-family records, and every station by structure and latest imported ridership. Accessible tables · no JavaScript required":
    - /url: /data/comparisons/
  - link "Changelog The project's run log as a reader-facing history of new research, corrections, audits and data layers, regenerated at build time. Generated from docs/run-log.md":
    - /url: /data/changelog/
  - heading "Use it" [level=2]
  - paragraph: All of this is derived from Taiwan government open data and is reproduced here under the same terms. If you are building something and need Taipei Metro line colours or station records, take them — a link back is welcome but not required.
  - paragraph: If you find an error, it matters. The whole point of this section is that incorrect values propagate quietly for years, and the only defence is people checking.

Several fail 4.5:1 against white or black, so a badge fill and an accent ink are derived from each one — same hue, lightness reduced until it clears WCAG AA with a small margin. Every derived value on this site is generated that way, never picked by eye.
  - heading "What everyone else has" [level=2]
  - table:

  - heading "The one that is not from TDX" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: The Sanying Line opened on 30 June 2026 and has no record on the platform of any kind — no line record, so no
    - code: LineColor
    - text: to read. Every operator code on TDX was probed for it; New Taipei's two light rail lines turned out to be filed under codes of their own, and there is no equivalent for Sanying.
  - paragraph:
    - text: "What settled it was the operator's own line mark: New Taipei Metro publishes the LB roundel on its Sanying Line station page as a 156×156 lossless PNG, and the whole ring — a third of the image, to the pixel — is"
    - code: "#48B6D2"
    - text: . That is the operator rendering its own line identity at a known value on its own site, which is the same kind of thing a
    - code: LineColor
    - text: field is, read out of a different file.
  - paragraph:
    - strong: The PANTONE figure is a genuine loose end.
    - text: "“PANTONE 637C” circulates for this line and could not be confirmed anywhere: not on the operator's site, not on the New Taipei rapid transit bureau's route page or its identity page, and not in either Wikipedia article — all of which say only 淺藍色, light blue. Nor is it a value you could simply adopt: the third-party PANTONE-to-sRGB converters disagree among themselves ("
    - code: "#4EC3E0"
    - text: ","
    - code: "#4DC5E2"
    - text: ","
    - code: "#42BFDF"
    - text: ","
    - code: "#48A8D0"
    - text: ), so taking the designation on trust would still mean picking one conversion over three others. The table above records the commonest of them against the operator's own value; the difference is what it is, and this page is not going to resolve it by choosing.
  - heading "A warning about citation chains" [level=2]
  - paragraph: Two of these are worth dwelling on, because they show a failure mode that is easy to repeat.
  - paragraph:
    - text: This site originally carried
    - code: "#B57A28"
    - text: for the Wenhu Line. That was replaced with
    - code: "#C48C31"
    - text: on the strength of a Wikidata value
    - emphasis: citing TRTC's own route map
    - text: — which sounds authoritative and is the kind of provenance you would normally accept. The official value is
    - code: "#B57A25"
    - text: . The correction moved the value further from the truth than the guess it replaced.
  - paragraph:
    - text: The same thing happened with the Airport MRT. An earlier
    - code: "#8246AF"
    - text: was replaced by
    - code: "#8E47AD"
    - text: from Wikidata. The official value is
    - code: "#8246AF"
    - text: — exactly what was discarded.
  - paragraph:
    - text: The lesson is not that Wikidata is unreliable. It is that
    - strong: a citation to an official source is not the same as the official source
    - text: ", and confidence in a chain of references is not evidence about what sits at the end of it. Where a government publishes the data through an API, use the API."
  - heading "Caveats" [level=2]
  - list:
    - listitem:
      - strong: Circular and Airport MRT are not TRTC.
      - text: Circular is New Taipei Metro and the Airport MRT is Taoyuan Metro, so their colours come from those operators' records. A request limited to TRTC returns five lines.
    - listitem:
      - strong: These are screen values.
      - text: DORTS states its signage system defines Pantone, RGB and CMYK values per line; that specification is not published openly and may not match these hex values exactly. The Sanying Line is the case where that gap is visible rather than theoretical — see above.
    - listitem:
      - strong: The source data is not new.
      - text: See
      - link "provenance":
        - /url: /data/provenance/
      - text: .
  - heading "Download" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - link "↓ taipei-metro-line-colours.json":
      - /url: /data/taipei-metro-line-colours.json
    - text: 11 lines · official + derived
  - paragraph: Official colours with the contrast-checked badge and accent values derived from them, generated from the same source this page renders.
  - paragraph:
    - text: The official values are Taiwan government open data under the
    - link "Open Government Data Licence":
      - /url: https://data.gov.tw/licenses
    - text: — free to use, adapt and redistribute, including commercially, with attribution. The derived values are ours and carry no additional conditions.

  - heading "Provenance" [level=1]
  - paragraph: Which facts on this site are official records, which are our own research, and which are still open. A reference site that will not tell you this is asking you to take it on trust.

    - strong: The source data is not current.
    - text: We retrieved it on 2026-08-24, but the operators' own last-updated stamps run from
    - strong: 2016-11-23
    - text: to 2026-08-22. That is fine for a network which has not changed since — but a station opening after those dates will not appear here, and no amount of refetching changes that until the operator republishes.
  - heading "Who publishes what" [level=2]

  - list:
    - listitem:
      - strong: Elevated or underground.
      - text: TDX does not publish structure. Ours is compiled by hand and kept in a separate overlay file so refetching official data can never overwrite it — and so it is never mistaken for official data. Two Wenhu stations are marked
      - emphasis: not established
      - text: rather than guessed.
    - listitem:
      - strong: Everything about rolling stock and depots.
      - text: Fleet sizes, car dimensions, capacities, depot areas and stabling capacity are not in any open dataset we have found. Anything marked TBC on those pages is genuinely unknown to us, not merely unfetched.

    - code: RouteLength

The lesson is the same one the line colours taught — check the whole record before concluding a source is silent.

  - list:

      - link "the colours page":

      - text: .

  - paragraph:
    - text: The underlying records are Taiwan government open data, published by MOTC through TDX under the
    - link "Open Government Data Licence":
      - /url: https://data.gov.tw/licenses
    - text: . You may use, reproduce, distribute and adapt them, including commercially, provided you attribute the source.
  - paragraph: Our derived work — the contrast-checked badge and accent colours, the chained geometry, the structure overlay — is offered on the same terms. Attribution to Taiwan Transit Guide is welcome but not required; attribution to MOTC is required by their licence, not ours.

      - link "Kinmen island ferry services Jin–Lie domestic ferries and the cross-strait mini-three-links from Kinmen, with dated August 2026 schedules, service fees, operators and the limits of the published fare data.":
        - /url: /ferry/routes/kinmen/
    - listitem:
      - link "Matsu island ferry services Island ferries, Daqiu excursions, Fuzhou mini-three-links and the overnight Keelung route serving Matsu, with official fares and date-sensitive operating rules.":

        - /url: /ferry/routes/orchid-island/
    - listitem:
      - link "Penghu island ferry services Public and visitor ferry services linking Magong with Penghu's inhabited islands, the southern islands and Taiwan, with dated schedules, fares and weather limits.":
        - /url: /ferry/routes/penghu/
  - paragraph: Taipei has scheduled passenger boats. The Blue Highway routes on the Tamsui and Keelung rivers are small in ridership but they are genuine public transit — inside the regional fare ecosystem, which most English sources do not realise — and a transit guide that skipped them would be drawing the network's boundary in the wrong place.
  - paragraph: Start with the Blue Highway guide for current routes, operators, piers, published fares, stored-value-card rules, and weather-dependent operation. The guide keeps the official timetable and fare conflicts visible instead of turning a changing river service into a single timeless schedule.

    - text: ","

    - text: and

section-rail.snapshot:
- main:
  - navigation "Breadcrumb":
    - link "Home":
      - /url: /
    - text: Rail & cable
  - link "Back to the previous page":
    - /url: /ferry/routes/
  - heading "Rail & cable" [level=1]
  - paragraph: Fixed-guideway transit across Taiwan — metro and light rail in five cities, Taiwan Railway, High Speed Rail, the Maokong and Alishan cable and forestry lines.
  - list:
    - listitem:
      - link "The network Every line on one map, drawn from official route geometry, with official colours, station counts, termini and end-to-end times.":
        - /url: /rail/network/
  - heading "Systems" [level=2]
  - list:
    - listitem:
      - link "Metro The metropolitan metro network — the lines a rider treats as one railway, under one numbering scheme and one fare system. 31 pages":
        - /url: /rail/metro/
    - listitem:
      - link "Cable The Maokong Gondola — an aerial ropeway run by a TRTC subsidiary, and the region's only cable transit. 5 pages":
        - /url: /rail/cable/
    - listitem:
      - link "Taichung Metro Taichung's Green Line — a single steel-wheel, driverless metro linking Beitun, the city centre and the HSR station. 26 pages":
        - /url: /rail/tmrt/
    - listitem:
      - link "Taiwan High Speed Rail Taiwan’s 350 km high-speed railway, with 12 stations from Nangang to Zuoying and a BOT history that changed during financial restructuring. 19 pages":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/
    - listitem:
      - link "Taoyuan Metro Taoyuan Metro’s operating Airport MRT and the separate Green Line project registry published by the city engineering bureau. 52 pages":
        - /url: /rail/tymc/
    - listitem:
      - link "Taiwan Railways Taiwan Railways current station and line data, with historical route architecture kept distinct from the live TDX snapshot. 269 pages":
        - /url: /rail/tra/
    - listitem:
      - link "Kaohsiung Metro Kaohsiung Metro’s Red and Orange Lines and the Circular Light Rail, with TDX metro data and operator/government LRT records kept distinct. 88 pages":
        - /url: /rail/krtc/
    - listitem:
      - link "Alishan Forest Railway Taiwan's 762 mm forest and mountain railway from Chiayi to Alishan, with active sunrise and forest-park branches. 4 pages":
        - /url: /rail/alishan/
  - heading "Projects All projects →" [level=2]:
    - text: Projects
    - link "All projects →":
      - /url: /rail/projects/
  - paragraph: Lines under construction, approved extensions, proposals and abandoned alignments.
  - list:
    - listitem:
      - link "Taipei-region rail projects What is being built, what is approved, what remains a proposal, and what the primary record still cannot establish.":
        - /url: /rail/projects/project-status/
    - listitem:
      - link "TOD and joint development The station-area buildings, land rights, public returns and disputes that sit beside Taipei-region rail.":
        - /url: /rail/projects/tod-joint-development/
    - listitem:
      - link "Taichung Metro Blue Line Taichung's approved 24.78-kilometre east–west metro project, now entering route construction from the port toward the city centre.":
        - /url: /rail/projects/taichung-blue-line/
    - listitem:
      - link "Taichung Metro Purple Line Taichung's feasibility-stage Tun District Loop project, planned as a 16-station elevated medium-capacity route linking Dali, Taiping, Beitun and Daqing.":
        - /url: /rail/projects/taichung-purple-line/
    - listitem:
      - link "Taichung Airport MRT Orange Line Taichung's feasibility-approved airport-to-Wufeng MRT project, planned at approximately 29.23 km with 26 stations and still in pre-construction planning.":
        - /url: /rail/projects/taichung-orange-line/
    - listitem:
      - link "Taichung Orange Line Sea Line Extension Feasibility-stage Orange Line extension toward Taichung's coastal districts, with an interim 16.50 km branching proposal that is not yet the approved route.":
        - /url: /rail/projects/taichung-orange-sea-extension/
    - listitem:
      - link "Taichung Metro Chongde–Fengyuan Line Taichung's feasibility-stage Red Line, a proposed 15.42 km elevated route with 11 stations and a depot linking North Taichung, Tanzi and Fengyuan.":
        - /url: /rail/projects/taichung-red-line/
    - listitem:
      - link "Taipei Metro Wanda–Zhonghe–Shulin Line A two-phase medium-capacity route from central Taipei through Yonghe, Zhonghe, Tucheng and Shulin to Huilong, with construction dates and progress measures that must be read by phase.":
        - /url: /rail/projects/wanda-zhonghe-shulin/
    - listitem:
      - link "“Sanmin Line” — no verified New Taipei project record A checked source boundary for the requested Sanmin Line name; official records read in full identify Sanying and Minsheng–Xizhi as separate projects.":
        - /url: /rail/projects/sanmin-line/
    - listitem:
      - link "Minsheng–Xizhi Line A cross-city LRRT project whose Taipei section remains in central review while the separately reported Xidong section is under construction.":
        - /url: /rail/projects/minsheng-xizhi-line/
    - listitem:
      - link "Xinyi Line East Extension A one-station underground extension from Xiangshan toward Guangci/Fengtian Temple, with the former Xinyi Road Sec. 6 station removed from the approved scope.":
        - /url: /rail/projects/xinyi-east-extension/
  - heading "History All history →" [level=2]:
    - text: History
    - link "All history →":
      - /url: /rail/history/
  - paragraph: How the railway came to be the way it is — the contracts, disputes and decisions whose consequences are still running.
  - list:
    - listitem:
      - link "The Matra dispute Two disputes thirteen years apart, usually told as one — the test-track fires an engineering change explains, the seventeen-year lawsuit Matra won, and the walkout that taught Taipei how to buy its next railway. BR Wenhu Line":
        - /url: /rail/history/matra-dispute/
    - listitem:
      - link "Public art in the Taipei-region rail network A primary-source catalogue of commissioned works named by DORTS, NTMC and TYMC, with missing fields and conflicting costs left visible.":
        - /url: /rail/history/public-art/
    - listitem:
      - 'link "The Circular Line''s 0403 earthquake What the official investigation says about the 3 April 2024 earthquake: a pot-bearing mechanism, a design and inspection chain, the eight-month recovery, and a cause still disputed by the contractor. Y Circular Line"':
        - /url: /rail/history/circular-line-0403-earthquake/
    - listitem:
      - link "Station naming and renames Officially documented former names, appended station names and the gaps where a current label is not yet a rename record.":
        - /url: /rail/history/station-naming/
    - listitem:
      - link "Metro incidents and service disruptions A primary-source record of flooding, derailment, signalling faults, fires and earthquake disruptions, with unresolved counts and dates left visible.":
        - /url: /rail/history/incidents/
    - listitem:
      - link "The Linkou Line A former Taiwan Railways corridor whose 1968 operation record, 2005 passenger opening and 2012–13 shutdown describe different phases of one railway.":
        - /url: /rail/history/linkou-line/
    - listitem:
      - link "The Shen'ao–Liandong Line A former 6.0 km Taiwan Railways alignment whose southern section was dismantled in 1977 while the northern route later returned to passenger service.":
        - /url: /rail/history/shenao-line/
    - listitem:
      - link "The Hualien–Tianpu Line A 2.4 km former Taiwan Railways alignment whose 1982 dismantling followed the East Line widening and the move from Hualien's old station.":
        - /url: /rail/history/hualien-tianpu-line/
    - listitem:
      - link "The Taiwan Railways Taipei–Danshui Line A 21.2 km former TRA route opened in 1901, left railway service in the 1988 era and began physical dismantling in 1989 before its corridor became MRT infrastructure.":
        - /url: /rail/history/taipei-danshui-line/
    - listitem:
      - link "The Taiwan Railways Xindian Line A former 10.4 km Wanhua–Xindian railway, bought by the state in 1949, withdrawn in 1965 and later overlapped by roads and the Taipei Metro.":
        - /url: /rail/history/xindian-line/
    - listitem:
      - link "The Taiwan Railways Zhonghe Line A former 6.5 km freight-only TRA branch from Banqiao to Zhonghe that opened in 1965, stopped service in 1990 and was physically dismantled in 1993.":
        - /url: /rail/history/zhonghe-line/
    - listitem:
      - link "The Taiwan Railways Fengyuan–Dongshi Line A former 14.1 km TRA branch built in 1958, opened in 1959 and withdrawn after its final train on 31 August 1991.":
        - /url: /rail/history/fengyuan-dongshi-line/
    - listitem:
      - link "The Taiwan Railways Tanzi–Shengang Line An 8.7 km route listed in TRA's construction table alongside a roughly 14 km municipal greenway whose official histories disagree about the former railway's administrative identity.":
        - /url: /rail/history/tanzi-shengang-line/
    - listitem:
      - link "The Taiwan Railways Ruifang–Shen'ao Line A 6.3 km operator-table route with conflicting 1961 and 1965 opening records, passenger and freight service stopped in 1989, and passenger service restored on a shorter surviving route in 2014.":
        - /url: /rail/history/ruifang-shenao-line/

    - listitem:
      - link "The Japanese-era trunk line, 1895–1945 How 臺灣總督府鐵道部 built the west-coast trunk line that became TRA — a 1908 completion at a gauge fixed years earlier under the Qing, two named stations lost to demolition and bombing, and a ten-week gap before the Republic of China's own railway administration took over.":

      - link "Coal and mineral mining railways The private colliery railway that became the Pingxi Line, and the separate gold and copper networks at Jinguashi and the coal railway at Houtong — three industrial systems whose Japanese-era origins are still visible in today's TRA branch and heritage sites.":
        - /url: /rail/history/mining-railways/

      - link "The Taiwan Railways Sanmin Station Track Record The operator's historical PDF records a 2.1 km Sanmin Station subject with 2010 construction and 2017 operation-start fields and an Add track explanation; current TDX places Sanmin at Eastern Main Line position 52.":
        - /url: /rail/history/sanmin-station-track/
    - listitem:
      - link "Port rail connections — Kaohsiung, Keelung, Taichung Kaohsiung's century-old harbour line closed in 2018 and was partly reused for light rail; Keelung's went silent by 2015; only Taichung's port branch still runs freight today, on a construction date that conflicts with its own operator's two histories.":

      - link "The Ten Major Constructions and the THSR BOT crisis Six transport projects launched in the 1970s under one banner, and a fundamentally different procurement model 25 years later for high speed rail — whose 2009 financial crisis a Control Yuan investigation called a \"knockoff BOT\" that left the government carrying nearly all the risk.":

  - paragraph:
    - text: This section holds Taiwan's
    - strong: fixed-guideway
    - text: "systems: services that run on their own track or cable, to published stations, in a published order. That is the property metro, light rail, conventional rail, high speed rail and an aerial ropeway share, and it is what separates them from a bus route or a bike dock."
  - paragraph:
    - text: Below this heading the next level down is a
    - strong: system
    - text: ", not a page type. A system is a network with its own stations, its own numbering and its own fleet: the Taipei Metro network is one, Kaohsiung Rapid Transit another, Taiwan Railway and High Speed Rail two more. Lines, stations, rolling stock and depots belong to a system and are filed under it, so that a TRA line does not have to share an index with the Wenhu Line. Operators, history and technology cut across systems — one company runs metro and light rail, one dispute shaped several lines — so they stay at this level rather than being copied into each."
  - paragraph: The heading says "cable" as well as "rail" because some of these systems are ropeways or cable-hauled forestry railways, and calling them rail without qualification would be a small false claim in the furniture, which is the sort of thing this site keeps catching in itself.
  - paragraph:

    - link "Taipei Metro":

  - paragraph:
    - text: The Alishan Forest Railway is a working heritage railway, not a scenic line invented after the forest industry ended. The operator dates its opening to 1912 and describes a main line of about 72 km with a network that once grew to 21 branches.
    - superscript:
      - link "[1]":
        - /url: "#ref-1"
    - text: Its current public timetable runs from Chiayi to Alishan, while the forest-park branches continue the railway beyond the main-line terminus toward Shenmu, Zhaoping and Zhushan.

  - paragraph:
    - text: The railway is unusually legible as a system because the operator publishes route technology and station information together. Its gauge is 762 mm, and the line climbs from Chiayi at 30 m above sea level to Alishan at 2,216 m before the Zhushan branch reaches 2,451 m.

        - /url: "#ref-1"
    - superscript:
      - link "[2]":
        - /url: "#ref-2"
    - text: "The line is non-electrified and its engineering vocabulary is a response to tight mountain land, not a decorative theme: the official heritage record identifies spiral, horseshoe, Ω/U-turn and Z-shaped alignments alongside the special Shay geared locomotive."
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
  - paragraph:
    - text: The line should be read in two layers. The 16-stop main line is the current intercity-style forest-railway service between Chiayi and Alishan, with a timetable effective from 10 January 2025.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: "The branch timetable is a separate operating pattern inside the Alishan National Forest Recreation Area: Shenmu and Zhaoping have frequent short workings, while the Zhushan service is an observation train whose departure is announced the day before because it is tied to sunrise."
    - superscript:
      - link "[4]":
        - /url: "#ref-4"
    - text: Duigaoyue is a named platform and passing location on the Zhushan alignment in the operator's station overview, but the branch timetable does not establish it as a separately scheduled passenger stop.
    - superscript:
      - link "[2]":
        - /url: "#ref-2"
    - superscript:
      - link "[4]":
        - /url: "#ref-4"
  - paragraph:
    - text: This distinction also explains why station counts vary between pages. The current operator FAQ enumerates 16 main-line stations and four named forest-park points, while the heritage potential-site description uses an older landscape boundary and a different list of 16 named stations.
    - superscript:
      - link "[8]":
        - /url: "#ref-8"
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
    - text: "The guide keeps the inventories side by side in the station data rather than treating a heritage boundary as a current timetable. The older operation-mileage page adds another source view: its matrix omits Luma Chan and the branch points, even though the current operator overview and timetable include Luma Chan and the park services."
    - superscript:
      - link "[9]":
        - /url: "#ref-9"
    - superscript:
      - link "[2]":
        - /url: "#ref-2"
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
  - paragraph:
    - text: The railway's most famous engineering is concentrated in the climb. At Duli Shan, the track circles the mountain in a three-turn spiral; at Shuisheliao, the Ω-shaped alignment turns the train through 180 degrees; and beyond Pingzhena the railway uses Z-shaped reversals because the mountain shelf is too narrow for a normal curve.
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
    - superscript:
      - link "[2]":
        - /url: "#ref-2"
    - text: "The operator describes the Shay design in the same practical terms: vertical cylinders, bevel gears and flexible drive connections let a short locomotive negotiate tight curves, tunnels and steep grades while relying on adhesion rather than a rack rail."
    - superscript:
      - link "[10]":
        - /url: "#ref-10"
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
  - paragraph:
    - text: The rolling stock records are a roster of families rather than a set of thin vehicle biographies. The operator identifies early 13-ton Shay locomotives, eight 18-ton two-cylinder locomotives bought between 1910 and 1913, and twelve 28-ton three-cylinder locomotives bought between 1912 and 1917.
    - superscript:
      - link "[10]":
        - /url: "#ref-10"
    - text: Its current steam-locomotive page says Nos. 25 and 31 were repaired and returned to running after conversion from coal to diesel firing, with the repairs completed in 2006 and 2004 respectively.
    - superscript:
      - link "[11]":
        - /url: "#ref-11"
    - text: The operator's FAQ separately places No. 26 in static display and says the surviving display and occasional-running locomotives can be seen at the Chiayi and Fenqihu facilities or on the mountain.
    - superscript:
      - link "[8]":
        - /url: "#ref-8"
    - text: "Diesel power is the everyday roster: the operator's table lists active DL25–30, DL31–34, DL38, DL39–43 and DL45–51 groups, alongside retired early Mitsubishi and O&K groups."
    - superscript:
      - link "[12]":
        - /url: "#ref-12"
  - paragraph:
    - text: Typhoon damage is part of the railway's operating history. Typhoon Morakot damaged the system in 2009, and Typhoon Dujuan caused two collapses totalling 55 m in the old No. 42 tunnel between Shizilu and Pingzhena in 2015.
    - superscript:
      - link "[6]":
        - /url: "#ref-6"
    - superscript:
      - link "[7]":
        - /url: "#ref-7"
    - text: The replacement 1,106 m tunnel began construction on 8 January 2021 and was completed on 29 December 2023, according to the railway's project record.
    - superscript:
      - link "[7]":
        - /url: "#ref-7"
    - text: That is an infrastructure milestone; the scheduled passenger reopening was separately announced for 6 July 2024 after Railway Bureau inspection, with four daily main-line services in the opening timetable.
    - superscript:
      - link "[6]":
        - /url: "#ref-6"
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: The distinction matters because “completed” and “open to passengers” are not the same date.
  - paragraph:
    - text: The line is a Taiwanese World Heritage potential site, not an inscribed UNESCO World Heritage property. The Ministry of Culture's heritage page presents the railway and its surrounding cultural landscape as a potential site, describes its 762 mm non-electrified mountain railway, and gives a 71.34 km potential-site scope across Chiayi and Nantou.
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
    - text: The same record compares the route's industrial settlements, forest ecology and mountain engineering with the values usually used to assess railway heritage.
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
    - text: In 2019, the government recreation history records the railway's registration as an important cultural landscape, which is a domestic heritage status distinct from UNESCO inscription.
    - superscript:
      - link "[13]":
        - /url: "#ref-13"
  - paragraph:
    - text: "This system page therefore links to a sourced line record and one station-inventory page. It does not create twenty short articles whose only content would be a name and elevation: the official sources provide a strong route-level history and a useful station table, but not a uniform 300-word engineering or accessibility record for every stop."
    - superscript:
      - link "[2]":
        - /url: "#ref-2"
    - superscript:
      - link "[8]":
        - /url: "#ref-8"
  - paragraph:
    - text: The
    - link "rolling-stock record":
      - /url: /rail/alishan/rolling-stock/fleet-roster/
    - text: goes deeper on the Shay fleet than this page does, including a conflict between the operator's own pages over how many locomotives can still run, and a Wikipedia citation that doesn't check out against the source it names. The
    - link "fares and ridership record":
      - /url: /rail/alishan/operations/fares-and-ridership/
    - text: covers the distance-based fare formula and a full decade of monthly ridership this project extracted directly from an operator PDF an earlier research pass couldn't open.
  - region "References":
    - heading "References" [level=2]
    - paragraph: 13 of 13 sources on this page are primary — published by the operator, the builder or government.
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - link "Railway technology":
          - /url: https://afrch.forest.gov.tw/0000524
        - text: 鐵道技術 primary Alishan Forest Railway and Cultural Heritage Office ( 阿里山林業鐵路及文化資產管理處 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The operator's technical history gives the 1912 opening, approximate main-line length, 762 mm gauge, earlier branch count and the spiral, U-shaped and Z-shaped mountain methods.
      - listitem:
        - link "Alishan Forest Railway station overview":
          - /url: https://afrch.forest.gov.tw/
        - text: 阿里山百年鐵道 primary Alishan Forest Railway and Cultural Heritage Office ( 阿里山林業鐵路及文化資產管理處 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The operator's current station overview gives the published station names, chainages and elevations and describes the forest-park branch points.
      - listitem:
        - link "Main-line timetable":
          - /url: https://afrch.forest.gov.tw/0000115
        - text: 林鐵本線 primary Alishan Forest Railway and Cultural Heritage Office ( 阿里山林業鐵路及文化資產管理處 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The timetable effective 10 January 2025 gives the currently published main-line service sequence and daily train times.
      - listitem:
        - link "Branch-line timetable and closure notes":
          - /url: https://afrch.forest.gov.tw/0000300
        - text: 林鐵支線 primary Alishan Forest Railway and Cultural Heritage Office ( 阿里山林業鐵路及文化資產管理處 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The current branch page gives the Shenmu, Zhaoping and Zhushan service records, the Mianyue closure history and the 6 July 2024 timetable boundary.
      - listitem:
        - link "Alishan Forestry and Railway Cultural Landscape":
          - /url: https://twh.boch.gov.tw/taiwan/intro.aspx?id=7&lang=zh_tw
        - text: 阿里山林業暨鐵道文化景觀 primary Bureau of Cultural Heritage, Ministry of Culture ( 文化部文化資產局 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The official Taiwan World Heritage potential-site page describes the route's heritage status, engineering methods, 71.34 km potential-site boundary and 32,900-hectare landscape.
      - listitem:
        - link "Alishan Forest Railway full-line opening on 6 July 2024":
          - /url: https://www.forest.gov.tw/news/0073945
        - text: 阿里山林鐵113年7月6日全線通車 primary Forestry and Nature Conservation Agency, Ministry of Agriculture ( 農業部林業及自然保育署 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The agency's full announcement records the Morakot and Dujuan typhoon damage, the 15-year interruption, the 6 July 2024 passenger opening, four daily main-line trains and the NT$600 Chiayi–Alishan fare.
      - listitem:
        - link "No. 42 tunnel completion ceremony":

        - text: 林鐵42號隧道竣工典禮 祈願一路順遂 primary Alishan Forest Railway and Cultural Heritage Office ( 阿里山林業鐵路及文化資產管理處 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The official project notice gives the 55 m collapse, the new 1,106 m tunnel, construction start on 8 January 2021 and the engineering and environmental constraints.
      - listitem:
        - link "Frequently asked questions":

        - text: 常見問答 primary Alishan Forest Railway and Cultural Heritage Office ( 阿里山林業鐵路及文化資產管理處 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The operator's current FAQ lists the 16 main-line stations and the named forest-park points and describes the Shay display and running locations.
      - listitem:

        - text: 營業里程 primary Alishan Forest Railway and Cultural Heritage Office ( 阿里山林業鐵路及文化資產管理處 ) accessed 2026-08-25 The operator's mileage matrix, updated 31 March 2016, is retained as a dated historical measurement view.

rail-alishan-operations-fares-and-riders.snapshot:
- main:
  - navigation "Breadcrumb":
    - link "Home":
      - /url: /
    - link "Rail & cable":
      - /url: /rail/
    - link "Alishan Forest Railway":
      - /url: /rail/alishan/
    - link "Operations":
      - /url: /rail/alishan/operations/
    - text: Alishan Forest Railway fares and ridership
  - link "Back to the previous page":
    - /url: /rail/alishan/
  - article:
    - heading "Alishan Forest Railway fares and ridership" [level=1]
    - paragraph: A flat NT$600 to ride the full mountain line, worked out from a published per-kilometre rate — and a decade of monthly ridership data this project extracted directly from the operator's own PDF, showing the branch lines carrying five to ten times the main line's traffic every single year.
    - region "Quick facts":
      - text: Alishan Forest Railway fares and ridership
      - term: Main-line full fare, Chiayi-Alishan
      - definition:
        - text: NT$600 (阿里山號/檜木列車) or NT$540 (中興號)
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - term: Main-line fare structure
      - definition:
        - text: distance-based, NT$8.33/km or NT$7.50/km, 6km minimum
        - superscript:
          - link "[2]":
            - /url: "#ref-2"
      - term: Branch-line fares
      - definition:
        - text: Zhushan NT$150, Shenmu NT$100, Zhaoping NT$100 (full fare)
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - term: Standard concession fare
      - definition:
        - text: 50%
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - term: TPASS coverage
      - definition: TBC (the one domain that would confirm this failed to resolve)
      - term: Historical fare change
      - definition: TBC (only a negative confirmation exists — unchanged at the 2024 reopening)
    - navigation "On this page":
      - paragraph: On this page
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - link "What it costs":
            - /url: "#what-it-costs"
        - listitem:
          - link "Booking, and a limit that isn't a number":
            - /url: "#booking-and-a-limit-that-isnt-a-number"
        - listitem:
          - link "A decade of ridership, extracted directly from the source":
            - /url: "#a-decade-of-ridership-extracted-directly-from-the-source"
        - listitem:
          - link "Remaining gaps":
            - /url: "#remaining-gaps"
        - listitem:
          - link "Specifications":
            - /url: "#specifications"
        - listitem:
          - link "References":
            - /url: "#references"
    - heading "What it costs" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: A full-fare ride the length of the main line,
      - link "Chiayi":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/chiayi/
      - text: to Alishan, costs NT$600 on the 阿里山號 or 檜木列車 services, or NT$540 on the 中興號 local — both figures confirmed unchanged at the railway's July 2024 full-line reopening.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: "The fare isn't a single flat number so much as a distance formula worked backwards: NT$8.33 per kilometre for 阿里山號/區間車, NT$7.50 for the 中興號-class local, each with a six-kilometre minimum — multiplying either rate by the line's 71.6km length lands within a few dollars of the two published full fares."
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: A ticket to Alishan Station comes bundled with admission to Alishan National Forest Recreation Area at no extra charge.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: Fares for intermediate stops exist on a station-pair matrix this page could not reliably read — two attempts at extracting the same table returned two different numbers for the same segment, and neither is published here.
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The three forest-park branch lines charge flat, not distance-based, fares: NT$150 on the Zhushan sunrise line, NT$100 each on the Shenmu and Zhaoping lines, all half-price for concessions."
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: A branch-line day pass covering all three costs NT$400 (or NT$200 concession); a two-day pass costs NT$500 (NT$250 concession) — though neither covers the special New Year Zhushan sunrise service.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: Seniors 65 and over, disability-certificate holders (plus one companion), and children aged 6–11 or 115–149cm tall all qualify for the standard 50% concession fare; younger or shorter children ride free without a seat, capped at two per paying adult, as do licensed tour guides.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - heading "Booking, and a limit that isn't a number" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Tickets go on sale at station counters 12 days before travel, and online on a rolling window from 14 days out to the day before — except the Zhushan sunrise line, whose next-day online booking closes at noon the day before.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: Each ID can book up to six tickets per travel date, or twelve for a same-transaction round trip; a first itinerary change is free, a second costs 10% of the fare, and tickets bought during an announced typhoon warning can be fully refunded within a year.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: The Zhushan line's same-day tickets go on sale 30 minutes before the first departure with what the operator's own FAQ describes only as "a limited number" — no figure is published anywhere found for what that limit actually is.
    - paragraph:
      - text: Whether the
      - link "Alishan Forest Railway":
        - /url: /rail/alishan/lines/alishan-forest-railway/
      - text: "participates in TPASS or any multi-operator pass could not be confirmed either way: the one domain that would answer this authoritatively,"
      - code: tpass.motc.gov.tw
      - text: ", failed to resolve entirely during this research, and every operator page checked is simply silent on the question rather than stating an exclusion."
    - heading "A decade of ridership, extracted directly from the source" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The operator publishes a monthly operations PDF running January 2014 through December 2023.
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: A first research pass could not extract its contents; fetched directly and read with
      - code: pdftotext
      - text: in the main session, it gives a clean decade of monthly passenger, passenger-kilometre and load-factor figures, split between the main line and the three branch lines combined.
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: "Summed by year, the branch lines carry five to ten times the main line's annual ridership throughout the entire decade — unsurprising given their short length and status as popular short excursions, especially the Zhushan sunrise service, against the main line's long haul to Alishan:"

      - text: "The source data itself is not perfectly clean: three consecutive months in mid-2019 show negative or zero main-line passenger figures, which likely reflect an accounting correction during a service disruption rather than literal negative ridership — no source explains it, so it's reported here exactly as it appears in the primary data, not smoothed away."
