    - paragraph:
      - text: The station positions and elevations in the table come from the operator's current overview, while the main-line service status and sequence come from its published timetable.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: The operator's separate mileage matrix was updated on 31 March 2016 and omits Luma Chan from its station columns, so its values are retained as a dated source view rather than used to erase the newer station record.
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: "Chiayi is the lowland interchange: the operator describes it as the railway's connection to the Western Trunk Line and notes the former three-railway arrangement of TRA, sugar railway and forest railway."
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: Beimen is the timber-built gateway, estimated by the operator to date from 1910–1912 and built with Alishan red cypress.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: Zhuqi is the end of the flat section and the start of the climb; the government station history also records its historic triangle track for turning locomotives when Zhuqi and Erwanping were the two ends of the early mountain operation.
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The middle stations show why a station list is not just a sequence of names. Duli Shan is the point where the railway climbs in a three-turn spiral, while Shuisheliao's Ω-shaped track turns the train through 180 degrees.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: Fenqihu is the principal intermediate station with five tracks and a long history as a mountain settlement; its current station landscape was redesigned in 2021 with local planting and permeable paving.
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: Pingzhena is a reversing station, after which the line enters the famous Z-shaped ascent toward the high mountain section.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: Alishan is the current main-line terminus and the origin of the forest-park branches. The present station was built as a new terminus when tourism outgrew Zhaoping, opened in 1981, closed after the 1999 earthquake, and reopened on its rebuilt site in September 2007.
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: Zhaoping is the old terminus, first built in 1914 and replaced by a two-level building opened in 2013 that combines railway functions with exhibition and local cultural uses.
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: Shenmu was historically the third passing point, became known for the giant red cypress beside the track, and received a 2022 repair that added waiting space, weather protection, an accessible ramp and a restored passing track.
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The highest point in the current inventory is Zhushan at 2,451 m, reached by the sunrise-oriented branch; Duigaoyue lies on that route at 2,405 m with a platform and passing track, but no independent passenger timetable is published for it.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: Mianyue is deliberately absent from the operating table because the operator records it as a closed historical tourist railway after earthquake damage and later collapses.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: A future historical-stations page can add its former stops when the operator or a conservation record supplies a complete, citable inventory.

      - link "Zoo South Station The only one of the gondola's four stations to carry a different name today than the one it opened with — renamed from Zoo Interior Station eight years after opening, which is why the Control Yuan's own 2009 report on this line still calls it by the old name.":
        - /url: /rail/cable/stations/zoo-south-station/
    - listitem:
      - link "Zoo Station The gondola's lower terminus — a separate structure roughly 350 metres from the Wenhu Line's own Taipei Zoo station, not a shared platform, joined only by an out-of-station transfer.":
        - /url: /rail/cable/stations/zoo-station/
  - paragraph: "One system, one line: the Maokong Gondola. It is an aerial ropeway — a POMA installation, not a railway — and it is filed here rather than under its own top-level heading because a heading for a single line is a heading that says nothing. What it shares with the rest of this section is the thing this section is organised by: it runs on its own fixed guideway, to published stations, in a published order, inside the region's stored-value ticketing, and it meets the metro at Taipei Zoo."
  - paragraph: "The gondola is part of the network in the ways that matter here: metro affiliation, shared ticketing, and a genuine engineering and incident history that English coverage — which is entirely tourist-oriented — has not touched. The story worth telling is the long typhoon closure: a tower foundation undermined, a multi-institute engineering assessment, and a reopening under monitoring. That is the kind of material this site exists for, and it is written against the city's own engineering publications rather than travel blogs."

    - paragraph:
      - link "Taipei":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
      - text: "'s cable car climbs from the zoo to a tea-growing hillside on a line that is, for a tourist ride, unusually well documented by the government that owns it — because in 2008 one of its towers nearly fell into a residential neighbourhood, and the Control Yuan wrote a 22-page corrective resolution about why"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: .
    - heading "The system" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Maokong Gondola opened 4 July 2007, built by Taipei City's New Construction Office to a design supplied by the French ropeway manufacturer POMA, with 財團法人中華顧問工程司 (renamed 台灣世曦工程顧問股份有限公司 partway through the project) and 武林建築師事務所 supervising and 春原營造股份有限公司 building it as design-build contractor under a 最有利標 ("most advantageous tender") award of 2 May 2005
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . It was Taipei's first cable car
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: and is reported as Taiwan's longest gondola route
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The line runs 4.033 km — published as 4.03 km throughout the construction-era and Control Yuan record, almost certainly the same figure carried to one more decimal place on the operator's current site rather than a real disagreement
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: . It has
      - strong: four passenger stations
      - text: —
      - link "動物園站":
        - /url: /rail/cable/stations/zoo-station/
      - text: Zoo Station,
      - link "動物園南站":
        - /url: /rail/cable/stations/zoo-south-station/
      - text: Zoo South Station,
      - link "指南宮站":
        - /url: /rail/cable/stations/zhinan-temple-station/
      - text: Zhinan Temple Station, and
      - link "貓空站":
        - /url: /rail/cable/stations/maokong-station/
      - text: Maokong Station — plus
      - strong: two non-boarding angle stations
      - text: the alignment needs because it is not straight ("略呈7字型," roughly 7-shaped)
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: . Zoo South Station opened under the name 動物園內站 ("Zoo Interior Station") and was not renamed to its current form until 26 October 2015
      - superscript:
        - link "[13]":
          - /url: "#ref-13"
      - text: — which is why the Control Yuan's 2009 report on the same station still calls it 園內站. One-way journey time is given by the operator as
      - strong: 20 to 30 minutes
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: ; zh.wikipedia separately gives approximately 17 minutes, sourced to an in-article footnote not independently checked here
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: — both figures are published rather than one chosen over the other.
    - paragraph:
      - text: The system's own current page counts
      - strong: 25 pier bases carrying 47 tower columns
      - text: ", implying most bases carry a two-legged frame; the Control Yuan's 2009 resolution instead gives a single figure of 25 towers for the whole line"
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . The whole project's cost is given two ways in that same Control Yuan document — an approximate
      - strong: NT$1.3 billion
      - text: in its opening summary and a precise
      - strong: NT$1,108,870,438
      - text: later in the text discussing the planning contractor's survey work — without the document explaining whether the two figures cover different scopes
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: .
    - heading "The T16 failure" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: In September 2008 three typhoons crossed Taiwan in eighteen days — 辛樂克 (11–16 September), 哈格比 (21–23 September) and 薔蜜 Jangmi (26–30 September)
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . Their combined rainfall reached
      - strong: 1,271.5 mm
      - text: for the month in the
      - link "Muzha":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br02/
      - text: area — the Central Weather Bureau's second-highest September figure there in 22 years
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . Jangmi's own contribution on 28 September alone was separately measured at roughly 500 mm over Wenshan District, and it was that single day's rain that triggered the report the city acted on
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The slope below tower
      - strong: T16
      - text: began failing on 27 September; its first two sections slid on 28 September, sending debris into the 政大御花園社區 community below and prompting the evacuation of roughly 72 households (about 200 people) that night, with the debris stopping about 20 m short of the nearest building
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . A third, residual section of the slope came down after further heavy rain on 9 November. The city suspended service at
      - strong: 15:00 on 1 October 2008
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: Taipei's Department of Industrial Development commissioned
      - strong: four Taipei professional associations
      - text: — civil, geotechnical, structural, and soil-and- water-conservation engineering — to assess the failure, T16's remaining safety, and whether the tower should be reinforced in place or moved. Their initial report came 30 November 2008, the full report 12 December
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . It found T16's well-type foundation (井式基礎) left cantilevered by roughly 4 metres, with the overturning moment the exposed foundation would face in an earthquake exceeding what its existing reinforcement could carry — though continuous tilt monitoring installed from late September 2008 found no measurable tilt, displacement or settlement in T16 or any other tower over the following three months
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . In-place reinforcement was judged technically possible if carried out early in the slide, which the city did not do; by the time it acted, conditions had worsened enough that the assessors recommended relocation as the safer course
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Taipei City Government relocated T16
      - text: ", rather than rebuilding it in place — a decision the Control Yuan's own corrective resolution explicitly endorses. Engineers compared two candidate drill sites (NH-1, NH-2) toward neighbouring tower T17; POMA's own engineers preferred NH-1 as closest to the original tower's centreline and elevation, and both candidate sites tested with better geology than the original. Mayor Hau Lung-bin announced the new site at a press conference on 23 January 2009;"
      - strong: the rebuilt tower stands about 30 m from where the old one stood
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Control Yuan's own November 2009 investigation — carried out by committee members 杜善良, 葛永光 and 陳永祥 over more than eleven months
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: — went well beyond T16 itself. It rejected public allegations that the foundation piling had been built with substandard materials or that the site had no bedrock at all, but separately found fault with all three of the project's engineering contractors — the planning firm 鼎漢公司, project manager 台灣世曦, and design-build contractor 春原營造 — for inadequate geotechnical survey work along the whole alignment, and with the city government itself for a slow initial emergency response and for never requiring a proper site-wide geological survey in the original planning contract
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: .
    - heading "Reopening" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The gondola reopened in stages in March 2010: Mayor Hau announced on 18 March that formal service would resume 30 March;"
      - link "TRTC":
        - /url: /rail/operators/trtc/
      - text: published the detailed reopening rules on 21 March; a six-day
      - strong: free trial
      - text: ran 23–28 March, 10,000 free rides a day, 102,000+ riders over the six days; and
      - strong: formal, paid service resumed 30 March 2010
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: ". Two figures both appear in sources for \"the reopening date\" — 23 March and 30 March — and neither is wrong: they are the free trial's start and the formal reopening, respectively, both individually dated in the same source"
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The reopening had two small early scares. On 7 April 2010 a tilt-monitoring alarm on neighbouring tower
      - strong: T15
      - text: turned out to be a false alarm, with no actual movement found
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: . On 9 April, one week after reopening and with cumulative ridership past 100,000, a cable-detection alarm halted the system for 4 minutes 5 seconds that evening — no passengers were trapped, and service resumed within the hour
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: . By 29 April, ridership since reopening had reached 270,000
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: Over its first operating period — 4 July 2007 to 1 October 2008, about 15 months — the gondola carried more than
      - strong: 6.17 million riders
      - text: ", per zh.wikipedia's own footnoted figure"
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: .
    - heading "The crystal cabins" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: From the 30 March 2010 reopening, one pilot cabin ran with a transparent floor
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: . The full
      - strong: "\"貓纜之眼\" (\"Eyes of Maokong\") crystal-cabin fleet — 31 units — entered service from 2 November 2010"
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: ". Each floor is three layers of tempered glass, about 48 mm thick and 213 kg, CE-certified, and the extra weight costs three seats: a crystal cabin carries 5 passengers against a standard cabin's 8"
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: . zh.wikipedia separately gives the crystal cabins' individual numbers as 1–15, 66 and 133–147 (car 66 the original prototype) and puts the whole fleet, standard and crystal together, at
      - strong: 147 cabins including 3 spares
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: — a figure not independently checked against a primary fleet roster, though the 31-cabin crystal count matches the operator's own page.
    - heading "Fares and rules" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: A single one-way ride costs NT$180 full fare / NT$50 discount fare
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: ; an unlimited all-day pass is NT$300 / NT$100
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: . Upgrading to a crystal cabin adds NT$50 per person per trip; chartering a whole cabin adds NT$600 per trip
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: . Groups of 20 or more get 10% off an all-day pass, 40 or more get 20% off
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: . Discount fares are for Taipei City residents, retired city civil servants and teachers, children 6–11, seniors 65 and over (or Taipei-registered Indigenous residents 55 and over), and people with disabilities plus one companion — shown at boarding and tapped through a dedicated gate with a stored-value card
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: .
      - link "EasyCard":
        - /url: /ticketing/guides/cards-passes-and-fares/
      - text: and other stored-value cards work across the whole system
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: . The operator's current fare page makes no mention of the TPASS 基北北桃1200 monthly pass as an accepted option; a 2023 council-session report says TRTC had evaluated adding the gondola to TPASS but chose not to, to avoid complicating ticketing during the pass's early rollout
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - superscript:
        - link "[14]":
          - /url: "#ref-14"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: Service suspends automatically for a sustained gust of 16 m/s (roughly Beaufort 7) for three seconds or more, any gust of 18 m/s (Beaufort 8) or more, lightning on the route, an earthquake of intensity 4 or greater, or when a land typhoon warning covers Taipei and either weather or a city work/school closure calls for it
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: . Routine maintenance closes the system on scattered Mondays through the year, plus a separate, longer annual-overhaul block of consecutive Mondays in some months — the published 2026 calendar does not follow a simple "first Monday of the month" pattern
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: .
    - heading "Now" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The gondola is operated by
      - strong: North Metro Recreation Company (北捷遊憩事業股份 有限公司)
      - text: ", a 2025 joint subsidiary of Taipei City Government and TRTC that also runs"
      - link "Taipei Arena":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/g17/
      - text: and the Taipei Children's Amusement Park
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: . Cumulative ridership passed
      - strong: 40 million riders on 19 May 2026
      - text: ", ahead of the system's 20th operating anniversary in July 2027"
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: .

    - heading "One historical double-track record" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Taiwan Railways' full construction-history table lists Changhua–Minxiong as a 71.7 km double-track segment.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: The table gives 1957 as the construction year and 1970 as the operation-start year, with Taiwan Railways Administration listed as the constructor.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: Its explanation is 添築雙線, rendered by the operator as “Extended to be double-tracked.”
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The full operator PDF repeats the same segment and values in its row 43, so the HTML table and PDF are two presentations of the same primary construction record, not two different measurements.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: This page therefore treats 71.7 km as the operator's historical construction-table scope. It does not turn the row into a separate present-day line, and it does not infer that the table's operation-start field supplies an exact commissioning date.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
    - heading "Current endpoints are a separate data layer" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The current operator station page identifies
      - link "Changhua":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/changhua/
      - text: as station 3360 and displays current service entries at that station.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: The current Minxiong page identifies station 4060 and likewise displays current service entries.
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: These pages establish the current station records named by the historical segment; they do not provide the historical construction contract, intermediate station register or track plan.
    - paragraph:
      - text: The committed TDX StationOfLine snapshot places Changhua in the Western Main Line and
      - link "Western Main Line (Coast Line)":
        - /url: /rail/tra/lines/western-main-line-coast-line-coast/
      - text: families, while Minxiong is in the
      - link "Western Main Line":
        - /url: /rail/tra/lines/western-main-line/
      - text: .
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: That current membership is useful for locating the two anchors in today's data model. It is not a claim that the 71.7 km construction-table entry maps one-to-one onto one current TDX route record, or that every current service uses the same stopping pattern.
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The table's phrase “double-tracked” is retained as a construction explanation, not silently upgraded into a current track-count survey.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: A historical construction record, a current line-membership dataset and a live station information page answer different questions. Keeping them separate avoids adding the segment length to a current travelled-distance field or inventing a second Western Main Line identity.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
    - heading "Records still missing" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The checked operator records provide years, the 71.7 km table distance and the double-track explanation, but not the day and month of construction or opening, the contract and completion certificate, a surveyed boundary, an intermediate station list for the historical segment, or a current track-count/as-built survey.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: Those fields remain TBC. The current station and TDX records confirm the live anchors and memberships; they do not fill the historical engineering gaps.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":

rail-history-circular-line-0403-earthqua.snapshot:
- main:
  - article:
    - navigation "Breadcrumb":
      - link "Home":
        - /url: /
      - link "Rail & cable":
        - /url: /rail/
      - link "History":
        - /url: /rail/history/
      - text: The Circular Line's 0403 earthquake
    - heading "The Circular Line's 0403 earthquake" [level=1]
    - paragraph: "What the official investigation says about the 3 April 2024 earthquake: a pot-bearing mechanism, a design and inspection chain, the eight-month recovery, and a cause still disputed by the contractor."
    - region "Quick facts":
      - link "Y":
        - /url: /rail/metro/lines/circular-line/
      - link "Circular Line":
        - /url: /rail/metro/lines/circular-line/
      - text: 環狀線
      - term: Earthquake
      - definition:
        - text: 3 April 2024, magnitude 7.2
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - term: Girder displacement locations
      - definition:
        - text: "11"
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - term: Damaged equipment items
      - definition:
        - text: "139"
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - term: Largest reported girder displacement
      - definition:
        - text: "92"
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - term: Full service restored
      - definition:
        - text: 12 December 2024
        - superscript:
          - link "[3]":
            - /url: "#ref-3"
      - term: Formal correction directed at
      - definition:
        - link "Taipei":
          - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
        - text: City Government
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
    - navigation "On this page":
      - paragraph: On this page
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - link "What the investigation says":
            - /url: "#what-the-investigation-says"
        - listitem:
          - link "The pot-bearing mechanism":
            - /url: "#the-pot-bearing-mechanism"
        - listitem:
          - link "More than a construction finding":
            - /url: "#more-than-a-construction-finding"
        - listitem:
          - link "The shaking and the code":
            - /url: "#the-shaking-and-the-code"
        - listitem:
          - link "What is disputed":
            - /url: "#what-is-disputed"
        - listitem:
          - link "References":
            - /url: "#references"
    - heading "What the investigation says" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: At 07:58 on 3 April 2024, a magnitude 7.2 earthquake in Hualien damaged the pot bearings connecting the
      - link "Circular Line":
        - /url: /rail/metro/lines/circular-line/
      - text: "'s steel box girders to their piers."
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: The Control Yuan's investigation records eleven girder-displacement locations, track deformation and 139 damaged equipment items; its account says no train was on the damaged section when the earthquake struck.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: New
      - link "Taipei":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
      - text: DORTS reported a displacement range of about 3.5 to 92 cm, with seven of the eleven locations in the 20–92 cm severe group.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The line's operator describes the repair in a different unit: nine steel-box- girder spans were repositioned, and the full line resumed service at noon on 12 December 2024."
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: The two counts are not silently merged. Eleven locations and nine spans may be related, but the sources read here do not publish a damage schedule mapping one to the other.
    - heading "The pot-bearing mechanism" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Control Yuan's first finding concerns the grade-adjustment plate (調坡板) between the girder and the pot bearing.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: It says the contractor, BES Engineering, milled through the plate instead of building to the construction drawings. That left excess space above the locating pin; during the earthquake the pin jumped upward, its base left the interface between the upper and lower bearing plates, and the bearing lost its shear resistance.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph: "The report's dimensions make the proposed mechanism checkable:"
    - table:
      - rowgroup:
        - row "Measurement Value":
          - columnheader "Measurement"
          - columnheader "Value"
      - rowgroup:
        - row "Recess shown on the shop drawing 5 mm[1]":
          - cell "Recess shown on the shop drawing"
          - cell "5 mm[1]":
            - text: 5 mm
            - superscript:
              - link "[1]":
                - /url: "#ref-1"
        - row "Recess measured in the field 41 mm[1]":
          - cell "Recess measured in the field"
          - cell "41 mm[1]":
            - text: 41 mm
            - superscript:
              - link "[1]":
                - /url: "#ref-1"
        - row "Space left above the locating pin 36 mm[1]":
          - cell "Space left above the locating pin"
          - cell "36 mm[1]":
            - text: 36 mm
            - superscript:
              - link "[1]":
                - /url: "#ref-1"
        - row "Locating-pin height 40 mm[1]":
          - cell "Locating-pin height"
          - cell "40 mm[1]":
            - text: 40 mm
            - superscript:
              - link "[1]":
                - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The report explains the arithmetic as 36 mm of excess space plus the required 5 mm of engagement, for a 41 mm recess around a pin only 40 mm high.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: After the damaged bridges were jacked up, the New Taipei City Civil Engineers Association found pins lodged in the bearing's upper plate or fallen onto the pier cap.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - heading "More than a construction finding" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The investigation does not describe the earthquake damage as a contractor-only story.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: It says the structure was Taiwan's first stacked viaduct of this type, with climbing and descending sections and tree-form piers, but that no higher design standard or displacement-limiting devices were added and no external structural review was performed.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: It also records an error in the detailed design calculation that double-deducted dead load when estimating the bearing's uplift demand, and a pot-bearing drawing whose pin dimensions conflict between its note, table and the pins found on site.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The report's third finding is about inspection. The grade-adjustment plate was a contractor-designed, factory-assembled secondary component that became hidden when the girder was installed, so it was not an inspection hold point. The Control Yuan says its review of other listed elevated-bridge and railway projects found the same component absent from their inspection checkpoints. It records Taipei DORTS adding a pot-bearing inspection flow chart and sampling standard on 13 December 2024.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The monitoring finding is separate but important. Zhongyuan station had triaxial accelerometers at both ends of the platform level, but the Control Yuan says their signals were not relayed to the control centre. It found no record of seismic data from those instruments in the Circular Line control centre between the line's opening and the investigation.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - heading "The shaking and the code" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The report says the affected viaduct was designed under the 2006 railway-bridge seismic code with a Taipei-basin design ground motion of 0.24 g and an importance factor of 1.2, producing a minimum design force of 0.288 g.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: At the nearby 積穗國小 station, the report records a peak horizontal acceleration of 0.229 g, below that design value, and a peak ground velocity of 32.16 cm/s.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Control Yuan's comparison is between seismic microzones, not between metro lines. It says the DF112 range around Zhonghe and Yonghe saw horizontal peak ground acceleration about twice that in adjacent zones and peak ground velocity about fifteen times higher, while the neighbouring DF111 and DF113 ranges had no bridge damage in this earthquake.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: It separately finds that the 2021 revision of the national bridge-seismic code still did not address transverse, sideways displacement in the way the investigation considered necessary.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - heading "What is disputed" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: BES's own statement says the damaged section was between its
      - link "Y12":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/y12/
      - link "Qiaohe":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/y13/
      - text: and
      - link "Y14":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/y14/
      - link "Banxin":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/y15/
      - text: engineering labels and that the contractor followed the approved drawings.
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: BES says the upper and lower bearing arrangements both had milled-through slope plates but only the upper support failed; it therefore argues that the milling-through detail and bearing failure were not the main cause, and that the design strength and unequal seismic demand require further examination.
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
    - paragraph:
      - text: That position conflicts with the Control Yuan's finding that the work did not follow the drawings and that the pin's loss of the shear interface was the failure mechanism.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: The sources on this page establish the competing positions, not a final court determination. The full court merits judgment, final settlement and current responsibility allocation remain TBC.
    - paragraph:
      - text: The repair itself added permanent unseating-prevention and uplift-restraint devices as a second line of defence, while replacing the pot-bearing facilities and restoring track, cables and other systems.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: That is the published remedy; it does not by itself decide which party's explanation of the original cause will prevail.
    - region "References":
      - heading "References" [level=2]
      - paragraph: 4 of 4 sources on this page are primary — published by the operator, the builder or government.
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - 'link "Investigation report 114交調0005: Circular Line 0403 earthquake damage"':
            - /url: https://www.cy.gov.tw/CyBsBoxContent.aspx?s=49082
          - text: 監察院調查報告 114交調0005 primary Control Yuan of the Republic of China ( 監察院 ) accessed 2026-08-27 Official Control Yuan case record and report landing page. It identifies the commissioners, review and publication dates, supplies the report files, and records the investigation's findings on the earthquake damage, pot bearings, design, supervision, instrumentation and code. The report's direct files are the DOCX at https://cybsbox.cy.gov.tw/CYBsBoxSSL/edoc/download/68978 and PDF at https://cybsbox.cy.gov.tw/CYBsBoxSSL/edoc/download/72631.
        - listitem:
          - link "Eleven locations severely damaged on the Circular Line; recovery initially estimated at over a year":
            - /url: https://www.dorts.ntpc.gov.tw/news/indexInfo/1AldprRBmLK7
          - text: 環狀線11處受損嚴重 初估復原工期超過1年 primary New Taipei City Government Department of Rapid Transit Systems ( 新北市政府捷運工程局 ) accessed 2026-08-27 The 24 April 2024 official damage notice. It records 11 steel-box-girder displacement locations, a range of about 3.5 to 92 cm, the seven severe and four less-severe locations, the initial over-one-year recovery estimate, and the staged operating response.
        - listitem:
          - link "New Taipei Circular Line ready; full service resumes at noon":
            - /url: https://www.ntmetro.com.tw/basic/?mode=detail&node=754
          - text: 新北環狀線準備好了!確認安全無虞12:00 全線復駛 primary New Taipei Metro Corporation ( 新北大眾捷運股份有限公司 ) accessed 2026-08-27 The operator's 12 December 2024 reopening notice. It records nine repositioned steel-box-girder spans, 139 damaged items, 1,438 replaced track baseplates, 1,050 metres of restored track, 41,500 metres of replaced cable, the 248-day repair account and the added permanent unseating and uplift-restraint devices.
        - listitem:
          - link "Circular Line statement":
            - /url: https://www.bes.com.tw/en/news_detail.php?id=186
          - text: 環狀線聲明稿 primary BES Engineering Corporation ( 中華工程股份有限公司 ) accessed 2026-08-27 BES's 6 January 2025 statement of its own technical and legal position.       - text: Metro incidents and service disruptions
    - heading "Metro incidents and service disruptions" [level=1]
    - paragraph: A primary-source record of flooding, derailment, signalling faults, fires and earthquake disruptions, with unresolved counts and dates left visible.
    - paragraph:
      - text: The page is a chronology of what the cited primary records establish, with the live operator log treated as a dated snapshot rather than a permanent archive.
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
    - navigation "On this page":
      - paragraph: On this page
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - 'link "Flooding: Typhoon Nari"':
            - /url: "#flooding-typhoon-nari"
        - listitem:
          - 'link "Derailment: Xiaonanmen"':
            - /url: "#derailment-xiaonanmen"
        - listitem:
          - link "Signals, smoke and fire":
            - /url: "#signals-smoke-and-fire"
        - listitem:
          - 'link "Earthquake: Circular and Ankeng lines"':
            - /url: "#earthquake-circular-and-ankeng-lines"

        - listitem:
          - link "References":
            - /url: "#references"
    - 'heading "Flooding: Typhoon Nari" [level=2]'
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The primary records agree on the scale of the September 2001 disaster: DORTS technical material records flooding at 16 underground stations, one depot and one high-capacity control centre, followed by three months of repairs and full service on 15 December."
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: Another DORTS volume says the control centre flooded to approximately 4.7 metres and that its train-control computers were badly damaged.
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
    - paragraph:
      - text: DORTS names the
      - link "Taipei":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
      - text: Main Station–Taiwan Railways shared underground area, the Zhongxiao Dunhua–department-store interface and
      - link "Kunyang":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/bl21/
      - text: station entrances as examples of openings through which water entered.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: The same engineering volume records later flood gates, watertight doors and removable barriers, including a design criterion based on the recorded Nari water level plus 20 centimetres.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The Control Yuan's correction adds an accountability record: it found flood preparation and drills deficient and identified defects in the Zhongxiao Fuxing station Y-shaped ventilation-shaft partition and the shared Taipei Main Station underground interfaces involving DORTS,"
      - link "TRTC":
        - /url: /rail/operators/trtc/
      - text: and Taiwan Railways.
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
    - 'heading "Derailment: Xiaonanmen" [level=2]'
    - paragraph:
      - text: At 04:00 on 13 September 2016, an engineering vehicle at the
      - link "Xiaonanmen":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/g11/
      - text: station platform toward
      - link "Songshan":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/g19/
      - text: had a wheel leave the rail and could not move.
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: The response ran the Xiaonanmen–Zhongshan section single-track in both directions for 11 hours 39 minutes and used shuttle buses for the interrupted sections.
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: The fetched primary does not establish the exact restoration clock, the vehicle type or the mechanical cause, so those details remain TBC.
    - heading "Signals, smoke and fire" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: TRTC records a 2025 Wenhu Line signalling anomaly between Zhongshan Junior High School and
      - link "Wende":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br18/
      - text: .
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: The line continued operating, with longer waits; the release attributes the immediate recovery to restarting a delayed signalling-network transmission system and says the detailed cause was still to be clarified with the original manufacturer.
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
    - paragraph:
      - text: On 11 March 2022, sparks and smoke appeared in the track between Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall and
      - link "NTU Hospital":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/r09/
      - text: .
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: Trains passed slowly, a driver went down to extinguish the fire, and TRTC later replaced the failed insulation-baseplate assembly and embedded sleeve.
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
    - paragraph:
      - text: On 28 December 2025, a fire alarm at the main substation outside Zhongxiao Fuxing was traced to an abnormal main transformer.
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: Power transfer restored train operation, nobody was injured, and some nearby lifts and escalators were temporarily affected.
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
    - paragraph:
      - text: TRTC's live operations table, fetched on 17 August 2026, also records a
      - link "BR10":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br10/
      - text: signalling fault, an
      - link "O07":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/o07/
      - text: signalling fault, passenger power-bank smoke/fire at
      - link "O11":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/o11/
      - text: ", third-rail cable smoke at"
      - link "BL07":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/bl07/
      - text: and platform-door automatic-opening failure at
      - link "BL15":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/bl15/
      - text: .
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: The table gives the local response and service effect for each row; its live nature means these entries should be re-fetched before being treated as a historical register.
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The DORTS Wenhu project record supplies an older primary description without a station or exact date: during 1993 system testing, the Muzha Line had a tyre- ignition accident."
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: The station, unit, time and relationship to the two fires described in secondary histories remain TBC.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - 'heading "Earthquake: Circular and Ankeng lines" [level=2]'
    - paragraph:
      - text: The 3 April 2024 earthquake displaced eleven Circular Line girder locations and is covered in the focused
      - link "0403 earthquake investigation":
        - /url: /rail/history/circular-line-0403-earthquake/
      - text: . closed the damaged section.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - superscript:
        - link "[13]":
          - /url: "#ref-13"
      - text: The Control Yuan investigation attributes the failure to construction and inspection problems around the bearing assembly, while New Taipei DORTS records seven severe displacements of 20–92 centimetres and four smaller displacements.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - superscript:
        - link "[13]":
          - /url: "#ref-13"
    - paragraph:
      - link "NTMC":
        - /url: /rail/operators/ntmc/
      - text: recorded full Circular Line suspension on the day, followed by single-track bidirectional operation between Banqiao and
      - link "New Taipei Industrial Park":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/y20/
      - text: from 17:00.
      - superscript:
        - link "[14]":
          - /url: "#ref-14"
      - text: Full service resumed at noon on 12 December 2024; the operator's repair inventory says nine steel-box-girder spans were repositioned, alongside track-baseplate, cable and equipment replacement.
      - superscript:
        - link "[15]":
          - /url: "#ref-15"
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The same earthquake temporarily changed Ankeng LRT service: NTMC recorded"
      - link "K09":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/k09/
      - text: –
      - link "K06":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/k06/
      - text: single-track bidirectional working and
      - link "K06":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/k06/
      - text: –
      - link "K01":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/k01/
      - text: partial operation, followed by normal service at 16:30 with a 15-minute headway.
      - superscript:
        - link "[16]":
          - /url: "#ref-16"
      - superscript:
        - link "[14]":
          - /url: "#ref-14"
    - heading "Conflicts and gaps" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: DORTS technical-book no. 29 p. 87 labels Nari 「民國90年9月6日」, while DORTS technical journal no. 46 p. 214 gives 「民國90年9月17日」.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: Both dates are published here; no fetched primary reconciles them.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Control Yuan and New Taipei DORTS count eleven Circular Line displacement locations, while NTMC's reopening release counts nine spans repositioned. The sources appear to count different things, but no fetched primary explicitly maps eleven locations to nine spans, so this page does not choose between them.

      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":

      - text: In the aligned chronology, the record carries 1973 as the construction year and 1974 as the operation-start year.
      - superscript:

      - superscript:

      - text: The following rows contain separate 添築雙線 (“Extended to be double-tracked”) entries, but their explanations are not transferred to Jianan–Taichung Port.

    - paragraph:
      - text: This page calls it a PDF-recorded construction subject because the source provides a historical record, not a current route identity. The 7.8 km value is therefore retained as the PDF's construction-table scope.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: The operation-start field supplies a year, not an exact commissioning date, and the absence of a row-45 explanation is not converted into a claim about the current track count.

    - heading "Two operator presentations, not one merged table" [level=2]

      - text: and
      - link "Chiayi–Xinshi":
        - /url: /rail/history/chiayi-xinshi-double-track/
      - text: records as its rows 23 and 24, and then proceeds to a row 25
      - link "Xinpu–Tongxiao":

      - text: entry.

      - superscript:

      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: That address keeps the historical Jianan wording visible as a research lead, but it does not establish that the historical PDF place name is a current station identity or that the 7.8 km scope has a one-to-one present-day boundary.

      - text: These are current data observations, not evidence that the historical name should be renamed to Taichung Port or that a current track count can be inferred.
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - superscript:

      - superscript:

      - text: They also do not supply a verified current station ID for the historical Jianan name; that mapping remains TBC rather than being inferred from a street address.

- main:
  - article:
    - figure "The system Matra built and left — a VAL 256 on the Wenhu Line at Zhongxiao Fuxing. Lokseng01 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons":

      - text: ·

      - text: The Matra dispute
    - heading "The Matra dispute" [level=1]
    - paragraph: Two disputes thirteen years apart, usually told as one — the test-track fires an engineering change explains, the seventeen-year lawsuit Matra won, and the walkout that taught Taipei how to buy its next railway.
    - paragraph:
      - text: Taiwan's first metro line was bought as a French turnkey system in 1988, caught fire twice on the test track in 1993, opened in 1996 more than four years late, and lost its builder's maintenance staff not long afterwards
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: . Seventeen years after the signing, the Supreme Court ordered
      - link "Taipei":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
      - text: to pay Matra roughly
      - strong: NT$1.64 billion
      - text: ", and the city paid"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph: Almost all tellings run this together into one story about a French company storming off. It is two stories, thirteen years apart, and telling them apart is the point of this page.

    - heading "Two disputes, not one" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - strong: The delay claim, 1988–2005.
      - text: Matra sued for the cost of a contract that ran years longer than it was written for, because the civil works its equipment depended on were late — the claim arises, in 自由時報's words, 「因土木工程部分包商施工延誤，連帶造成馬特拉的工期延長，增加成本費用」
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . This is the dispute that went to arbitration in 1993 and was still before the Supreme Court in 2005
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . It is about money and contract law, and
      - strong: Matra won it
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - strong: The withdrawal, 1996–97.
      - text: After the line opened, Matra pulled its technical staff out of Taiwan and stopped maintaining the system
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: . This is the dispute everybody remembers — the one that produced the most famous sentence said about the
      - link "Taipei Metro":
        - /url: /rail/operators/trtc/
      - text: ", and the one that steered the procurement that followed."
    - paragraph:
      - text: "They are connected: the withdrawal happened because the delay claim had poisoned the relationship. But they are not the same event, and the NT$1.64 billion that circulates belongs to the first, not the second"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - heading "The contract" [level=2]
    - table:
      - rowgroup:
        - row "Term Agreed Source":
          - columnheader "Term"
          - columnheader "Agreed"
          - columnheader "Source"
      - rowgroup:
        - row "Matra selected as preferred bidder 20 April 1988 [6]":
          - cell "Matra selected as preferred bidder"
          - cell "20 April 1988"
          - cell "[6]":
            - superscript:
              - link "[6]":
                - /url: "#ref-6"
        - row "Negotiations concluded 25 June 1988 [6]":
          - cell "Negotiations concluded"
          - cell "25 June 1988"
          - cell "[6]":
            - superscript:
              - link "[6]":
                - /url: "#ref-6"
        - row "Contract signed 13 July 1988 [6][1]":
          - cell "Contract signed"
          - cell "13 July 1988"
          - cell "[6][1]":
            - superscript:
              - link "[6]":
                - /url: "#ref-6"
            - superscript:
              - link "[1]":
                - /url: "#ref-1"
        - row "Value ≈ NT$7.87 billion [6]":
          - cell "Value"
          - cell "≈ NT$7.87 billion"
          - cell "[6]":
            - superscript:
              - link "[6]":
                - /url: "#ref-6"
        - row "Scope Muzha Line E&M, design, 51 two-car sets, testing, training [6]":
          - cell "Scope"
          - cell "Muzha Line E&M, design, 51 two-car sets, testing, training"
          - cell "[6]":
            - superscript:
              - link "[6]":
                - /url: "#ref-6"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The scope matters more than the number. Taipei did not hire a contractor to electrify a railway; it bought a complete driverless system — vehicles, control, design and testing in one contract
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: ". That single fact decides both halves of this story: it is why the courts eventually read the deal the way they did, and it is why losing the vendor meant losing the means to run the railway."
    - paragraph:
      - text: 黃令名's account of the tender is that it was deliberately written to a 「歐美標準」 — a European-or-American standard rather than a US-only one — which opened it to European bidders, and that VAL was then the most mature automated system on the market
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: . He also records, without endorsing, that the award fed rumours connecting it to arms purchases from France
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: . He reports them as rumours; so does this page.
    - heading "The fires, and the engineering behind them" [level=2]
    - heading "Two fires, and what the builder calls them" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - strong: There were two, four and a half months apart
      - text: ", and the second is recorded as exactly that: 「1993年5月5日：辛亥站前發生火燒車事件」 and 「1993年9月24日：發生"
      - strong: 第二次
      - text: 火燒車事件」
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: . A second vehicle-fire incident. 自由時報 in 2005 said the same from the other end, describing 「接連被兩把大火燒得焦黑的電聯車」 — trains burned black by two successive fires
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: That matters more than the count suggests.
      - strong: One fire during testing is an accident. Two is a pattern
      - text: ", and a pattern is what makes the rest of the year explicable: MOTC halting all work, the Control Yuan impeaching eight officials the following February, and a city council that then spent eight years refusing to let the same technology go north."
    - paragraph:
      - strong: DORTS's own project record does not use the word fire at all.
      - text: It says 「木柵線於82年系統測試階段發生
      - strong: 輪胎起火意外事故
      - text: 」 — during the Muzha Line's system-testing phase in 1993, a
      - strong: tyre ignition accident
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: ". One noun phrase, no date, no count, and it is the most precise wording anyone has used about the mechanism: what burned was a tyre, not a train."
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Which of the two it refers to, the builder does not say.
      - text: It may be either, or it may be the class of event rather than an instance of it. This page does not choose, because there is nothing to choose from.
    - paragraph: So the two vocabularies are kept side by side rather than collapsed. The gap between 輪胎起火 and 火燒車 is roughly the gap between "an overheated tyre ignited" and "the train was on fire", which from a platform look identical — and the more precise phrasing belongs to the organisation that was impeached over it, which is worth seeing at the same time as the other.
    - heading "The mechanism" [level=3]
    - paragraph: There is an actual mechanism here, and it is better than "the French trains kept catching fire".
    - paragraph:
      - text: The trains were designed and run in France as
      - strong: two-car units
      - text: . For Taipei the capacity specification became
      - strong: four cars
      - text: ", and the automatic train control was not redesigned to match — two two-car units were coupled and run on a shared signal path"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: ". When the link between them failed, the units disagreed about what to do next: in 黃令名's reconstruction the lead unit began to move while the trailing unit, having heard nothing, kept its brakes locked"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: ; in 自由時報's, braking seized one axle pair while another drove on — 「煞車咬死，輪胎空轉摩擦過熱起火燃燒」
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The two accounts differ in that detail and agree in everything that matters: a capacity change outran the signalling design, brakes dragged, and on rubber tyres against a concrete running surface, dragging makes heat and heat makes fire"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . On a steel-wheel railway the same failure produces wheel flats and noise. The fires were the tyres' version.
    - paragraph: Two independent tellings, three years apart, is decent corroboration for a causal chain — but neither is an accident investigation, and none has been found. That gap is flagged again at the foot of this page.
    - heading "The recorded incidents" [level=3]
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - text: 5 May 1993
        - strong: First fire
        - text: ", during testing, 辛亥站前 — in front of"
        - link "BR05":
          - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br05/
        - text: Xinhai
        - superscript:
          - link "[5]":
            - /url: "#ref-5"
        - text: ; attributed to 「煞車系統故障及人為疏忽」 — brake failure and human error; Matra apologised publicly on 14 May
        - superscript:
          - link "[6]":
            - /url: "#ref-6"
      - listitem:
        - text: From April 1993 Cracked cap beams found at
        - link "BR07":
          - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br07/
        - text: Liuzhangli,
        - link "BR03":
          - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br03/
        - text: Wanfang Community and elsewhere; investigation and reinforcement demanded.
        - superscript:
          - link "[6]":
            - /url: "#ref-6"
      - listitem:
        - text: 19 June 1993 Testing suspended after further smoke and fire events; in July Matra attributed them to 「晶片問題」 — chip faults.
        - superscript:
          - link "[6]":
            - /url: "#ref-6"
      - listitem:
        - text: 24 September 1993
        - strong: Second fire
        - text: ", recorded as 第二次火燒車事件, between"
        - link "BR07":
          - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br07/
        - text: Liuzhangli and
        - link "BR06":
          - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br06/
        - text: Linguang.
        - superscript:
          - link "[5]":
            - /url: "#ref-5"
        - superscript:
          - link "[2]":
            - /url: "#ref-2"
      - listitem:
        - text: 1 July 1994 Matra stops work, resuming on 23 July.
        - superscript:
          - link "[6]":
            - /url: "#ref-6"
      - listitem:
        - text: 25 August 1994 Final inspections conclude.
        - superscript:
          - link "[6]":
            - /url: "#ref-6"
      - listitem:
        - text: 28 March 1996 The line opens — four and a quarter years after the completion date the contract envisaged.
        - superscript:
          - link "[9]":
            - /url: "#ref-9"
        - superscript:
          - link "[6]":
            - /url: "#ref-6"
    - paragraph:
      - text: Most of this chronology is one encyclopedia entry deep
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: ". The two fires themselves are better anchored: 自由時報 places them in May and September of 1993"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: ", and its 2005 commentary invokes 「接連被兩把大火 燒得焦黑的電聯車，以及將近兩百根暴露著裂縫的捷運支柱」 — two burned trains and nearly two hundred cracked columns"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: Those cracked columns deserve their own sentence. Cap beams are civil works, not Matra's electrical and mechanical scope — they belong to the other contractors on the project
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . The same programme that burned Matra's trains in public was also, more quietly, running late underneath them, and that lateness is what Matra's claim was made of.
    - heading "The arbitration, and seventeen years of litigation" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: From the 自由時報 report of the final judgment
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: "— the best-documented part of the whole affair and the part least often told accurately:"
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - text: Matra's claim 「廿多億元」 — over NT$2 billion, for time added by others' delays
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - listitem:
        - text: Negotiation Collapsed
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - listitem:
        - text: "Arbitration, 6 October 1993 For Matra: awards in NT dollars, US dollars and francs totalling ≈"
        - strong: NT$1.025 billion
        - text: ", plus 5% annual interest"
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - listitem:
        - text: DORTS sues to annul the award Loses; the Supreme Court upholds the award in November 2000
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - listitem:
        - text: "DORTS resists enforcement Argues the claim is time-barred: a works contract carries a short limitation period, expired since 1998."
        - strong: Two courts agree.
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - listitem:
        - text: Supreme Court remands The High Court, rehearing the case, reclassifies the contract as 「買賣、承攬的混合契約」 — a mixed sale-and-works contract — carrying a
        - strong: fifteen-year
        - text: limitation. Matra is in time.
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
      - listitem:
        - text: Supreme Court, 22 July 2005 DORTS's appeal dismissed. Principal plus twelve years' interest ≈
        - strong: NT$1.64 billion.
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: "Sit with the pivot for a moment, because it is the best irony in Taipei's transit history. The city very nearly won: two courts accepted that Matra had simply waited too long. What defeated it was the"
      - emphasis: character of the contract
      - text: — the rehearing found that a deal covering route definition, structural design, and the purchase, installation and testing of vehicles and equipment was not mere contracting but a purchase of a system, with a purchase's fifteen-year limitation
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
      - strong: "Taipei lost the lawsuit for the same reason it had lost control of its railway: it had bought a turnkey system."
      - text: The clause that cost it NT$1.64 billion
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: and the lock-in that cost it its maintainer were the same decision, read twice.
    - paragraph:
      - emphasis: The judgment itself has not been read here — only the reporting of it. The full sequence between 2000 and 2005 involves stages this page has deliberately left undated, because the accounts found disagree on the intermediate chronology and the judgment text would settle it. See the foot of the page.
    - heading "The withdrawal, and the year nobody can pin down" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - strong: That Matra pulled its people out is not in dispute. When, exactly, is.
    - paragraph:
      - text: 〈木柵線〉 says it happened 「在通車兩個月之後」 — two months after the March 1996 opening, so around May 1996
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: . The same encyclopedia's article on the through line says it happened in
      - strong: "1997"
      - text: ", after a contract dispute, when Matra 「將技術人員全數撤離，不再提供維修服務」"
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: . Both readings circulate; this site could not separate them, and no contemporaneous news report of the walkout itself has been found. One reconciliation — staff leaving through 1996, maintenance formally ending in 1997 — is plausible and is exactly the kind of guess this site does not publish as fact.
      - strong: No year is asserted here.
    - paragraph:
      - text: "What the period looked like from inside city hall has, since March 2026, an account from the mayor himself: 陳水扁 describes a fight over spare-parts pricing — Matra quoting NT$10,000 for a patented rubbish bin is his example — and the company using the threat of pulling its technicians as leverage in the renegotiation"
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: . A memoir published on the line's thirtieth anniversary is a primary source with an interest in its own story, and it is cited here as that; but note that it frames the withdrawal not as a sudden exit but as a
      - strong: negotiating instrument that was eventually used
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: 商業周刊 was writing about the relationship under the title 「恩怨情仇」 — grudges and feuds — by 30 May 1996, six weeks after opening
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: ". That article is the closest thing to a contemporaneous account of the collapse; it is paywalled, has not been read past its opening here, and is cited only for what its date and title establish: whatever the formal end date, the marriage was publicly over within weeks of the trains carrying passengers"
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: .
    - heading "Keeping a metro nobody would maintain" [level=2]
    - paragraph: What Taipei was left holding was a driverless system whose builder would not service it — proprietary control software, proprietary parts, and no second source for either.
    - paragraph:
      - text: "黃令名's account — and this is his research speaking, singular and attributed, not a settled record — is that Taiwanese engineers kept the line running by 「偷偷複製法方半成品的列車控制程式、請台廠製造甚至赴光華商場取得 電子零件」: covertly copying the French side's half-finished train control software, commissioning parts from Taiwanese manufacturers, and sourcing electronics at Guanghua Market, Taipei's consumer electronics bazaar"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: . He calls this 「技術能動性」 — technological agency — and it is fair to say his article exists to make that argument
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "陳水扁's retelling corroborates the substance from the client's side, minus the market stalls: replacement components were developed with 中研院, 中科院, 工研院 and private industry until every part had a domestic alternative, cheaper than the originals"
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: . Between a scholar's account of improvisation and a politician's account of mobilisation sits what actually happened; both agree the parts stopped coming from France and the trains kept running.
    - paragraph:
      - text: For the cost of the other road, 黃令名 points at Jacksonville, Florida — a city that faced a comparable dead end with its own Matra system and resolved it by demolition, rebuilding with a Bombardier monorail
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: . Taipei's choice to keep the French railway alive without the French is the road that led, eventually, to this site's
      - link "Wenhu Line":
        - /url: /rail/metro/lines/wenhu-line/
      - text: page describing one seamless operation.
    - heading "The political ledger" [level=2]
    - blockquote:
      - paragraph:
        - text: 「馬特拉不拉，我們自己拉」
        - superscript:
          - link "[2]":
            - /url: "#ref-2"
        - superscript:
          - link "[4]":
            - /url: "#ref-4"
      - paragraph:
        - text: 陳水扁, then Mayor of Taipei —
        - emphasis: if Matra won't pull, we'll pull it ourselves
    - paragraph: The dispute consumed three mayors, one per act.
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - strong: 黃大洲
        - text: presided over the fires. 自由時報's commentary holds that the 木柵線 debacle 「間接導致了當時台北市長黃大洲的敗選下台」 — indirectly cost him the 1994 election
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
        - text: . A newspaper asserting why an election was lost is a genre with a poor record; the timing fits, the claim is widely repeated, and it is published here as the paper's judgment rather than a fact.
      - listitem:
        - strong: 陳水扁
        - text: opened the line on 28 March 1996
        - superscript:
          - link "[6]":
            - /url: "#ref-6"
        - text: and gave the affair the epitaph above. 自由時報 canonises it as his 名言
        - superscript:
          - link "[2]":
            - /url: "#ref-2"
        - text: ; his own account of saying it, thirty years later, has it blurted out mid-crisis in the parts-pricing fight
        - superscript:
          - link "[4]":
            - /url: "#ref-4"
        - text: . The line is quoted everywhere and dated almost nowhere — no contemporaneous record of the moment of utterance has been found, and its setting rests on the speaker's memory.
      - listitem:
        - strong: 馬英九
        - text: was mayor when the final bill arrived in July 2005, and said the city would pay what the judgment required
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
        - text: . The DORTS director, 常岐德, declined all interviews and switched off his phone
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
        - text: ". The commentary's arithmetic was blunter: 「全民買單繳『學費』，足足要花十六億 四千萬元」 — the public pays the tuition, all NT$1.64 billion of it"
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
        - text: .
    - 'heading "What it changed: buying the Neihu extension" [level=2]'
    - paragraph:
      - text: When the line's northern half came to be tendered, DORTS changed the two things that had produced the trap, on 黃令名's analysis of the procurement
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: ":"
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - strong: CBTC was specified
        - text: — communications-based train control, an open signalling approach — rather than an extension of Matra's proprietary fixed-block system
        - superscript:
          - link "[3]":
            - /url: "#ref-3"
        - text: .
      - listitem:
        - strong: Civil works and E&M were let together
        - text: ", as one integrated contract, rather than split across contractors whose mutual delays had just spent seventeen years in court"
        - superscript:
          - link "[3]":
            - /url: "#ref-3"
        - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: By then the incumbent was not even Matra. Siemens had taken control of Matra Transport International in the 1990s — 95% by October 1998
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: — and completed the takeover in November 2001, renaming the business Siemens Transportation Systems
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: . VAL was now a Siemens product, and a tender written around VAL would have had exactly one credible bidder. 黃令名's argument is that the CBTC-plus-turnkey structure existed precisely so that Siemens could not name its price as the only party able to extend the existing system
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: . Procurement rationales are the kind of thing institutions tidy up afterwards, and his is the only account found
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: — but it is consistent with what was actually bought.
    - paragraph:
      - text: What was bought was Bombardier. And here the engineering gets genuinely elegant, because Bombardier could not supply a VAL — VAL belonged to a competitor. So it built the
      - link "Innovia APM 256":
        - /url: /rail/metro/rolling-stock/innovia-apm-256-c370/
      - text: ": a people mover dimensioned to a French railway it had no rights to, matching the running-surface spacing, the side guide bars and the 750 V supply taken off them, with a car body 20 mm narrower than the"
      - link "VAL256":
        - /url: /rail/metro/rolling-stock/val256/
      - text: it would run beside
      - superscript:
        - link "[13]":
          - /url: "#ref-13"
      - text: . The incumbent's guideway became the tender's interface specification.
    - paragraph:
      - text: The last act was the cutover. Rather than run two signalling systems, the whole line switched to Bombardier's CITYFLO 650 on the day the extension opened —
      - strong: 4 July 2009
      - text: — and the 1996 Matra fleet was withdrawn that same day for conversion, returning on 26 December 2010 after eighteen months with its French control system replaced
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: . 黃令名 adds — his account alone; nothing else found says it — that CITYFLO had been tested at night on the Muzha Line's own tracks while the Matra system carried passengers by day
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: . It is a striking detail, it is single-source, and those two properties are related; it is recorded here with its attribution showing.
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The last Matra-controlled train ran thirteen years after Matra stopped maintaining any of them. Nobody from the company was there to see it, and by then there was no company: the name had been gone from the rail business for eight years"
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: .
