    - heading "Overview" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Sanying Line is New
      - link "Taipei":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
      - text: "'s first metro of its own: the operator describes it as the city's first autonomously led medium-capacity system, rather than a line delivered for New Taipei by Taipei's DORTS."
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: It opened on
      - strong: 30 June 2026
      - text: with 12 elevated stations over 14.29 km, linking the Bannan Line at Dingpu to
      - link "Sanxia":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/lb06/
      - text: and
      - link "Yingge":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/lb08/
      - text: and to the TRA main line at Yingge station.
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: That opening followed a feasibility approval on 3 September 2012, comprehensive- planning approval on 2 June 2015, advance works from October 2014, and main works from July 2016.
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: The line completed stability testing on 7 April 2026, preliminary inspection on 26 April, the Ministry of Transportation's final inspection on 7 June and its operating permit on 23 June.
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
    - heading "Route and alignment" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: From LB01 beside the
      - link "Bannan Line":
        - /url: /rail/metro/lines/bannan-line/
      - text: "'s Dingpu terminus, the viaduct follows Zhongyang Road Section 4, crosses Freeway 3 and reaches Jieshou Road in Sanxia. It turns onto the"
      - link "Hengxi":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/lb04/
      - text: riverside road and the new
      - link "Longpu":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/lb05/
      - text: Road approach to the Taipei University district, passing the National Academy for Educational Research before following Sanshu, Guoqing and Fuxing roads.
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The alignment then climbs across Freeway 3 and the Dahan River into Yingge, follows the Yingge River, crosses Wenhua Road and the TRA main line, and bends north past Park No. 3. A second crossing of the main line brings it to Yingtao Road and the LB12 terminus at Fude 1st Road; tail tracks there preserve an interface for the Bade extension.
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
    - paragraph:
      - text: This is not a simple road-median railway. The city's early-works account lists crossings of Freeway 3, the TRA railway, the Dahan, Yingge, Sanxia and Hengxi waterways.
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: "The 2018 engineering report measured 13,452 m of bridge structures: 6,450 m of precast or cast-in-place prestressed U-girder, 2,052 m of prestressed box girder, 4,375 m of steel box girder and 575 m of special arch structures."
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
    - heading "Planning and approvals" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The project moved while its approved programme kept changing. The 2015 plan release said the National Development Council had completed its review, that basic design and project management were already proceeding in parallel, and that a construction access road beside Freeway 3 would let the viaduct works start promptly.
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: The Executive Yuan approved the comprehensive plan that June; a first revised plan was not approved until October 2023, with an end-2025 completion target and project period through 2027.
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The live builder record lists four submissions of a second revised plan between February 2025 and July 2026.
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: It nevertheless records the railway opening in June 2026 while that revision remained under review — a useful distinction between the passenger railway being complete and the wider funded project, including land and close-out work, reaching its administrative end.
    - heading "The rejected underground alternative" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The elevated scheme was contested in
      - link "Tucheng":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/bl03/
      - text: . At an August 2016 public meeting, residents opposed an elevated medium-capacity line on Zhongyang Road and asked for the underground, high-capacity Bannan Line to continue from Dingpu to LB02 , with Sanying beginning there.
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: The road was planned as 30 m wide but some sections then provided only 18–20 m.
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
    - paragraph:
      - text: New Taipei DORTS said the underground station and crossover would still require demolition, place shield tunnels beneath houses, and meet a Dingpu station built without an extension interface.
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: Taipei DORTS additionally identified operating disruption, land acquisition, demolition, poor financial performance and changes to an approved project; New Taipei therefore retained the elevated scheme.
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: Those are the agencies' stated reasons, not an independent comparison of the alternatives.
    - heading "Engineering and construction" [level=2]
    - heading "Ground, foundations and tight curves" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The basic alignment was shaped to limit land acquisition and demolition, which produced a
      - strong: 50 m minimum curve radius
      - text: and a
      - strong: 4.535% maximum gradient
      - text: .
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: The engineering report describes Tucheng largely as the Dahan River's right-bank hills and alluvial plain, then a sequence of river terraces toward Yingge. Mountain sections expose sandstone and shale formations; the newer terraces and alluvium carry gravel, sand and silt over rock, with groundwater commonly 3.4–13.7 m below ground.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The designers preferred well foundations where ground and groundwater allowed, especially on 18–20 m roads where a smaller work area reduced traffic impact.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: Pile foundations were retained for difficult dewatering or conflicts with major buried utilities.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: The report's comparison put a typical well foundation at about 20 m² and 21 days against about 57 m² and 30 days for a pile-cap alternative; those are design comparisons, not whole-project averages.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
    - heading "Bridges, BIM and the single design-build contract" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: For ordinary spans under 35 m the project made the prestressed U-girder its default.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: Its low structural depth, continuous appearance and ability to carry a 90-degree curve were the stated reasons; the technical report expected roughly 800 m of U-girder erection work.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: At the Sanxia River the metro bridge was planned parallel to two road bridges with a 6 m clear gap and a 180 m arch span. Across the Dahan River the report shows a 520 m crossing with a 100 m deep-channel zone and a flying-bird arch concept.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The civil, water-and-environmental, railway systems and track works were procured together as one large design-build contract using a best-value award.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: The report says 22 firms returned 502 comments in the first consultation, ten returned 235 in the second, and 17 returned 431 during public review before three teams ultimately tendered.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: The city also combined a three-dimensional terrain model with BIM to simulate stations, bridges, construction space and later operations — its first such metro application in New Taipei.
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
    - heading "Stations and interchanges" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: All 12 passenger stations are elevated.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: LB01 connects with the Bannan Line at Dingpu, while LB08 connects the metro with TRA Yingge station; the opening notice presents those two transfers as the route into the Taipei metro network and the conventional railway.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The technical report's design-stage station programme used two standard forms. Road-median stations were about 58 m long and 21 m wide, while constrained sites used a side-platform form intended to reduce the bulk over the road.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: It also required station entrances to include level-access or lift provision and parking for motorcycles and bicycles.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
    - paragraph:
      - text: Public art was planned as a line-wide system rather than a late collection of objects. By July 2026 the bureau described three themed trains — Hakka, New Taipei City Art Museum and Indigenous — alongside station works tied to local culture.
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: The Indigenous train uses Amis clothing and weaving motifs, an Amis
      - emphasis: "'alofo"
      - text: bag, and Atayal and Paiwan characters; the bureau says these trains are dispatched randomly rather than to a published timetable.
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
    - heading "Rolling stock" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Hitachi Rail designed the steel-wheel, steel-rail trains and they were manufactured in Japan.
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: The fleet is
      - strong: 29 two-car trains
      - text: ", not 29 cars. Each aluminium train is 35 m long, 2.6 m wide and 3.8 m high, carries 330 people — 50 seated and 280 standing — and uses electric and hydraulic braking."
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The operator publishes an
      - strong: 80 km/h maximum operating speed
      - text: ", 750 V DC third- rail supply and communications-based train control."
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: The 2018 functional specification required CBTC, a system headway of 90 seconds or less and GoA 4 unattended operation, but specified a design maximum speed of at least 70 km/h.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: "Those figures describe different things: the earlier minimum performance requirement and the delivered fleet's maximum operating speed."
    - heading "Operations" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Opening service was advertised at roughly six-minute peak and eight-minute off- peak headways, with about 30 minutes end to end.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: "The free-trial period ran through 31 August 2026: stored-value-card users tapping in and out paid nothing."
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: Hours began at 10:00–20:00, expanded to 08:00–22:00 from 1 August and to 06:00–24:00 from 16 August.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The published normal fare band is NT$20–35 by distance, but the operator says the actual charging date will be announced separately.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: Ending the free trial therefore does not, by itself, establish when fares began.
    - paragraph:
      - text: By 25 July the bureau counted more than
      - strong: 750,000 journeys
      - text: ", an average of 53,000 on holidays, and 72,000 station exits on 4 July during the museum's fireworks and light show."
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: For that event it says trains ran at a 2.2-minute interval.
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: That demonstrated a special-event service, not the normal opening headway and not proof that the full line can sustain the 2018 design-stage 2.2-minute pattern in every operating condition.
    - heading "Bade extension" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The approved extension continues 4.03 km from LB12 with three stations and a published budget of NT$16.058 billion.
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - code: LB12a
      - text: and
      - code: LB13
      - text: are planned elevated; the line then descends beneath the south side of Danan Forest Park to underground
      - code: LB14
      - text: ", built together with"
      - link "Taoyuan Green Line":
        - /url: /rail/tymc/lines/green-line/
      - text: station
      - code: G04
      - text: .
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The builder records feasibility approval on 13 November 2019, environmental- assessment acceptance on 2 November 2023 and Executive Yuan approval of the comprehensive plan on
      - strong: 1 August 2025
      - text: .
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: Its header gives an expected completion in
      - strong: "2034"
      - text: .
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: The same live page still labels the introductory alignment 「本計畫尚未核定」 — “the project remains unapproved.”
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: That sentence conflicts with the approval timeline on the page and is published here as stale official copy, not silently resolved.
    - heading "Where the sources disagree" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Project cost.
      - text: Three official values survive. The October 2014 early-works release gave
      - strong: NT$55.022 billion
      - text: .
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: The April 2015 NDC-stage release and August 2018 engineering report gave
      - strong: NT$50.5 billion
      - text: ; the report says value engineering used shorter trains, tighter headways, shorter stations, well foundations and U-girders to reduce the earlier NT$55 billion proposal.
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: The live builder page now gives
      - strong: NT$50.200 billion
      - text: .
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: These are dated project estimates or current programme figures, not interchangeable measurements of final expenditure.
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Journey and peak interval.
      - text: In 2014 the city forecast an end-to-end journey of no more than
      - strong: 23 minutes
      - text: and a
      - strong: three-minute
      - text: peak interval.
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: Opening service was about
      - strong: 30 minutes
      - text: and
      - strong: six minutes
      - text: .
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: The engineering report's mature design pattern put LB01 – LB08 at 2.2 minutes but LB08 – LB12 at 4.4 minutes.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: The sources describe an early forecast, initial operations and a design-year branching pattern respectively; none is substituted for another.
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Bade approval.
      - text: The extension page's dated record says the Executive Yuan approved the comprehensive plan on 1 August 2025, while its introduction says the project has not been approved.
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: The page gives no update date for the stale sentence, so its provenance cannot be reconstructed.

    - heading "Overview" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: At 07:58 on 3 April 2024 a magnitude 7.2 earthquake off Shoufeng in Hualien County destroyed the pot bearings between the steel box girders and the piers on the Circular Line's viaduct through
      - link "Zhonghe":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/y12/
      - text: and along
      - link "Jingping":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/y10/
      - text: Road, shoving eleven girders out of position, deforming the track, damaging 139 items of equipment, and closing the railway between Banqiao and Zhonghe
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . No train was on the damaged section when it happened
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: Eight months later the line reopened. Between those two dates the Control Yuan — Taiwan's audit and censure branch — opened an investigation on its own motion, and its report, case 114交調0005, reviewed on 11 March 2025 and published on 17 June 2025 by commissioners 趙永清 and 葉宜津, is the fullest published account of what happened and why
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . It is the source for most of this page.
    - heading "Incident investigation and engineering findings" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Read the report carefully and the first thing to notice is what is
      - emphasis: not
      - text: a finding
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . Its terms of reference recite the allegation it was asked to look at — eleven suspected displacements, a repair initially costed at over NT$400 million, at least a year to fix
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . Those are the reported claims the Control Yuan set out to test, not its conclusions, and they are quoted here as such.
    - heading "The mechanism" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The report's first finding is a construction fault, stated without hedging: the contractor, BES Engineering (中華工程),"
      - strong: did not build to the drawings
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . It milled through the grade-adjustment plate (調坡板) that sits between the girder and the bearing, leaving void space above the locating pin; under the earthquake the pin jumped upward into that void, its base left the interface between the upper and lower plates of the pot bearing, and it lost its ability to resist shear
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The numbers behind that sentence are the heart of the case
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: ":"
    - table:
      - rowgroup:
        - row "Dimension Depth":
          - columnheader "Dimension"
          - columnheader "Depth"
      - rowgroup:
        - row "Milled recess, as shown on the contractor's own shop drawing 5 mm[1]":
          - cell "Milled recess, as shown on the contractor's own shop drawing"
          - cell "5 mm[1]":
            - text: 5 mm
            - superscript:
              - link "[1]":
                - /url: "#ref-1"
        - row "Milled recess, as measured on site by the investigation 41 mm[1]":
          - cell "Milled recess, as measured on site by the investigation"
          - cell "41 mm[1]":
            - text: 41 mm
            - superscript:
              - link "[1]":
                - /url: "#ref-1"
        - row "Void left above the pin 36 mm[1]":
          - cell "Void left above the pin"
          - cell "36 mm[1]":
            - text: 36 mm
            - superscript:
              - link "[1]":
                - /url: "#ref-1"
        - row "Height of the pin itself 40 mm[1]":
          - cell "Height of the pin itself"
          - cell "40 mm[1]":
            - text: 40 mm
            - superscript:
              - link "[1]":
                - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: 36 mm of void plus the 5 mm of engagement the drawing required is 41 mm — the report's own arithmetic — and 41 mm is more than enough to swallow a pin only 40 mm tall
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . The pins were found by the New
      - link "Taipei":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
      - text: City Civil Engineers Association, which jacked the damaged bridges up and discovered them lodged in the upper plate of the bearing or lying on the pier cap where they had fallen
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The section was built under contract CF651B, part of the CF650 section works, and the structures carried a warranty running to 12 March 2026
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: — which is why the timing of the claim against the contractor matters.
    - heading "The shaking was smaller than the design case" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: This is the part most likely to be misread. The viaducts were designed to the Ministry of Transportation and Communications' 2006 railway bridge seismic design code, at a Taipei basin design ground motion of 0.24 g, with an importance factor of 1.2 because metro bridges are classed as important structures — so the minimum design seismic force is 0.288 g, which on the Central Weather Administration's 2020 intensity scale falls in the 6-weak band
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . The "designed for 6-weak" formulation is the report's own arithmetic on 0.24 g × 1.2 followed by a lookup on the 2020 scale, not a design document that says 6-weak
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: What the instruments recorded near the damaged bridges was smaller
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: ":"
    - table:
      - rowgroup:
        - row "Station North–south peak ground acceleration":
          - columnheader "Station"
          - columnheader "North–south peak ground acceleration"
      - rowgroup:
        - row "TAP026, 頂溪國小 224.60 gal[1]":
          - cell "TAP026, 頂溪國小"
          - cell "224.60 gal[1]":
            - text: 224.60 gal
            - superscript:
              - link "[1]":
                - /url: "#ref-1"
        - row "TAP032, 積穗國小 206.77 gal[1]":
          - cell "TAP032, 積穗國小"
          - cell "206.77 gal[1]":
            - text: 206.77 gal
            - superscript:
              - link "[1]":
                - /url: "#ref-1"
        - row "TAP115, 安和國小 223.17 gal[1]":
          - cell "TAP115, 安和國小"
          - cell "223.17 gal[1]":
            - text: 223.17 gal
            - superscript:
              - link "[1]":
                - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: At 積穗國小 the peak ground velocity reached 32.16 cm/s, an intensity of 5-strong, and the peak horizontal acceleration measured there was 0.229 g — below the 0.288 g of the 475-year return-period design earthquake
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: ". New Taipei DORTS said the same thing three weeks after the earthquake: intensity 5-strong at the nearest recording station"
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The comparison the report itself draws is between seismic microzones rather than between metro lines. The adjacent zones — the DF111 contract range covering Wenshan and
      - link "Xindian":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/g01/
      - text: ", and the DF113 range covering"
      - link "Sanchong":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/o15/
      - text: ","
      - link "Xinzhuang":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/o18/
      - text: and Banqiao — recorded far lower ground motion in the same earthquake and suffered
      - strong: no bridge damage at all
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . In the DF112 range covering Zhonghe and Yonghe, horizontal peak ground acceleration was around twice its neighbours' and horizontal peak ground velocity around fifteen times
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "Which produces the single most quotable line in the document: 「也就是說，輸入比 規範要求小20%的地震，卻得到比預期大50%的力量，顯示出反應譜分析不能反映當地地震反應 的實況」 — an input earthquake 20% smaller than the code requires produced forces 50% larger than expected, showing that response-spectrum analysis does not reflect the local seismic response"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - heading "The design, and what nobody checked" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The report's second finding is against the design. The structure is described in it as
      - strong: Taiwan's first stacked viaduct
      - text: — 國內史無前例的疊式高架橋 — carried on branching piers through climbing and descending sections, and the finding is that no higher design standard was adopted and no displacement-limiting devices were added to provide a further line of defence, and that this unprecedented structural form went through
      - strong: no external structural review
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "Note the word: viaduct, not station. Nothing found in the research behind this page describes stacked"
      - emphasis: stations
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The structural engineers' report the investigation relied on sets out the hierarchy plainly: displacement-limiting devices assist the bearings and resist seismic force, and fall-prevention equipment or sufficient seat length prevents the span dropping — the second and third lines of defence respectively for a bridge bearing system in an earthquake"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . The line was built with neither of the two backups.
    - paragraph:
      - text: Three further design failures are recorded
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: ":"
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - text: The detailed design consultant, CECI (世曦),
        - strong: double-deducted dead load
        - text: when calculating the bearings' uplift design force, and so underestimated the required uplift resistance
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
        - text: .
      - listitem:
        - text: The pot-bearing detail drawing
        - strong: contradicts itself about the pins
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
        - text: . Note 1 in its lower-left corner gives every pin a height of 40 mm with diameters of 120, 140, 150, 160, 200, 210, 220 and 280 mm; the table on the same drawing gives every pin a diameter of 100 mm with heights of 15, 20 and 25 mm; and neither set matches the pins actually found in the damaged bearings
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
        - text: . The report's own word for this is 令人費解 — baffling.
      - listitem:
        - strong: Nobody senior signed that drawing
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
        - text: . Only the handling officer at Taipei DORTS's third civil works office stamped it; neither the design unit responsible for reviewing it nor DORTS as the approving authority signed at all, which the report finds is a failure to carry out the review and approval the contract's specification chapter on pot bearings required
        - superscript:
          - link "[1]":
            - /url: "#ref-1"
        - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: 888 pot bearings were supplied to the works in total, sampled in six batches against the production schedule and tested at National Taiwan University of Science and Technology's structural mechanics laboratory
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - heading "The plate that nobody in Taiwan inspects" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The third finding is the one most easily missed, and it is the reason the fault survived construction. The grade-adjustment plate is a secondary component between the girder and the bearing; it is designed by the contractor, assembled in the fabrication shop, and concealed once the girder is lifted into place — so it was
      - strong: not an inspection hold point
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The investigation then checked whether it is one anywhere else, and found that it is not: not on the Directorate General of Highways' viaducts, not on the Hualien–Taitung railway works, not on the Tamkang Bridge, not on the"
      - link "Ankeng LRT":
        - /url: /rail/metro/lines/ankeng-lrt/
      - text: ", not on the"
      - link "Sanying Line":
        - /url: /rail/metro/lines/sanying-line/
      - text: ", not on the"
      - link "Taichung":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taichung/
      - text: Metro, not on the Wenhu Line, not on the second phase of the Wanda Line, and not in the Public Construction Commission's inspection checkpoints for steel bridge erection
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . Taipei DORTS's remedy, dated 13 December 2024 — the day after the line reopened — was to add a pot-bearing inspection flow chart and a sampling standard
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - heading "The seismometer that was told not to report" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The fourth finding concerns an instrument that was installed, worked, and was disconnected from anyone who could act on it.
      - link "Zhongyuan":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/y14/
      - text: station has triaxial accelerometer-type seismometers at both ends of its platform level
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . On 28 August 2019 Taipei DORTS's electrical and mechanical systems engineering office wrote to
      - link "Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation":
        - /url: /rail/operators/trtc/
      - text: that the seismometer detection signals need not be relayed to the control centre — and from the line's opening in 2020 to the date of the report, the Circular Line control centre held
      - strong: no seismic record from that instrument at all
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The 2019 letter identifies the instruments by the codes
      - code: Y9
      - text: and
      - code: Y13
      - text: ", which are not the codes the stations at those positions carry today; the two numbering schemes remain unreconciled, and the station the report names is Zhongyuan"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The report also states as fact that when Taipei City Government handed operations to New Taipei City Government on 23 May 2023,
      - link "New Taipei Metro":
        - /url: /rail/operators/ntmc/
      - text: took the equipment as it stood, and received training on the anemometer only — nothing on the seismic instrumentation
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - heading "The code itself" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The sixth finding is against the ministry. Through years of revision, including the substantially updated 2021 edition of the railway bridge seismic design code, MOTC has never addressed
      - strong: transverse
      - text: "displacement: the rules still deal only with the longitudinal, running direction"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . The line failed sideways.
    - heading "Who was actually corrected" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: This is worth stating precisely, because the operator of the line and the builder of it are different cities and the two are easily transposed. The formal 糾正 — a correction, the Control Yuan's censure of an agency — was proposed against
      - strong: Taipei City Government
      - text: ", on findings one and three: the construction fault and the supervision gap"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . Taipei DORTS built the line and supervised its own construction
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: New Taipei City Government and MOTC received 函請檢討改進 — a request to review and improve, and report back — not a correction
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . Findings two and four went to Taipei City for review, finding four also to New Taipei City, and findings five and six to MOTC
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - heading "Incident and recovery timeline" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - strong: 3 April 2024.
      - text: The whole line was suspended
      - superscript:
        - link "[13]":
          - /url: "#ref-13"
      - text: . The
      - link "Danhai LRT":
        - /url: /rail/metro/lines/danhai-lrt/
      - text: was unaffected and the Ankeng LRT was back to normal by 16:30 on a 15-minute headway
      - superscript:
        - link "[13]":
          - /url: "#ref-13"
      - text: . From 17:00 the Circular Line ran
      - strong:
        - text: single-track bidirectional between Banqiao and
        - link "New Taipei Industrial Park":
          - /url: /rail/metro/stations/y20/
      - text: on a 16-minute headway, and free shuttle buses ran between New Taipei Industrial Park and Dapinglin from 06:00 to 24:00 — every 10 to 15 minutes at peak, 20 to 30 off-peak — calling at every Circular Line station except Shisizhang, which was served instead from the 新店民權路工業區 bus stop
      - superscript:
        - link "[13]":
          - /url: "#ref-13"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - strong: 24 April 2024.
      - text: "New Taipei DORTS published the severity split: of the eleven girder displacements,"
      - strong: seven were severe, between 20 and 92 cm
      - text: ", and four were between 3.5 and 6 cm"
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: . Recovery was initially assessed at over a year
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: . The largest single displacement, 92 cm, is the figure the Control Yuan also carries, attributed to New Taipei DORTS's briefing
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - strong: 12 December 2024, 12:00.
      - text: Full service resumed
      - superscript:
        - link "[14]":
          - /url: "#ref-14"
      - text: ". The repair inventory the operator published: nine spans of steel box girder repositioned, 139 items damaged, 1,438 track baseplates replaced, 1,050 m of track restored, 41,500 m of cable replaced, and headways back to 5–7 minutes at peak and 8–10 off-peak"
      - superscript:
        - link "[14]":
          - /url: "#ref-14"
      - text: . The bearings were replaced wholesale with optimised pot bearings, and permanent fall-prevention and anti-uplift devices were added as a second line of defence — the protection the design had lacked
      - superscript:
        - link "[14]":
          - /url: "#ref-14"
      - text: . The published repair inventory gives no count of bearings replaced
      - superscript:
        - link "[14]":
          - /url: "#ref-14"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The Control Yuan's own summary of the repair: 250 days of emergency work against an original estimate of one year and two months, finished six months early, with 123 hours of total testing before service resumed — whole-line and section tests, and ten simulation drills"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - heading "Engineering responsibility and dispute" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: On 3 January 2025 New Taipei City Government announced that the two city governments would jointly sue BES Engineering for
      - strong: NT$1.927 billion
      - text: ", on the basis that the contractor had not built to the approved drawings; the same release carries the 40 mm pin, the 5 mm drawing and the 41 mm as-built account of the mechanism"
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: . The suit was filed on 27 March 2025 at the Taipei District Court
      - superscript:

      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: BES has not conceded. It says it 「均依核定施工圖說嚴格執行」 — that it strictly executed the approved construction drawings — and that the milled-through plate and the bearing failure are

      - text: the main cause of the damage, which it says needs further examination from the direction of structural design strength
      - superscript:

        - text: .

    - heading "Route and alignment" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Circular Line is a
      - strong: steel-wheel, steel-rail, fully automatic driverless medium-capacity system
      - text: — not straddle-beam and not rubber-tyred
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . The section in service is 15.4 km with 14 stations, thirteen elevated and one underground, and one depot
      - superscript:

          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . It opened on 31 January 2020
      - superscript:

      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The second revised plan for Phase 1 was approved by the Executive Yuan on 6 May 2015 at a total cost of
      - strong: NT$69.973 billion
      - text: ", against an initial financial plan of NT$40.118 billion"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":

      - text: — an increase of roughly 74%, which is arithmetic on those two published figures rather than a figure DORTS states. New Taipei DORTS publishes the same total
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: .

      - strong: South Depot

      - link "南機廠":

      - text: "), in the Shisizhang agricultural zone in Xindian: about 14.33 hectares of site, of which about 12.19 hectares are laid out as depot"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The trains were built by
      - strong: Hitachi Rail Italy
      - superscript:

      - text: ". The bureau published an article specifically to explain why the winning bidder was reported as AnsaldoBreda and the trains arrived branded Hitachi: Hitachi bought AnsaldoBreda in 2015 and renamed it"
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: . That article gives no fleet size, formation or technical specification, and none is asserted here.

      - paragraph: 13 of 16 sources on this page are primary — published by the operator, the builder or government.
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - 'link "Control Yuan investigation report, case 114交調0005: the displacement of Circular Line track following the 3 April 2024 earthquake"':
            - /url: https://www.cy.gov.tw/CyBsBoxContent.aspx?s=49082
          - text: 監察院調查報告 114交調0005 primary 監察院 (Control Yuan of the Republic of China) accessed 2026-08-23 The single most important document on this subject, and the source for everything on this page attributed to the investigation. Commissioners 趙永清 and 葉宜津, on their own motion; reviewed 11 March 2025, published 17 June 2025. Read here from the report's .docx (https://cybsbox.cy.gov.tw/CYBSBoxSSL/edoc/download/68978), whose word/document.xml was extracted directly — about 15,800 characters of body text, the whole report minus figures and tables. A .pdf of the same report is at https://cybsbox.cy.gov.tw/CYBSBoxSSL/edoc/download/72631 and could not be rendered in the environment used. Note that the report's 案由 recites the allegation being investigated — eleven displacements, NT$400m+, over a year — and is not the same thing as its findings.
        - listitem:
          - link "What is the route and the system type of the whole Circular Line?":
            - /url: https://www.dorts.gov.taipei/News_Content.aspx?n=2A66A485FACB0D5B&sms=87415A8B9CE81B16&s=5283528B7AF0EECA
          - text: "常見問答－機電設施＞環狀線全線之路線與型式為何? primary 臺北市政府捷運工程局 (Taipei City Government, Department of Rapid Transit Systems) accessed 2026-08-23 The builder's own whole-line answer, and the only page found in this research that gives all four sections' dimensions together: 環狀線係採鋼軌鋼輪全自動無人駕駛中運量系統; 共15.4公里，14車站(地下1站，高架13站) 及1座機廠; 北環段：共14.93公里，12車站及1座地下機廠; 南環段：共5.73公里，6車站（地下6站，不包括大坪林站）; 東環段：約13.25公里，10車站及1座地下機廠（地下10站）. It states no whole-ring total. Fetched twice, the second time asking only for verbatim sentences containing 公里, because a first fetch had produced a total that the second could not find."
        - listitem:
          - link "Circular Line Phase 1":
            - /url: https://www.dorts.gov.taipei/cp.aspx?n=86E55BE3A390F789
          - text: "環狀線第一階段 primary 臺北市政府捷運工程局 (Taipei City Government, Department of Rapid Transit Systems) accessed 2026-08-23 The builder's project record for the section now open: 於109年1月31日通車營運; 第2次修正計畫於104年5月6日奉行政院核定，總經費699.73億元 against an initial financial plan of 401.18億元; and the depot, 南機廠位於新店十四張農業區，面積約14.33公頃，供佈設機廠之面積約12.19公頃. The depot's published name is 南機廠, South Depot; 十四張 is where it is, not what it is called."
        - listitem:
          - link "The New Taipei Circular Line":
            - /url: https://www.dorts.ntpc.gov.tw/about/route/zj6Dd5ajdA1o
          - text: 新北環狀線 primary 新北市政府捷運工程局 (New Taipei City Government, Department of Rapid Transit Systems) accessed 2026-08-23 The other bureau's page for the same railway, cited here because it independently repeats Taipei DORTS's figures — 15.4 公里, 14 座車站, 中運量, 109年1月31日全線通車營運, 699.73億元, one depot in the 新店十四張 agricultural zone. Two bureaux publishing the same numbers is what makes the 15.4 km figure solid enough to set beside the chainage.
        - listitem:
          - link "Circular Line — South Ring and North Ring":
            - /url: https://www.dorts.ntpc.gov.tw/about/route/bQw92Vzy2jOk
          - text: "環狀線(南環段/北環段) primary 新北市政府捷運工程局 (New Taipei City Government, Department of Rapid Transit Systems) accessed 2026-08-23 The under-construction rings, from the bureau building them: 路線全長20.66公里(其中新北市轄內8.21公里), 18 stations of which 7 are inside New Taipei, 1798.98億元, 預計120年完工. Also the section-contract start dates quoted on this page. Its 20.66 km equals the 5.73 + 14.93 of Taipei DORTS's two section figures exactly, which is a cross-check between two bureaux rather than a coincidence."
        - listitem:
          - link "Circular Line East Ring":
            - /url: https://www.dorts.gov.taipei/cp.aspx?n=F47E41B6C8884DC6
          - text: "環狀線東環段 primary 臺北市政府捷運工程局 (Taipei City Government, Department of Rapid Transit Systems) accessed 2026-08-23 The East Ring project page: 約13.25公里, 10 stations all underground, one underground depot, basic design completed 110年10月18日 and approved 112年3月29日. It carries no cost figure and no completion year, which is why neither appears on this page. A DORTS press release that would have settled both returned HTTP 404 on 2026-08-10."
        - listitem:
          - link "Taiwan MOTC TDX — Line, Route, StationOfRoute and Shape, operator NTMC":
            - /url: https://tdx.transportdata.tw/
          - text: "primary Ministry of Transportation and Communications, Taiwan accessed 2026-08-05 Government open data, committed to this repository at data/tdx/NTMC/. Source for the station sequence and codes, the 34-minute end-to-end run time, the transfer times, and the 15.06 km cumulative chainage from Y07 to Y20 . The RouteLength field is 0 — present and unpopulated — which is the same behaviour this site found on every TRTC metro route. line.json records IsBranch: false, and the fourteen stations run in one unbranched sequence, so the nineteen segments of the published geometry are an artefact of how the alignment is drawn rather than a statement about the railway."
        - listitem:
          - 'link "The Hitachi that came from Italy: unravelling the parentage of the New Taipei Circular Line''s trains"':
            - /url: https://www.dorts.ntpc.gov.tw/documentary/articleInfo/pW0dxgqY23Ex
          - text: "來自義大利的日立：解開新北環狀線列車身世之謎 primary 新北市政府捷運工程局 (New Taipei City Government, Department of Rapid Transit Systems) accessed 2026-08-10 Written to explain why the winning bidder was reported as 安薩爾多 and the trains arrived branded 日立軌道義大利: Hitachi bought AnsaldoBreda in 2015 and renamed it Hitachi Rail Italy. Cited for that identity chain and nothing else — it gives no fleet size, no formation and no technical specification, which is why those rows are TBC."
        - listitem:
          - 'link "Displacement investigation report published: contractor did not build to the approved drawings; the two city governments will jointly sue BES Engineering for NT$1.927 billion"':
            - /url: https://www.ntpc.gov.tw/ch/home.jsp?id=e8ca970cde5c00e1&dataserno=9be8e636a516475bafac1bcac788d423
          - text: 環狀線位移鑑定報告出爐!廠商未按核定施工圖施作 雙北市府將一同向中華工程提告 求償19.27億 primary 新北市政府 (New Taipei City Government), 3 January 2025 accessed 2026-08-10 The city's own announcement of the claim total and of the 40 mm / 5 mm / 41 mm account of the pin and the milled plate. A three-way breakdown of the NT$1.927 billion circulates in search summaries and secondary reporting; a full fetch of this page on 2026-08-10 returned the total and no breakdown, so no breakdown is published here.
        - listitem:
          - link "Circular Line earthquake damage — the two city governments sue BES Engineering for NT$1.927 billion":
            - /url: https://www.cna.com.tw/news/aloc/202503270341.aspx
          - text: 捷運環狀線震損 雙北市府提告中華工程求償19.27億 secondary 中央社 CNA, 27 March 2025 accessed 2026-08-10 Cited for the fact and date of the filing — 27 March 2025, at the Taipei District Court, against 中華工程 — which no primary document read in this research records. It also reports nine displaced spans, which is the count the repair records use and not the eleven the investigation uses; both are on this page.
        - listitem:
          - link "Sued for NT$1.9 billion over the Circular Line earthquake damage, BES Engineering says it built to the drawings":
            - /url: https://news.pts.org.tw/article/732085
          - text: "捷運環狀線震損遭求償19億 中華工程：均按圖施工 secondary 公視新聞網 PTS accessed 2026-08-10 The contractor's own position, quoted: 均依核定施工圖說嚴格執行, and 調坡板銑穿與支承失效，並非災損主因，相關原因需從結構設計強度等因素進一步檢討. Secondary, because it is a news outlet reporting what the company said — but it is the only account found of the defendant's case, and the defendant has not conceded."
        - listitem:
          - link "Eleven locations severely damaged on the Circular Line; recovery initially estimated at over a year":
            - /url: https://www.dorts.ntpc.gov.tw/news/indexInfo/1AldprRBmLK7
          - text: "環狀線11處受損嚴重 初估復原工期超過1年 primary 新北市政府捷運工程局 (New Taipei City Government, Department of Rapid Transit Systems), 24 April 2024 accessed 2026-08-10 Three weeks after the earthquake, and the only source found for the severity split: of the eleven displacements, seven severe at 20–92 cm and four at 3.5–6 cm. Also the initial estimate of 復原工作初步評估須約1年以上 and the intensity 5-strong recorded at the station nearest the damage. The Control Yuan report gives neither the split nor this estimate as its own."
        - listitem:
          - link "New Taipei's two light rail lines back to normal; the Circular Line runs single-track bidirectional over part of its route":
            - /url: https://www.ntmetro.com.tw/basic/?mode=detail&node=719
          - text: "新北捷運兩線輕軌恢復正常營運 環狀線採部份區段單線雙向營運 primary 新北大眾捷運股份有限公司 (New Taipei Metro Corporation), 3 April 2024 accessed 2026-08-10 The operator's own account of the day itself: the whole line suspended, the Danhai LRT unaffected, the Ankeng LRT back to normal at 16:30 on a 15-minute headway, single-track bidirectional working from 17:00 between Banqiao and New Taipei Industrial Park at 16-minute headway, and the free shuttle bus arrangement including the one station it could not serve directly."
        - listitem:
          - 'link "The New Taipei Circular Line is ready: safety confirmed, full service resumes at 12:00"':
            - /url: https://www.ntmetro.com.tw/basic/?mode=detail&node=754
          - text: "新北環狀線準備好了!確認安全無虞12:00 全線復駛 primary 新北大眾捷運股份有限公司 (New Taipei Metro Corporation), 12 December 2024 accessed 2026-08-23 The reopening, with the repair inventory: nine spans of steel box girder repositioned, 139 items damaged, 1,438 track baseplates replaced, 1,050 m of track restored, 41,500 m of cable replaced, headways back to 5–7 min peak and 8–10 off-peak. Also 李政安 on the remedy — 除了全面更換為優化的盤式支承設施外、也增設永久防落橋及抗拉拔裝置為第二道防線 — which replaces the bearings wholesale without stating how many."
        - listitem:
          - link "New Taipei Metro's 2025 ridership passes 30 million — an all-time high":
            - /url: https://www.ntmetro.com.tw/basic/?mode=detail&node=843
          - text: 新北捷運2025全年運量突破3,000萬人次！ 創歷史新高 primary 新北大眾捷運股份有限公司 (New Taipei Metro Corporation) accessed 2026-08-23 環狀線發揮強大路網轉乘效益，全年服務超過2,204萬人次; 2025年全年度總運量正式突破3,009萬人次大關; 相較於2024年全年的2,135萬人次，整體成長幅度超過40%.     - heading "Overview" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The Songshan–Xindian Line is a single operating railway assembled from three construction projects: the"
      - link "Xindian Line":
        - /url: /rail/history/xindian-line/
      - text: ", the"
      - link "Xiaonanmen":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/g11/
      - text: Line and the
      - link "Songshan":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/g19/
      - text: Line. DORTS records their different approval, construction and opening dates, while the 15 November 2014 Songshan opening created the continuous Songshan–Xindian service seen on the map today.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[20]":
          - /url: "#ref-20"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The main line is underground from Songshan to
      - link "Xindian":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/g01/
      - text: . Its short
      - link "Xiaobitan":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/g03a/
      - text: branch diverges at
      - link "Qizhang":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/g03/
      - text: ", changes from underground to grade and then rises to an elevated platform inside"
      - link "Xindian Depot":
        - /url: /rail/metro/depots/xindian-depot/
      - text: ; dedicated three-car trains serve that platform.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: The current TDX route data lists G01 through G19 on the main route and G03A on the branch, twenty stations in the operating sequence.
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
    - paragraph
    - figure "Xindian Station, the line's southern terminus, at the foot of the hills. Foxy1219, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons":
      - img "The green-signed main entrance to Xindian Station, at the foot of forested hills"
      - text: Xindian Station, the line's southern terminus, at the foot of the hills. Foxy1219, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons
    - paragraph
    - heading "Route and alignment" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Xindian project runs south from
      - link "NTU Hospital":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/r09/
      - text: through Guting and CKS Memorial Hall to Xindian. DORTS describes an approximately 10.5 km project with eleven stations, but explicitly says NTU Hospital operates as part of the
      - link "Tamsui–Xinyi Line":
        - /url: /rail/metro/lines/tamsui-xinyi-line/
      - text: ; the physical project and the present green-line service therefore have different northern boundaries.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The 1.6 km Xiaonanmen project links Ximen to CKS Memorial Hall.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: It was designed and built with the Nangang project to provide
      - link "Bannan Line":
        - /url: /rail/metro/lines/bannan-line/
      - text: trains access to maintenance facilities, then became part of Songshan–Xindian passenger service when the Songshan section opened.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Songshan project runs from Ximen through
      - link "Beimen":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/g13/
      - text: ", Zhongshan, Songjiang Nanjing, Nanjing Fuxing,"
      - link "Taipei Arena":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/g17/
      - text: and
      - link "Nanjing Sanmin":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/g18/
      - text: to Songshan. DORTS's project page calls it approximately 8.5 km, eight underground stations including Ximen, and fully underground; the 2014 technical article uses the earlier working labels G13 , G14 , G16 , G17 , G18 , G19 ,
      - code: G21
      - text: and
      - code: G22
      - text: for that same sequence.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
    - heading "Planning and approvals" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The first 70.3 km
      - link "Taipei":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
      - text: rapid-transit network, including the future Xindian corridor, received Executive Yuan approval on 4 April 1986.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: The approved form was partly elevated and partly underground; DORTS attributes the later change to narrow streets and the environmental and visual impact of elevated structures, and records Executive Yuan agreement to an entirely underground line on 20 May 1987.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Songshan planning record traces a 1993 network review, a 1994 corridor report, route-plan approval in 1997, financial-plan approval in 2004, civil construction beginning in 2006 and opening in 2014.
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: The DORTS project page gives the more precise approval date of 21 November 1997, the financial approval date of 2 December 2004 and the first civil contract signing on 29 March 2006.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
    - paragraph:
      - text: Xindian construction began at NTU Hospital on 1 March 1991.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: The northern section to Guting opened on 24 December 1998; Guting to Xindian opened on 11 November 1999.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: The Xiaobitan branch received Executive Yuan approval on 17 September 1999, and the Xiaonanmen project opened on 31 August 2000.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
    - heading "Construction history" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Songshan civil works were split into CG590A, CG590B and CG590C. DORTS's milestone article identifies CG590A as beginning on 18 December 2006 with Maeda as contractor, CG590B as beginning on 27 August 2006 with Rongmin and Okumura in a joint venture, and CG590C as beginning on 15 August 2006 with Daxin.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: The route project page lists the same three-contract structure and places the earliest contract signing on 29 March 2006.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The technical-document record says Xindian packages CH218, CH221, CH222 and CH224 were put to international tender where domestic technical capacity was insufficient, with other packages using domestic firms and foreign technical cooperation.
      - superscript:
        - link "[15]":
          - /url: "#ref-15"
      - text: This procurement history matters because the Xindian and Songshan projects were delivered in different eras and under different package structures, even though today’s passenger map presents one green route.
      - superscript:
        - link "[15]":
          - /url: "#ref-15"
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
    - heading "Engineering and construction" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The original 70.3 km first-phase network, including this line, was approved by the Executive Yuan on 4 April 1986 with a combined budget of NT$444.4 billion
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . As approved, the alignment was
      - strong: part underground and part elevated
      - text: ". DORTS's own record gives the reasons the route was changed: the width of the streets it runs under, and the environmental and visual impact an elevated structure would have had along that alignment"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . The Executive Yuan agreed to build the whole line underground on 20 May 1987
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: — before a single station on this line had opened.
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Songshan alignment had to pass beneath active TRA and HSR corridors, existing roads, deep foundations and operating metro infrastructure. DORTS describes bored tunnels beneath the Beimen overpass and railway tunnel, a minimum clearance requirement, cut-and-cover work at some stations, difficult crossings near Zhongshan and Songshan, and a tail track because a new depot site was not available.
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The milestone article records station boxes roughly 20–32 m deep.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: It describes soft clay and old foundations beneath Songshan station, narrow Bade Road, piles near the former Asiaworld site, and tunnelling 16.65 m below an operating Wenhu-line station. At Songjiang Nanjing, ten evacuation passages were manually constructed between tunnels inside an operating station, with grouting at more than 20 m depth.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
    - paragraph:
      - text: Beimen required a heritage procedure as well as a tunnel design. The DORTS heritage paper says contracts required an immediate stop when suspected relics appeared, followed by cultural-property review and expert assessment. It records Qing-period remains, drainage and foundations in the station area, and a 4.8 m overlap between the station and the 1909 Taipei Workshop; the workshop was moved about 30 m southeast after reinforcement and design-build changes.
      - superscript:
        - link "[13]":
          - /url: "#ref-13"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The power system was designed as part of the same engineering response.
      - superscript:
        - link "[14]":
          - /url: "#ref-14"
      - text: DORTS describes 161 kV and 22 kV gas-insulated equipment, optical-fibre temperature monitoring for tunnel cables, stray-current monitoring and high-impedance ground-fault warning. The Songshan main substation was placed underground at Taipei Arena to protect the surrounding urban view.
      - superscript:
        - link "[14]":
          - /url: "#ref-14"
    - paragraph:
      - text: On the earlier Xindian works, the CH218 geotechnical article records face pressure and water-pressure monitoring during shield tunnelling. Adjusting the face pressure and applying backfill and secondary grouting reduced observed surface settlement from 54 mm to about 25 mm, with quality checks continuing through the work.
      - superscript:
        - link "[17]":
          - /url: "#ref-17"
    - heading "Branch and depot" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The branch itself is short — DORTS's own project record gives it as approximately 1.5 km
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: ", while zh.wikipedia and Taiwan's TDX open-data platform both put it closer to 1.9 km"
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: (see "Length records and conflicts," below).
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: What makes it structurally unusual is that it drops from underground running to grade at Qizhang, then climbs to an elevated platform built inside Xindian Depot itself
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: DORTS's own planning FAQ explains why the branch cannot simply be folded into main-line service. The Xiaobitan platform is long enough for three cars only, so a full six-car main-line train arriving there could not open its rear three cars' doors — and there is no way to disable just those doors on demand, which the bureau describes as a fall risk
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: . The single-track section between Qizhang and Xiaobitan has only one platform face in each direction, and the branch also has to accommodate trains moving in and out of Xindian Depot
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: . DORTS's conclusion is that the branch is best kept as a dedicated three-car operation rather than merged with the main line
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: .
    - heading "Rolling stock" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: DORTS's procurement FAQ lists three three-car sets — nine cars in total — under contract CH321A specifically for this branch
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: . zh.wikipedia names two of the three sets, 397 and 398, built by Kawasaki as part of the
      - link "C371":
        - /url: /rail/metro/rolling-stock/c371/
      - text: "series-3 family, and describes them as genuine three-car trains rather than a shortened six-car formation: three cars form one set, and one set forms one train"
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: . The third set's number is not confirmed by the cited secondary account — TBC.
    - paragraph:
      - text: DORTS's same procurement table lists ten six-car sets, sixty cars, under Songshan contract CG391.
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: "These are procurement quantities tied to projects, not a present-day dispatch roster: DORTS explains that high-capacity batches are intended to be usable across the network, so current line allocation cannot be inferred safely from the old contract names alone."
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
    - paragraph
    - figure "A C371 car's doors, signed for Xindian on the Songshan–Xindian Line, stopped at Nanjing Sanmin. Solomon203, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons":
      - img "The doors of a C371 train car, a green destination sign overhead reading G Xindian, next stop Nanjing Sanmin"
      - text: A C371 car's doors, signed for Xindian on the Songshan–Xindian Line, stopped at Nanjing Sanmin. Solomon203, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons
    - paragraph
    - heading "Planning and catchment" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The branch was approved by the Executive Yuan on 17 September 1999
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . zh.wikipedia attributes the decision to lobbying by nearby residents and by representatives at various levels of government, and records the first documented planning reference as a 1999 Taipei County government notice — not an earlier date
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: . A News Lens feature examining the branch's low ridership (about 4,400 boardings and alightings a day) identifies 中央新村, a neighbourhood originally built to house retired National Assembly representatives, as overlapping the area the branch was built to serve, and frames the decision as representatives' pressure succeeding over planners' objections
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: . The named-director and construction-cost version is not included because the underlying page was not readable in full.
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
    - heading "Stations and interchange" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The current TDX sequence is G01 Xindian, G02
      - link "Xindian District Office":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/g02/
      - text: ", G03 Qizhang, G04 Dapinglin, G05"
      - link "Jingmei":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/g05/
      - text: ", G06"
      - link "Wanlong":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/g06/
      - text: ", G07"
      - link "Gongguan":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/g07/
      - text: ", G08 Taipower Building, G09 Guting, G10 CKS Memorial Hall, G11 Xiaonanmen, G12 Ximen, G13 Beimen, G14 Zhongshan, G15 Songjiang Nanjing, G16 Nanjing Fuxing, G17 Taipei Arena, G18 Nanjing Sanmin and G19 Songshan, with G03A Xiaobitan as the branch station."
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: This current numbering should not be confused with the 2014 technical article's working labels, in which Ximen appears as G13 and Songshan as
      - code: G22
      - text: .
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The line interchanges with the Tamsui–Xinyi Line at Guting and CKS Memorial Hall, with the Bannan Line at Ximen and Guting, with the
      - link "Wenhu Line":
        - /url: /rail/metro/lines/wenhu-line/
      - text: at Nanjing Fuxing, with the Airport MRT at Beimen, and with TRA at Songshan. DORTS's Songshan planning article describes six interchange stations in the project section and specifically identifies Beimen's airport connection and Songshan's railway connection.
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The NTU Hospital anomaly is a project-boundary issue rather than a missing station in the built network. DORTS counts it among the Xindian project's eleven stations but states that it operates as part of the Tamsui–Xinyi Line; TDX's current green-line sequence starts with G01 Xindian.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
    - heading "History, naming and public art" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Beimen takes its name from the historic north gate. The DORTS heritage paper records the station-area archaeological work, Qing-period remains, and the railway heritage buildings that shaped the final station treatment.
      - superscript:
        - link "[13]":
          - /url: "#ref-13"
      - text: The current code is G13 ; the 2014 technical article's contemporary working label for Beimen was G14 , so its labels are historical identifiers rather than current badges.
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Songshan technical article records public-art commissions at Zhongshan, Nanjing Fuxing, Taipei Arena, Nanjing Sanmin and Songshan, including the crystalline work 晶透, the platform work 流線月台 and works associated with the historic urban setting.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
    - paragraph:
      - link "TRTC":
        - /url: /rail/operators/trtc/
      - text: records that the earlier numeral "3" was replaced by the colour-letter code G in October 2016.
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: The exact date on which the numeral 3 was first assigned to this line remains TBC.
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
    - heading "Cross-colour service history" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: For sixteen years, Xindian Line trains and
      - link "Tamsui":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/r28/
      - text: Line trains ran through as one service while the wider network grew around them.
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: DORTS's operating-pattern article records the 1998 Zhonghe–Tamsui opening, the 1999 Tamsui–Xindian and Beitou–Nanshijiao pattern, later Beitou–Taipower Building and
      - link "Xiangshan":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/r02/
      - text: changes, and the 2014 separation into independent coloured lines.
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
    - paragraph:
      - text: On the night of 14 November 2014, the day before the Songshan section opened, a closing ceremony was held at Beimen.
      - superscript:
        - link "[20]":
          - /url: "#ref-20"
      - text: The last Tamsui–Xindian and Xiaonanmen trains departed at midnight. From 15 November, the former through service was replaced by Songshan–Xindian and Tamsui–Xiangshan operations.
      - superscript:
        - link "[20]":
          - /url: "#ref-20"
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"

      - text: The Xindian technical-document page gives a different 10.55 km main project and 1.53 km branch, and the track article describes 11.2 km from CKS Memorial Hall to Xindian with a separate depot scope.
      - superscript:

    - paragraph:
      - text: "The branch therefore has a second explicit conflict: approximately 1.5 km in DORTS's route project, 1.53 km in the construction-management article, 1.9 km in the secondary branch account and 1.94 km in TDX."
      - superscript:

    - paragraph:
      - text: The Songshan project page calls 499.3億元 its construction budget.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: The Audit Office fragment instead reports a 530億4,206萬元 expenditure budget and 502億9,566萬元 audited final expenditure. These are different accounting labels, so no single unqualified “cost” is presented.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":

      - superscript:

    - heading "Operations" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: "TRTC runs three named workings on this line: the full Songshan–Xindian service, a shorter Songshan–Taipower Building working, and the Qizhang– Xiaobitan branch"
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: . On the shared trunk, weekday peak headways run about 4–6 minutes, off-peak about 6–8 minutes, and about 12 minutes after 23:00; the Xiaobitan branch runs every 12–20 minutes throughout the day, with last trains at 23:57 from Xiaobitan and 00:09 from Qizhang
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: . End to end, Songshan–Xindian takes about 37 minutes and Songshan–Taipower Building about 23
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "TRTC's separate peak clarification gives a more granular picture: approximately three-minute Songshan–Taipower Building service, with some six-minute gaps on the shared section because Xiaobitan trains are inserted through shared Qizhang infrastructure."
      - superscript:
        - link "[21]":
          - /url: "#ref-21"
      - text: The two official pages describe different levels of the operating plan and are both retained.
    - heading "Incidents and ridership history" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Songshan technical article reports roughly 400,000 passenger trips per day in the 2014–2015 opening period.
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: Within the same network, the article gives about 1.98 million daily trips in 2014 and 3.028 million in 2015. These are the article's historical network and line measures.
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
    - paragraph:
      - text: On 13 September 2016 an engineering vehicle derailed near Xiaonanmen.
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: The response used single-track bidirectional working between Xiaonanmen and Zhongshan for 11 hours 39 minutes, shortened service intervals on the remaining segments and a bus bridge while the obstruction was cleared.
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The incident illustrates why the line's history includes operating interfaces: the Xiaonanmen segment was first built for Bannan Line depot access, then became a passenger section of the green line, and later formed the centre of a disruption-management plan."
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
