    - heading "Overview" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The red line runs the network's most varied ground: an inherited railway formation at the northern end, a viaduct across the Keelung River, the underground core through the main station, and the newer Xinyi arm under the financial district. It is also the oldest right-of-way on the system, and the builder says so in its own project record"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - heading "Route and alignment" [level=2]
    - heading "The corridor was a railway first" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Department of Rapid Transit Systems describes the northern half of this line as running
      - strong: 沿原北淡鐵路
      - text: — along the former TRA
      - link "Tamsui":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/r28/
      - text: railway — south from R28 to the Guizikeng Creek north of R22
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . That is the builder, in its own words, saying the alignment is not new. What was demolished, what was preserved, and when the railway itself closed are not established on this page; see the note at the foot.
    - heading "Three structures on one route" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: DORTS puts the whole northern alignment in a single sentence, and it is worth following in order
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: ":"
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - strong: At grade
        - text: from R28 as far as the Guizikeng Creek north of R22 — the inherited railway formation.
      - listitem:
        - strong: Elevated
        - text: from the Guizikeng embankment south, crossing the Keelung River.
      - listitem:
        - strong: Underground
        - text: from after Minzu West Road through to R08 .
    - paragraph:
      - text: Note the direction of travel in that description. The at-grade running is the
      - emphasis: northern
      - text: stretch, not a dip in the middle; an earlier draft of this site's research had it the other way round.
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Tamsui section is
      - strong: about 23.8 km
      - text: ", a figure that"
      - strong: includes
      - text: the approximately 1.2 km from R22 to R22A , and carries
      - strong: 22 stations and one main depot
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . The Xinyi section, by contrast, is
      - strong: wholly underground
      - text: ": about"
      - strong: 6.4 km
      - text: and seven stations, running east from R08 across Jinhua Street, Aiguo East Road and Hangzhou South Road and then along Xinyi Road into the Xinyi planning district
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: .
    - heading "Construction history" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Tamsui section came in three pieces, and DORTS records an inspection date against each
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: ":"
    - table:
      - rowgroup:
        - row "Section Trial inspection Final inspection Opened":
          - columnheader "Section"
          - columnheader "Trial inspection"
          - columnheader "Final inspection"
          - columnheader "Opened"
      - rowgroup:
        - row "Tamsui–Zhongshan 12 Feb 1997 21 Mar 1997 28 March 1997[1]":
          - cell "Tamsui–Zhongshan"
          - cell "12 Feb 1997"
          - cell "21 Mar 1997"
          - cell "28 March 1997[1]":
            - strong: 28 March 1997
            - superscript:
              - link "[1]":
                - /url: "#ref-1"
        - row "Zhongshan–Taipei Main — 17 Dec 1997 25 December 1997[1]":
          - cell "Zhongshan–Taipei Main"
          - cell "—"
          - cell "17 Dec 1997"
          - cell "25 December 1997[1]":
            - strong: 25 December 1997
            - superscript:
              - link "[1]":
                - /url: "#ref-1"
        - row "Taipei Main–CKS Memorial Hall — — 24 December 1998[1]":
          - cell "Taipei Main–CKS Memorial Hall":
            - link "Taipei":
              - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
            - text: Main–CKS Memorial Hall
          - cell "—"
          - cell "—"
          - cell "24 December 1998[1]":
            - strong: 24 December 1998
            - superscript:
              - link "[1]":
                - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: DORTS calls the result 「國內第一條通車的高運量捷運系統」 — the first high-capacity metro line in Taiwan to enter service
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: ". The last of those three stretches was not built with the rest of the Tamsui line at all: the project record notes against both R08 and R09 that 「本站工程併入捷運新店線辦理」, the station works were folded into the"
      - link "Xindian":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/g01/
      - text: line contract
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Xinyi section followed fifteen years later, inspected on 13 October and 8 November 2013 and opened on
      - strong: 24 November 2013
      - text: ", against a budget of NT$33.862 billion"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . Its seven-station count includes R08 and R05
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: ", both of which already existed on other lines — so a source giving a smaller number of stations \"opened in 2013\" is counting new stations rather than the project's, not contradicting it."
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The whole thing descends from one decision: the Executive Yuan approved the initial network on 4 April 1986 with a total budget of NT$444.4 billion, and the Tamsui line was let as 13 design contracts and around 120 construction contracts"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . The earliest of them is worth naming — contract CT107, earthworks for
      - link "Beitou Depot":
        - /url: /rail/metro/depots/beitou-depot/
      - text: ", signed on"
      - strong: 19 January 1988
      - text: ", which DORTS itself calls the earliest of them"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - heading "Engineering" [level=2]
    - 'heading "Dongmen: five tunnels and deep groundwater control" [level=3]'
    - paragraph:
      - text: Contract CK570H combined the cut-and-cover Dongmen interchange box with four metro shield tunnels and a fifth shield tunnel for a common-utility duct.
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: The later DORTS construction paper describes the box as about 216 m long, 25 m wide and 32 m deep.
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: Groundwater uplift in the
      - link "Songshan":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/g19/
      - text: No. 2 stratum would otherwise have required bottom sealing and extensive pumping, so the design used 1.5 m-thick diaphragm walls driven 72 m down, through a 28 m gravel layer, to an impermeable stratum; the wall was divided into 172 panels.
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
    - paragraph:
      - text: That geometry is not uncontested. A 2005 DORTS paper gives the same station as about 217 m long, 24.7 m wide and 31.2 m deep, and gives different shield-drive lengths.
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: Both primary sets are published in the conflicts section below; neither paper explains whether the difference reflects design stage, contract limits, as-built measurement or rounding.
    - 'heading "Daan Park: value engineering changed the architecture" [level=3]'
    - paragraph:
      - text: The station now known as R06 was engineering station R09 in the design paper. Its alternative scheme moved the box 9 m south and raised it 1.5 m, increasing the distance to buildings on the north from 9 m to 18 m.
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: The same move avoided most diversion of a drainage box culvert, reduced utility relocation and road occupation, separated two tunnels that had been only 50 cm apart, and allowed the intermediate sump between Dongmen and
      - link "Daan Park":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/r06/
      - text: to be removed.
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: The authors estimated about NT$160 million in works savings; that is an estimate in the paper, not a verified final-account saving.
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
    - paragraph:
      - text: Moving the box also reduced its distance from Daan Forest Park from about 14 m to about 5 m.
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: That engineering decision enabled the sunken garden and the design brief to bring sunlight and greenery into an underground station.
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
    - heading "Stations and architecture" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: DORTS says the breadth of the former railway land gave the northern section unusual freedom from site constraints, and its line-level design account describes variation as deliberate rather than accidental.
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - link "Jiantan":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/r15/
      - text: suspends a Chinese-form roof from steel cables;
      - link "Beitou":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/r22/
      - text: uses glass and a space truss for a bright large-span interior; Tamsui uses modern materials to evoke Fort San Domingo; and the other surface and elevated stations draw on local residential and Chinese structural forms.
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
    - paragraph:
      - text: Beitou's width follows its operating job. The DORTS monograph records a central island platform, side platforms and four tracks for the main line,
      - link "Xinbeitou":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/r22a/
      - text: branch and short-turn services.
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: At roughly twice an ordinary station's width, it needed a space-truss roof; the foundations use piles, pile caps and ground beams, while the above-ground structure is cast-in-place reinforced concrete with metal roof panels and glazed curtain walls.
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The Xinyi stations use a different line-wide language. DORTS calls the theme “dialogue”: architecture, landscape, interiors, public art, street furniture, lighting and colour were planned together to connect the stations to their urban surroundings."
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
    - heading "Operations" [level=2]
    - heading "The Xinbeitou branch" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: R22A hangs off R22 on a spur of about
      - strong: 1.2 km
      - text: ", and the builder counts that 1.2 km inside the Tamsui section's 23.8 km rather than alongside it"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: ". It is not a through service:"
      - link "TRTC":
        - /url: /rail/operators/trtc/
      - text: publishes
      - strong: Beitou–Xinbeitou
      - text: as one of the line's three service patterns in its own right, with its own headway table — about 7 to 8 minutes at peak, 10 minutes off-peak, 12 to 15 minutes early and late — and a running time of about
      - strong: 3 to 4 minutes
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: Chinese Wikipedia dates the branch's opening to 28 March 1997, alongside the Tamsui section, and says the shuttle runs Kawasaki
      - link "C371":
        - /url: /rail/metro/rolling-stock/c371/
      - text: stock in three-car sets
      - superscript:
        - link "[14]":
          - /url: "#ref-14"
      - text: ". Both are plausible and neither is confirmed here. That article's only external citation was followed on 10 August 2026: it points at a TRTC page which turns out to be the old-version network map and timetable index, and which says nothing about the branch at all"
      - superscript:
        - link "[13]":
          - /url: "#ref-13"
      - text: . The opened primary records do not establish the branch's track configuration or train livery, so both fields remain TBC.
    - heading "What runs, and how often" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: "TRTC operates three patterns:"
      - strong: Tamsui–Xiangshan
      - text: ","
      - strong: Beitou–Daan
      - text: and
      - strong: Beitou–Xinbeitou
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: ". The short working terminates at R05 , but the overlap that matters to a passenger is longer than that: at weekday peaks each pattern runs about every 6 minutes, giving"
      - strong: about 3 minutes over Beitou–Xiangshan
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: . Off-peak it is about 8 to 10 minutes each and 4 to 5 minutes over the overlap; after 23:00 only Tamsui–Xiangshan runs, at about 12 minutes
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: . End to end, Tamsui to
      - link "Xiangshan":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/r02/
      - text: takes about
      - strong: 54 minutes
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: .
    - 'heading "Ridership: what is published is not this line" [level=3]'
    - paragraph:
      - text: This line is routinely described as one of the two busiest on the network, and TRTC's published series does not permit a line-specific total. It reports
      - strong:
        - link "文湖線":
          - /url: /rail/metro/lines/wenhu-line/
        - text: separately and everything else as an aggregate
      - text: — 高運量包含淡水信義、 松山新店、中和新蘆、
      - link "板南線":
        - /url: /rail/metro/lines/bannan-line/
      - text: ", four lines under one heading"
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: . For June 2026 that aggregate was 5,651.03 萬人次 against the Wenhu Line's 596.14, and for the year to June, 34,448.75 against 3,583.92
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The ridership rows therefore remain TBC. TRTC does publish per-station entry and exit counts going back to 2015
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: ", but no opened operator table supplies the line total directly."
    - heading "Xinyi east extension" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: "An eastward extension of the Xinyi section is under construction:"
      - strong: about 1.4 km
      - text: ","
      - strong: one underground station
      - text: ", plus tail tracks for operational turnback"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: . The station is 廣慈/奉天宮, sited under Fude Street in front of the Guangci Boai park complex, with shield tunnels continuing east under Fude Street and Zhongpo South Road to Yucheng Park
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: . The Executive Yuan approved the planning report on 12 February 2010, with amendments in September 2014 and January 2018
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "It was meant to be two stations. DORTS gives the reason the other was dropped in plain terms: the landowners at the Xinyi Road Section 6 site refused to take part in the joint land development, so the condition for siting a station there was never met"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The separate contract page identifies CR580C, a 17 October 2016 construction start, design by Moh and Associates, supervision by DORTS's Second District Project Office and a construction joint venture of BES Engineering and Obayashi's Taiwan branch.
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: It describes a three-level island- platform station about 213.9 m long and 16.55 m wide, a 119.4 m crossover and two shield machines selected for hard rock, weak clay and mixed ground.
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The narrow Fude Street site forced diaphragm-wall work close to buildings on both sides. DORTS says the shallow soil was weak, while deep rock proved four times harder than expected; suspending night work to limit disturbance also broke the continuity of construction.
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: The architectural scheme turns the historical Liugong irrigation system into blue horizontal and curved “water” forms, with entrances integrated into the planned Xinyi District administrative centre and a Guangci Boai complex building.
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
    - paragraph:
      - text: Neither opened DORTS page gives a project cost or opening date, so both remain TBC.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
    - paragraph:
      - text: A numbering trap worth flagging while it is still live. The station being built takes
      - strong:
        - code: R01
      - text: ", at the end of a line whose other codes were assigned long before — and this line already carries one scheme laid over another: DORTS's own station table prints a separate"
      - link "工程編號":
        - /url: /rail/technology/station-numbering/
      - text: column of original construction numbers beside today's passenger codes, and the two do not run in step
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . Any planning-era station number for this extension should be read as belonging to that older scheme rather than to the codes a passenger sees.
    - heading "Where the sources disagree" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Dongmen dimensions and shield drives.
      - text: The 2005 DORTS paper reports a box about
      - strong: 217 m × 24.7 m
      - text: ", excavated about"
      - strong: 31.2 m
      - text: ", with Xinyi shield drives of"
      - strong: 1,240.5 m
      - text: and
      - strong: 1,247.0 m
      - text: (about 2,487.5 m combined).
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: The 2014 DORTS construction paper instead reports about
      - strong: 216 m × 25 m
      - text: ", an excavation of about"
      - strong: 32 m
      - text: ", and drives of"
      - strong: 1,219.3 m
      - text: and
      - strong: 1,225.8 m
      - text: (about 2,445.1 m combined).
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: The difference is published as a conflict because neither source states why its measuring basis differs.
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Route length.
      - text: DORTS's two published figures are 23.8 km for the Tamsui section including the branch
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: and 6.4 km for the Xinyi section
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . They meet end to end at R08 , so they sum to 30.2 km with the branch, or 29.0 km for the main line alone — but that sum is this page's arithmetic on two primary figures, not anybody's published length. Chinese Wikipedia's infobox gives
      - strong: 32.3 km
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: . Nothing read for this page explains the two-to-three kilometre gap, and the whole-line spec row therefore reads TBC rather than picking one. The Wenhu Line's three lengths turned out to be three correct measurements of three different things; this may be the same, and saying so is not the same as knowing it.
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Station count.
      - text: DORTS's 22
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: and 7
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: share R08 , which nets to 28 — the number in service today, R02 to R28 plus R22A . Chinese Wikipedia says 29, counting the unopened
      - code: R01
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: . Those are compatible once you know what each counts.
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Rolling stock.
      - text: Chinese Wikipedia's line infobox names
      - link "C301":
        - /url: /rail/metro/rolling-stock/c301/
      - text: ","
      - link "C381":
        - /url: /rail/metro/rolling-stock/c381/
      - text: and C381A
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: ; its Xinbeitou article names C371 for the branch
      - superscript:
        - link "[14]":
          - /url: "#ref-14"
      - text: . Two articles on one encyclopedia, two fleets. Neither was checked against a TRTC or manufacturer record, so the facts panel names no fleet at all. The obvious reconciliation is obvious enough to be suspicious.

      - text: "See also:"

      - text: .

          - text: 淡水信義線／淡水線路線說明 primary Taipei City Government, Department of Rapid Transit Systems ( 臺北市政府捷運工程局 ) accessed 2026-08-10 The builder's own project record. The whole alignment in one sentence — 淡水線北起淡水站沿原北淡鐵路南行至北投以北之貴子坑溪為地面段；自貴子坑溪堤起高架南行跨基隆河，過民族西路下降進入地下至中正紀念堂站，全長約23.8公里(含北投至新北投路段約1.2公里)，設22座車站及1座主機廠 — plus 另新北投支線為北投站至新北投站, the 1986 approval and NT$444.4bn budget, the 13 design and ~120 construction contracts, the opening and inspection dates in ROC years, and 最早CT107標北投機廠土方工程，自77年1月19日簽約開始施工. Its station table carries a 工程編號 column distinct from the passenger codes.

        - listitem:
          - link "Station Architectural Design":
            - /url: https://www.dorts.gov.taipei/cp.aspx?n=980C85299DA2890A&s=D040F0979870BED5
          - text: "車站建築設計 primary Taipei City Government, Department of Rapid Transit Systems ( 臺北市政府捷運工程局 ) accessed 2026-08-23 DORTS's line-level architectural account: 淡水線的基地原為北淡線舊鐵路用地，其基地的可運用度最大，因此建築設計形式幾乎不受任何限制. It identifies the design ideas at Jiantan, Beitou and Tamsui, and describes the Xinyi street architecture under the theme 對話."
        - listitem:
          - 'link "Taipei MRT Engineering Series, Revised Edition No. 34: Architectural Form Design for Elevated MRT Stations"':
            - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page68.html
          - text: 捷運工程叢書 精進版－34 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Government, Department of Rapid Transit Systems ( 臺北市政府捷運工程局 ) accessed 2026-08-23 The Beitou case study states 車站中央設有島式月臺及兩側為側式月臺，共計四軌, explains that the station is twice the normal width, and documents the space-truss roof, piles, pile caps, ground beams and cast-in-place reinforced-concrete superstructure.
        - listitem:
          - 'link "From Concept Creation to Innovation: Planning and Design of Taipei MRT Daan Park Station ( R09 )"':
            - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/JRTST/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page71.html
          - text: 從創意到創新－以臺北捷運大安森林公園站（R09）站之規劃設計為例探討 primary Rapid Transit Systems & Technology, Taipei DORTS ( 臺北市政府捷運工程局《捷運技術》 ) accessed 2026-08-23 The value-engineering alternative states R09 車站南移9.0m，站體提高1.5m, gives the building-clearance, drainage, tunnel-gradient and road-occupation reasons, and estimates about NT$160 million in works savings.
        - listitem:
          - 'link "Construction Problems Where Multiple Tunnels Cross and Overlap: Xinzhuang Line CK570H"':
            - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/JRTST/ebook/no33/files/basic-html/page96.html
          - text: 多條隧道交叉重疊施工問題探討—以新莊線 CK570H 為例探討 primary Rapid Transit Systems & Technology, Taipei DORTS ( 臺北市政府捷運工程局《捷運技術》 ) accessed 2026-08-23 The earlier paper reports Dongmen at about 217 m by 24.7 m with a 31.2 m excavation, and Xinyi shield drives of 1,240.5 m and 1,247.0 m. These values conflict with the later DORTS paper.
        - listitem:
          - link "Construction of Taipei MRT Xinyi Line Contract CK570H":
            - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/JRTST/ebook/no51/files/basic-html/page82.html
          - text: 臺北捷運信義線CK570H區段標施工 primary Rapid Transit Systems & Technology, Taipei DORTS ( 臺北市政府捷運工程局《捷運技術》 ) accessed 2026-08-23 The later paper reports Dongmen at about 216 m by 25 m with a 32 m excavation, Xinyi shield drives of 1,219.3 m and 1,225.8 m, and 72 m diaphragm walls driven through 28 m of gravel to an impermeable layer.
        - listitem:
          - link "Xinyi Line East Extension — CR580C Section Contract":
            - /url: https://www.dorts.gov.taipei/cp.aspx?n=027CDB8C2A690039&s=A900A23BE33939EA
          - text: 捷運信義線東延段CR580C區段標工程 primary Taipei City Government, Department of Rapid Transit Systems ( 臺北市政府捷運工程局 ) accessed 2026-08-23 The live contract page gives the 17 October 2016 start, designer, supervisors and joint contractors; describes the one-station, crossover and two-shield-machine works; and states 淺層土壤弱軟，深層岩盤堅硬，硬度超出預期4倍.
        - listitem:
          - 'link "Routes and headways: Tamsui–Xinyi Line"':
            - /url: https://www.metro.taipei/cp.aspx?n=EAD981369A065968&s=1CC297E1D0B4C7B1
          - text: "路線及班距／淡水信義線 primary Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation ( 臺北大眾捷運股份有限公司 ) accessed 2026-08-10 The operator's own service table: 營運模式【淡水－象山】、【北投－大安】、【北投－新北投】; peak 約6分鐘，北投－象山區間約3分鐘; off-peak 約8～10分鐘，重疊區間約4～5分鐘; after 23:00 約12分鐘（僅行駛【淡水－象山】模式）; and running times of 約54分鐘, 約32分鐘 and 約3～4分鐘. The Xinbeitou shuttle has its own headway rows, 7～8分鐘 at peak."
        - listitem:
          - link "Ridership statistics by year and by month":
            - /url: https://www.metro.taipei/cp.aspx?n=FED7CC0F31E0A664
          - text: 各年度暨前一月旅運量統計資料 primary Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation ( 臺北大眾捷運股份有限公司 ) accessed 2026-08-10 Cited here for what it does not break out. 單位：萬人次. The line column is 文湖線 against 高運量, and 高運量包含淡水信義、松山新店、中和新蘆、板南線 — one number for four lines. June 2026 (民國115年6月) gave 高運量 5,651.03 萬人次 against 文湖線 596.14; the year to June, 34,448.75 against 3,583.92; full-year 民國114, 69,462.4 against 7,249.5.
        - listitem:
          - link "Tamsui–Xinyi line":
            - /url: https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/淡水信義線
          - text: 淡水信義線 secondary 維基百科 (Chinese Wikipedia) accessed 2026-08-10 Read as a lead index. Its infobox gives 路線長度 32.3公里 and 車站數目 29, and names C301, C381 and C381A as the fleet — all of which this page publishes only as conflicts, because the article's footnote list could not be retrieved and so none of it could be traced to what it cites.
        - listitem:
          - link "Network map, station information and timetables (old version)":
            - /url: https://www.metro.taipei/cp.aspx?n=91974F2B13D997F1
          - text: 路網圖、各站資訊及時刻表(舊版) primary 臺北大眾捷運股份有限公司 (Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation) accessed 2026-08-11 Cited only as the negative it is. This is the single external citation on zh.wikipedia's 新北投支線 article; it was fetched and read on 11 August 2026 and is a navigation index carrying menu items and contact details. 新北投支線 does not appear on it, nor does anything about single-track working, the shuttle, or the branch's painted train. A citation to an official source is not that source — this is what checking one looks like when it fails.
        - listitem:
          - link "Xinbeitou branch line":
            - /url: https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/新北投支線
          - text: 新北投支線 secondary 維基百科 (Chinese Wikipedia) accessed 2026-08-10 全長1.2公里, which independently matches the builder's figure; 1997年3月28日：淡水線與新北投支線正式通車啟用; and 川崎重工371型 in three-car sets, 三節車廂為一組，以單組為一列. Its single external citation was checked on 10 August 2026 and does not support it — see the body.

        - /url: /rail/metro/lines/tamsui-xinyi-line/
      - text: 淡水信義線

    - navigation "On this page":
      - paragraph: On this page
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - link "Overview":
            - /url: "#overview"
        - listitem:
          - link "Procurement and specification":
            - /url: "#procurement-and-specification"
        - listitem:

        - listitem:
          - link "Manufacture, delivery and testing":
            - /url: "#manufacture-delivery-and-testing"
        - listitem:
          - link "Renewal":
            - /url: "#renewal"
        - listitem:
          - link "Fleet-count conflict":
            - /url: "#fleet-count-conflict"
        - listitem:
          - link "Specifications":
            - /url: "#specifications"
        - listitem:
          - link "References":
            - /url: "#references"
    - heading "Overview" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The 301 type was the first electric fleet bought for
      - link "Taipei":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
      - text: "'s high-capacity metro."
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: Contract CT301 supplied 132 cars for the original
      - link "Tamsui":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/r28/
      - text: Line, and DORTS's detailed history counts them as 22 fixed six-car trains.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: Passenger service began when the first Tamsui section opened on 28 March 1997.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The contracting record is more precise than the usual “Kawasaki-built” label. DORTS names the contractor as Union Rail Car Partnership (URC); a later DORTS article describes URC as the United States subsidiary of Kawasaki Heavy Industries.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: No corporate filing defining that relationship was found in this search, so the contractor and DORTS's description are retained as two separate statements.
    - heading "Procurement and specification" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The train contract formally began on 20 December 1989 at a stated value of NT$4.5 billion.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: "Its first tender failed: the original specification called for all six cars to be motored, which DORTS's retrospective says made the offer too expensive."
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: The specification was changed to 4M2T — four motor cars and two trailers — arranged as two three-car DM1–T–M2 units and operated as a fixed six-car train at both peak and off-peak times.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: That decision sat beside two other foundational choices. DORTS selected AC induction motors after comparing them with DC traction, citing efficiency, maintenance and reliability, and selected stainless steel rather than aluminium after considering corrosion and welding in Taiwan's climate.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: The published design load was 60 seated and 310 standing passengers per car, with a maximum operating speed of 80 km/h.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - heading "Design" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The original electrical system collected 750 V DC from a bottom-contact third rail and combined regenerative electrical braking with pneumatic friction braking.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: Its bolsterless two-axle bogies used conical rubber primary suspension and air-spring secondary suspension, while ATP and ATO supervised train operation.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The stainless bodysides incline inward above the waist, a profile DORTS says both fitted the tunnel envelope and left passengers a step back from a door that opened unexpectedly.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: Each 1,500 mm exterior-sliding door used pneumatic drive, and each car had two independent split air-conditioning sets, with condensers below and evaporators above the ceiling.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: The driving end used an FRP face panel and an anti-climber intended to resist cars riding over one another in a collision.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
    - heading "Manufacture, delivery and testing" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Final design review finished on 31 August 1992, followed by a prototype-train factory ceremony in the United States that September.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: Prototype cars EMU 01/02 reached
      - link "Beitou Depot":
        - /url: /rail/metro/depots/beitou-depot/
      - text: on 1 December 1992; production deliveries followed in March, May and August 1993, and all 132 cars had reached
      - link "Beitou":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/r22/
      - text: by November 1995.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: Testing lasted from December 1992 until May 1996.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: DORTS lists fourteen prototype-test groups covering coasting, abnormal operation, wheel slip and slide, heat rise, regenerative power, clearances, functions, noise, vibration, bogie stability, ride comfort, communications, train-control simulation and electromagnetic interference.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: The operator completed the production-car tests and joint inspections in November 1996 before passenger opening the following March.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
    - heading "Renewal" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The fleet's systems have been renewed in stages rather than in one documented mid-life package. By 2012,
      - link "TRTC":
        - /url: /rail/operators/trtc/
      - text: had renewed communications and passenger information on all 22 trains, adding three-colour LED displays, wider viewing angles, destination, door-side and time information, and line-colour frames on the exterior destination displays.
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
    - paragraph:
      - text: TRTC's 2014 report records preventive work on important traction circuit boards and improvements to door guides; the 2015 report records nine overhauled trains and traction and air-conditioning reset work.
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: A DORTS engineering article defines the central traction change as replacement of GTO inverter modules with IGBT modules to reduce energy use.
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: None of the fetched primary pages gives a single completion date or names both the original and replacement traction suppliers, so those details remain TBC.
    - heading "Fleet-count conflict" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The detailed DORTS history and TRTC's 2012 report both give 22 trains, while the fixed formation and total of 132 cars independently produce the same arithmetic: 22 × 6 = 132."
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: DORTS's later no. 48 article instead prints
      - code: 132 輛 (21 列)
      - text: — 132 cars and 21 trains.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: That parenthetical conflicts with both the other official records and its own six-car context; it is published here as an unresolved source error rather than quietly discarded.

    - paragraph:
      - text: There is no cab. Stand at the front of the leading car and the guideway comes straight at you — through the hills above
      - link "Muzha":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br02/
      - text: ", across the rooftops of eastern"
      - link "Taipei":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
      - text: ", over the Keelung River into"
      - link "Neihu":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br19/
      - text: . It is the best free view in the city, and it exists because nobody needs to sit where you are standing.
    - paragraph:
      - text: The Wenhu Line was
      - strong: Taiwan's first metro line
      - superscript:
        - link "[15]":
          - /url: "#ref-15"
      - text: ", and it remains the only line in the Taipei network running on rubber tyres rather than steel wheels. That choice is what lets it climb through Wenshan's hills; the precise gradients remain TBC, and the design criteria that would establish them were not found in the sources used here."
    - heading "History" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The name is a contraction:"
      - strong: Wen
      - text: shan and Nei
      - strong: hu
      - text: ", the districts at either end. The two halves opened thirteen years apart, and they are the two halves of one of the strangest procurement stories in modern transit."

    - heading "The alignment was redrawn by protest before a metre of it was built" [level=3]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The route that opened in 1996 is not the route that was approved
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: . A 13 km scheme from
      - link "Taipei Zoo":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br01/
      - text: to
      - link "Liuzhangli":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br07/
      - text: had already been settled when
      - strong: residents in Muzha objected, and on 4 May the northern section was redirected onto Fuxing South and North Roads
      - text: — where it runs today
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "That is the earliest instance of a pattern this site records twice more: the"
      - link "Songshan–Xindian Line":
        - /url: /rail/metro/lines/songshan-xindian-line/
      - text: redesigned from part-elevated to fully underground in 1987 on street-width and visual-impact grounds, and the Neihu extension held up for years over the same argument.
      - strong: The objection came first, before the line existed, and it worked.
      - text: The sources read for this page do not identify exactly what moved or which proposed stations went with it.
    - paragraph:
      - text: The original section was bought in 1988 as a turnkey system from France's Matra
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: . What followed —
      - strong: two fires during testing in 1993
      - text: ", on 5 May and 24 September, the second recorded as exactly that, 第二次火燒車事件, a second vehicle-fire incident"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: ; an opening four and a quarter years late; the builder's withdrawal from maintaining its own system; and a lawsuit that ran until the Supreme Court ordered the city to pay roughly NT$1.64 billion in 2005
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: "— is told in full on its own page:"
      - strong:
        - link "The Matra dispute":
          - /url: /rail/history/matra-dispute/
      - text: . The short version is that Taipei learned, expensively, how not to buy a railway, and bought the second half differently.
    - paragraph:
      - text: When the Neihu extension opened on 4 July 2009, the two sections began running as one through line under the extension's new CITYFLO 650 signalling
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: . The original VAL256 fleet was withdrawn that same day for conversion to the new system and did not carry passengers again until 26 December 2010
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: — eighteen months in which the 1996 railway ran entirely on the 2009 trains. See
      - link "VAL256":
        - /url: /rail/metro/rolling-stock/val256/
      - text: .
    - heading "Route and alignment" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Elevated for almost its entire length. From BR01 the line climbs north through Wenshan District, crosses central Taipei on an east–west alignment, then turns north-east across the Keelung River into Neihu.
    - paragraph:
      - strong:
        - text: "Two of the twenty-four stations are underground: BR13"
        - link "Songshan Airport":
          - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br13/
        - text: and BR14
        - link "Dazhi":
          - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br14/
      - text: ", and both are now settled by DORTS itself rather than inferred."
    - paragraph:
      - text: The builder's project record gives the Neihu section as 14.8 km with 「地下段3.9公里，2座地下站」 — 3.9 km underground, two underground stations
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: "— which narrows the pair to BR13 – BR24 without naming them. Its station architecture page then names one of the two and counts the rest: 「除大直站為地下車站外，其餘共有十座高架車站」, apart from Dazhi being underground, the remaining ten are elevated"
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: . Ten elevated plus Dazhi is eleven of the section's twelve stations, and the project record says there are exactly two underground
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . The twelfth station is Songshan Airport, so Songshan Airport is the second. Two primary documents that never mention each other, and the identification falls out of the arithmetic between them. zh.wikipedia names the same pair outright
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: ; it is no longer what the claim rests on.
    - paragraph: No source read for this page establishes the platform depths; they remain TBC.
    - paragraph:
      - text: "Every platform on the line has full-height platform screen doors: Faiveley equipment from BR01 to BR12 , ST Electronics from BR13 to BR24"
      - superscript:
        - link "[13]":
          - /url: "#ref-13"
      - text: .
    - heading "Stations and passenger facilities" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: DORTS's station table counts the street exits at every station, and the distribution is lopsided in a way that says something about how the line was built
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Eight of the twenty-four stations have exactly one exit
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: ", and seven of those eight are consecutive: BR02 Muzha through BR08 Technology Building, an unbroken run from Wenshan into Daan where every station has one way in and one way out. BR12"
      - link "Zhongshan Junior High School":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br12/
      - text: is the eighth
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: "Twenty of the twenty-four have three exits or fewer. The whole line has sixty-three between its twenty-four stations, and a quarter of those are at two stations: BR11 Nanjing Fuxing and BR24 Nangang Exhibition Center have eight each. BR09 Daan has six, BR10 Zhongxiao Fuxing five. All four are interchanges"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: That is not a trivia column. A single-exit station is one lift, one stair, one escalator bank and one crowd; when it closes, the station closes. It is a predictable consequence of building a medium-capacity railway on a single row of columns down the middle of an existing road — the same constraint DORTS gives for why these stations carry no decoration, which is that a single-column support system limits what you can hang on it
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: . The exits are the same economy, at street level.
    - paragraph:
      - text: The builder's full design rationale is expanded in
      - link "Why the Wenhu Line looks the way it does":
        - /url: /rail/technology/wenhu-station-architecture/
      - text: ", including the three Neihu architectural vocabularies and the treatment of the viaduct underside."
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
    - paragraph:
      - text: Every station page carries its own count, from the same table
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - strong:
        - text: BR06
        - link "Linguang":
          - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br06/
        - text: is the exception that proves the constraint was real.
      - text: It has two exits and it is the first station on the
      - link "Taipei Metro":
        - /url: /rail/operators/trtc/
      - text: that opened with both of them already built
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: — everywhere else, a second exit was something added later or not at all. The same station has
      - strong: two ticket machines, the fewest anywhere on the network
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: .
    - heading "Operations and service" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Trains run without on-board drivers under automatic train control, at GoA4 — unattended train operation, the highest grade
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: Weekday headways are about 2–4 minutes at peak, 4–10 off-peak, and about 12 minutes after 23:00; weekends and holidays run the off-peak pattern all day
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: .
      - strong: End to end takes about 45 minutes
      - text: ", BR01 to BR24 or the reverse"
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: . zh.wikipedia adds that the headway can be compressed to 80 seconds
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: ; that is a signalling capability rather than a timetable, and no primary source for it was found.
    - heading "Length records and measurement conflicts" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Four figures circulate, and they are not in conflict — they measure four different things.
      - strong: This site publishes 25.17 km, the operating length
      - text: ", and says what each of the others counts."

    - paragraph:
      - text: "The last row is the one this site got wrong: it printed the untrimmed figure as the route length for four builds, because measuring everything MOTC draws counts depot lead and tail track that no passenger travels on"
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: . Trimmed to the termini, the same geometry lands within 130 m of the operator's own figure
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: — and that agreement is the check working, which is why both are still printed side by side on the
      - link "network page":
        - /url: /rail/network/
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: The 25.7 km that appears as 路線長度 on zh.wikipedia
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: is the
      - strong: sum of the two published section lengths
      - text: ": DORTS records 木柵線 約10.9公里 and 內湖線 約14.8公里, and 10.9 + 14.8 = 25.7 exactly"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . Those are project lengths — the extent of what was built, including non-revenue track at each end — which is why the total exceeds the 25.17 km of railway that carries passengers
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: .
    - heading "Rolling stock" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "Two fleets share the line, both running as four cars made up of two coupled pairs:"
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - link "VAL256":
          - /url: /rail/metro/rolling-stock/val256/
        - text: — 51 pairs, the original Muzha Line fleet
        - superscript:
          - link "[11]":
            - /url: "#ref-11"
      - listitem:
        - link "Innovia APM 256 (C370)":
          - /url: /rail/metro/rolling-stock/innovia-apm-256-c370/
        - text: — 101 pairs, delivered for the Neihu extension
        - superscript:
          - link "[12]":
            - /url: "#ref-12"
    - 'heading "The fleet totals do not divide: three readings" [level=3]'
    - paragraph:
      - text: A four-car train on this line is two coupled pairs. DORTS's procurement record gives
      - strong: 51 pairs of VAL256 and 101 pairs of Innovia
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: . The renewal reporting counts
      - strong: 25 Matra trains and 51 Bombardier trains
      - text: ", 76 in total"
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: .
    - paragraph:
      - text: Those do not reconcile
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: . 25 four-car trains need 50 pairs, not 51; 51 trains need 102 pairs, not 101. The totals agree — 152 pairs, 304 cars, 76 trains
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: — but
      - strong: neither fleet on its own divides into whole trains.
    - paragraph: "Three readings, and nothing found settles between them:"
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - strong: A spare pair in each fleet.
        - text: 25 Matra trains plus one pair out of service, 50 Bombardier trains plus one — which makes the "76 trains" figure a count of the two fleets' nominal sizes rather than of trains in traffic.
      - listitem:
        - strong: Formations are not fixed.
        - text: zh.wikipedia describes the VAL256 as 「非固定編組」, running as four consecutively-numbered cars rather than as a permanent set
        - superscript:
          - link "[5]":
            - /url: "#ref-5"
        - text: . If pairs are re-formed in maintenance, the two counts are simply two different things measured on two different days
        - superscript:
          - link "[5]":
            - /url: "#ref-5"
        - text: ", and there is no discrepancy to explain."
      - listitem:
        - strong: One train is mixed.
        - text: Moving a pair across the boundary makes both counts work — and would mean exactly one train on this line runs one fleet's pair coupled to the other's.
    - paragraph:
      - strong: The third would make this page wrong
      - text: ", because it describes the fleets as separate. It is also the only one of the three that requires something no source found here reports"
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: . It is recorded here because leaving it out would be picking an answer quietly.
    - paragraph:
      - text: "They are not the same vehicle and not the same design lineage — the second was built by a competitor to fit the first's guideway, which is the Matra story's last chapter — but the interface they share is exact: the same running-surface spacing, the same side guide bars, the same 750 V taken off them"
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - superscript:
        - link "[14]":
          - /url: "#ref-14"
      - text: . TRTC has announced a programme to replace all 76 trains by 2041 — see the research notes, and treat the figures as provisional.
    - heading "Depots" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - link "Muzha Depot":
        - /url: /rail/metro/depots/muzha-depot/
      - text: sits at the southern end beside BR01 and opened with the line in 1996
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: .
      - link "Neihu Depot":
        - /url: /rail/metro/depots/neihu-depot/
      - text: was built for the extension and came into use in 2009
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: . Despite its name it is in Nangang District, and it joins the running line at
      - strong: BR24
      - text: ", at the far end of the line"
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: .
    - heading "Sources" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Station names, codes, running order, coordinates and the end-to-end journey time come from
      - strong: Taiwan MOTC's TDX platform
      - text: ", operator TRTC — government open data, retrieved 5 August 2026."
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: The strip map is generated from it directly. Everything else is cited inline and listed below.
    - paragraph: TDX does not publish station structure, headways, or anything about rolling stock and depots; those come from TRTC's and DORTS's own publications where they exist, and are marked secondary where they do not.
    - heading "Corrections" [level=2]
    - paragraph: This page's errors are corrected in place and recorded here, most recent first.
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - strong: The strip map drew Neihu Depot at the wrong end of the line for four builds.
        - text: This page previously said the depot joined the running line near BR19 Neihu — an unsourced inference from the shared name. It actually connects at BR24 , in Nangang District
        - superscript:
          - link "[2]":
            - /url: "#ref-2"
        - text: ", and the map marker moved with the fact."
        - code: npm run facts
        - text: now cross-checks the marker against the depot page's own stated junction.
      - listitem:
        - strong: Two engineering superlatives were removed rather than corrected.
        - text: This page used to say the gradients through Wenshan were steeper than conventional heavy metro could manage, and that the elevated curves would be
        - emphasis: impossible
        - text: on a steel-wheel alignment. Both are probably true and neither was sourced, and "impossible" was doing a great deal of unattributed work. They can return when DORTS's design criteria are found.
      - listitem:
        - strong: The 25.7 km figure was described as unaccounted for.

The line runs on viaduct for all but 3.9 km of its length, dives under Songshan Airport and the Keelung River, and comes back up beside the south portal of the Ziqiang road tunnel at Dazhi.": STREET LEVEL ON VIADUCT IN TUNNEL BR01 BR09 BR12 BR13 BR14 BR15 BR24 0 5 10 15 20 25.17 km along the route
      - list:

      - text: The line runs on viaduct for all but 3.9 km of its length, dives under Songshan Airport and the Keelung River, and comes back up beside the south portal of the Ziqiang road tunnel at Dazhi.
      - strong: 3.9 km of the line runs underground.
      - text: "2.58 km of that is between the two underground stations, which is fixed by the operator’s own chainage. The remaining 1.32 km is ramp at the two portals, and no source divides it between them — so it is drawn as unplaced rather than split. The 3.9 km is DORTS's own figure for the Neihu section, and it is the line's only underground running: the builder records the Muzha section as 全線以高架方式興建, built entirely on viaduct. zh.wikipedia's route description reads 穿越福州山隧道後, which implies a tunnel between BR05 and BR06 where DORTS instead has the line passing the north side of the Xinhai road tunnel. A viaduct does not run through a hill, so the drawing follows the builder — but the two accounts of that half-kilometre have not been reconciled. Distance is to scale. Height is not: no source gives a rail level, and an axis invented to look like a measurement would be worse than none."

    - heading "Why there are no 500 individual stubs" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: "The source record can support useful rows for classes, contract lots, car-number ranges and delivery sequences. It cannot support a truthful page for every set: the missing fields are precisely the fields a roster page would promise — a stable number, current line, current depot, refurbishment state and withdrawal status."
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[19]":
          - /url: "#ref-19"
      - superscript:
        - link "[18]":
          - /url: "#ref-18"
      - text: A family/lot table therefore keeps the known identifiers visible, marks unit-level gaps as TBC, and can be split into individual pages later if TRTC or NTMC publishes an asset register.
    - paragraph:
      - text: The table also avoids treating procurement purpose as current allocation. DORTS explicitly says connected high-capacity depots can be mutually used, and NTMC's temporary Ankeng-to-Danhai validation movement shows the same problem in an operational release.
      - superscript:
        - link "[19]":
          - /url: "#ref-19"
      - superscript:
        - link "[18]":
          - /url: "#ref-18"
      - text: A line name in a contract column is therefore historical context, not a claim that every train remains there today.
    - paragraph: The unresolved items are current unit-to-depot mappings, full serial ranges, unit-level refurbishment histories, withdrawals and preservation. The next primary documents that would settle them are a TRTC 車輛處 asset/stabling register and NTMC procurement handover or vehicle-register records. Until those are fetched, the honest roster is the table above rather than invented precision.

    - heading "Overview" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: DORTS selected the French Matra V256 system through an international competition in March 1988.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: The builder's later technical history calls the fleet VAL 256, identifies it as a Matra-produced derivative of the VAL system and records manufacture in 1991.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: The cars opened
      - link "Taipei":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
      - text: "'s first metro service on the"
      - link "Muzha Line":
        - /url: /rail/metro/lines/wenhu-line/
      - text: on 28 March 1996.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
    - paragraph:
      - text: Contract CC350 covered 51 two-car pairs, or 102 cars.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: DORTS describes Taipei's service pattern as two pairs coupled into a four-car train — the first such double-pair operation in this vehicle family.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: The records recovered here do not say whether the same pairs remain permanently coupled into one four-car set, so train-level coupling permanence remains TBC.
    - heading "Carbody and passenger layout" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Each car is 13.78 m long, 2.56 m wide and 3.53 m high; DORTS says the width is the source of the
      - code: "256"
      - text: designation.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: A car has two outside-sliding passenger doors on each side and no gangway to the next car.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: That separation means an evacuation between stations must use the side doors rather than an internal route through the train.
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
    - paragraph:
      - link "TRTC":
        - /url: /rail/operators/trtc/
      - text: "'s current network introduction describes a four-car Matra train as carrying approximately 420 people at five standing passengers per square metre."
      - superscript:
        - link "[13]":
          - /url: "#ref-13"
      - text: That is not the fleet's original interior specification. In a 2023 trial on three trains, TRTC removed 12 seats and the luggage rack from the middle area of each of cars 2 and 3, added 16 hand straps and transverse handrails, narrowed door-side rails in cars 1 and 4, and removed selected doorway poles throughout the train.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
      - text: The operator said those changes raised each trial train's approximate capacity from 400 to 420.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
    - heading "Propulsion, automation and guideway" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Each car has two separately excited, self-cooled DC traction motors with class-H insulation, and each motor armature drives through its own shaft.
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: The original system used automatic train operation without an onboard driver; DORTS published a minimum operating headway of 72 seconds.
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: TRTC now gives 80 km/h as the fleet's maximum speed and says normal operation is fully computer-controlled from the operations control centre, with manual driving available when required.
      - superscript:
        - link "[13]":
          - /url: "#ref-13"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The fleet runs on rubber tyres over dedicated running surfaces.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: Most of the original
      - link "Muzha":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br02/
      - text: alignment used guided concrete surfaces, while the later network combines reinforced-concrete and steel running surfaces.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - superscript:
        - link "[13]":
          - /url: "#ref-13"
      - text: No opened primary vehicle specification in this search gave empty mass, maximum operating speed, motor rating or a complete braking specification, so those values are not reconstructed from the old encyclopedia table.
    - heading "Commissioning fires" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Two fires during testing burned the skins at car ends before opening.
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: "DORTS's engineering account ties them directly to Taipei's novel four-car use: the original VAL arrangement contemplated one car or one two-car pair, but Matra had not coordinated propulsion and braking signals correctly across the two pairs."
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: One pair could continue driving while the other braked, leaving a brake calliper gripping its disc until heat ignited a rubber tyre.
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The same account says the underlying cause was not removed after the first fire, so a second occurred within six months.
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: DORTS then convened academic experts and Matra engineers, used simulation and verification to identify the cause, and modified the design.
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: This primary account replaces the former page's uncited shorthand and links the incident to the four-car formation itself.
    - heading "Train-control conversion" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: The original VAL 256 train-control system used fixed blocks, with wayside control units and track transmission loops carrying train-position, speed, command and voice functions.
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: The
      - link "Neihu":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br19/
      - text: extension was designed as a one-seat continuation of the Muzha railway, so the 51 old pairs and 101 new Bombardier pairs had to operate automatically over one line without a transfer.
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
    - paragraph:
      - text: DORTS therefore replaced the VAL fleet's onboard control and communication equipment and installed Bombardier Cityflo 650 moving-block control.
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: The existing Muzha points and platform doors remained but were interfaced to the new system; after cutover, DORTS says the original Matra control equipment was completely removed.
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: TRTC records all 51 converted pairs joining Wenhu Line passenger service on 26 December 2010.
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
    - heading "Refurbishment" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: An operator-authored DORTS article records renewal of the VAL 256 air-conditioning plant, replacement of T12 saloon lamps and tail lights with LEDs, and addition of automatic temperature control that could raise the setting by 1°C off peak.
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: The opened source describes these as energy-saving measures but does not provide unit-by-unit completion dates or contract values.
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
    - paragraph: The signed procurement documents, acceptance chronology, current vehicle asset register and any awarded replacement contract were not recovered in this search. Builder allocation beyond Matra, exact delivery dates by pair, present depot allocation and a confirmed withdrawal programme therefore remain TBC.

    - heading "Overview" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Contract CB370 supplied 101 married pairs, 202 cars, for the
      - link "Neihu":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br19/
      - text: extension of the former
      - link "Muzha Line":
        - /url: /rail/metro/lines/wenhu-line/
      - text: .
      - superscript:
        - link "[11]":
          - /url: "#ref-11"
      - text: "Bombardier was the electromechanical subcontractor: its scope included the new fleet, a new operations control centre, an upgraded backup control centre and new onboard train-control equipment for the 102 older cars."
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: The C370 fleet entered passenger service when the Neihu extension opened on 4 July 2009.
      - superscript:
        - link "[12]":
          - /url: "#ref-12"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The opened DORTS records call these vehicles C370, CB370 or the Bombardier fleet.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: The more specific
      - code: APM 256
      - text: product suffix remains in this page's aliases because readers use it, but no opened primary
      - link "Taipei":
        - /url: /rail/thsr/stations/taipei/
      - text: procurement or manufacturer page recovered in this search gives that exact suffix.
    - heading "Procurement and production" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: DORTS's 2005 design article planned that half the order — 101 of 202 cars — would be assembled in Taiwan.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: "A later DORTS training report, written after production began, gives a different executable split: 100 cars assembled at Bombardier's Pittsburgh plant and 102 by Tang Eng Rolling Stock Technology in Taiwan."
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: These values describe different project stages and both remain visible; the later report's 100/102 split is used in the fact box because it accounts for the completed contract quantity.
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The production chain crossed four countries. Bombardier made carbodies at Derby in the United Kingdom and bogies at Crespin in France, then sent both to Pittsburgh for equipment installation, wiring and testing before shipment to Taiwan.
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
      - text: Pittsburgh's four assembly stations progressed from mechanical equipment through couplers and interiors to underfloor equipment, tyres, static testing and finally dynamic testing on the factory test track.
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
    - heading "Formation and interoperability" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Every service train is a fixed four-car formation made from two married pairs; the cars within each pair use a semi-permanent mechanical coupler, while the outer ends carry automatic couplers.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: This direct primary statement corrects the previous page's unresolved suggestion that coupling permanence was unknown.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The new vehicles could not be treated as a separate railway. DORTS required a one-seat ride over the original and extended sections, so both the 101 new pairs and 51 old pairs had to run automatically over the whole line.
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: The legacy points and platform doors were retained and interfaced to Bombardier's Cityflo 650 moving-block control system, while the old trains received new onboard control equipment.
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
    - heading "Carbody, guidance and suspension" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Each aluminium-alloy car is 13.78 m long, 2.54 m wide and 3.53 m high.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: The body uses flame-resistant, low-smoke and low-toxicity interior materials; the floor structure was specified to resist fire for 30 minutes.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: Published empty mass remains TBC.
    - paragraph:
      - text: Each car has two single-axle bogies. Vertical dampers form the primary suspension and air springs the secondary suspension.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: External side guide wheels steer against guide rails compatible with both the original
      - link "Muzha":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/br02/
      - text: and new Neihu infrastructure; a flanged bearing lets the axle and guidance assembly rotate beneath the body.
      - superscript:
        - link "[5]":
          - /url: "#ref-5"
      - text: That official account replaces the earlier page's secondary comparison of side- and bottom-contact shoes.
    - heading "Propulsion, braking and performance" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Power is 750 V DC collected by side-contact shoes.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: Each car has two forced-cooled, four-pole AC induction motors rated at 160 hp at 1,760 rpm.
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
      - text: Bombardier packaged two variable-voltage, variable-frequency motor inverters, an auxiliary static inverter, battery charger and cooling fans in an IP56 enclosure and used IGBT control devices.
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
    - paragraph:
      - text: DORTS specifies an 80 km/h design maximum and 70 km/h operating maximum, not the 90 km/h design figure previously carried by this page.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: Normal braking blends regenerative electrical braking with air-controlled hydraulic disc brakes; every axle also has a parking brake.
      - superscript:
        - link "[3]":
          - /url: "#ref-3"
      - text: Wheel-speed comparison reduces tractive effort during spin and transfers to friction braking during detected slide before electrical braking returns.
      - superscript:
        - link "[6]":
          - /url: "#ref-6"
    - heading "Passenger systems and capacity" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Each car has four externally sliding doors, two per side, driven by DC motors.
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
      - text: Microprocessor controllers monitor direction, speed, obstacle detection and ATC commands.
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: Door-side lights flash for five seconds before opening, and multi-tone audible warnings provide an equivalent cue before opening and closing.
      - superscript:
        - link "[7]":
          - /url: "#ref-7"
      - text: Four dynamic route displays, four passenger-information screens, two emergency intercoms, CCTV and two extinguishers were specified per car.
      - superscript:
        - link "[4]":
          - /url: "#ref-4"
    - paragraph:
      - text: Capacity has an unresolved primary-source disagreement. The design paper gives 20 seats and 93 people per car at five standing passengers per square metre, which implies 372 per four-car train.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - link "TRTC":
        - /url: /rail/operators/trtc/
      - text: "'s current network introduction uses the same five-person standing density but states approximately 386 people per Bombardier train."
      - superscript:
        - link "[13]":
          - /url: "#ref-13"
      - text: The 14-person difference is not explained in either opened page, so both values are published rather than one being chosen.
    - heading "Testing and service" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: DORTS sent staff to observe bogie-frame fatigue testing at Škoda Výzkum in Prague and passenger-door endurance testing at Faiveley Transport in Paris in May–June 2005.
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: The contractor first had to submit detailed designs and approved test procedures; dye-penetrant and magnetic-particle inspections fed the bogie analysis.
      - superscript:
        - link "[9]":
          - /url: "#ref-9"
      - text: The later prototype report records static factory tests followed by dynamic running tests at Pittsburgh.
      - superscript:
        - link "[8]":
          - /url: "#ref-8"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The procurement and integration records establish operation over the whole Wenhu Line, but they do not publish a current split between Muzha and Neihu depots.
      - superscript:
        - link "[10]":
          - /url: "#ref-10"
      - text: Present depot allocation therefore remains TBC pending an operator asset roster.
