  - heading "Station context" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: Muzha sits on the southern urban corridor that the project record traces from the zoo through Wanfang Road and Xinglong Road toward the Xinhai section.
    - superscript:
      - link "[1]":
        - /url: "#ref-1"
    - text: Its station architecture belonged to CC414, the package that grouped the three southern stations and recorded a 72-metre platform for the Muzha station.
    - superscript:
      - link "[2]":
        - /url: "#ref-2"
    - text: The station’s later land-development site was on the west side of the station at the Muzha Station and Military Works Road intersection.
    - superscript:
      - link "[8]":
        - /url: "#ref-8"
    - text: DORTS records the resulting Xinyi 18 building as a project by Jun-an Construction, completed in February 2011 with three basement levels and nineteen floors above ground.
    - superscript:
      - link "[8]":
        - /url: "#ref-8"
    - text: The city’s return from that development was recorded as fifteen homes on floors fourteen to seventeen, one home on the eighteenth floor, about 3,922.66 ping and sixteen parking spaces.
    - superscript:
      - link "[8]":
        - /url: "#ref-8"
    - text: A DORTS cost-allocation table separately lists the BR2 joint-development deduction as NT$121 million in construction cost, NT$2.347 million in detailed design and NT$123.447 million in total.
    - superscript:
      - link "[10]":
        - /url: "#ref-10"
    - text: The official record does not identify the individual CC414 station contractor, award date or final package value, so those fields remain TBC here.
    - superscript:
      - link "[2]":
        - /url: "#ref-2"
    - text: A DORTS risk case records a safety net from the Muzha joint-development site falling above the elevated track and delaying a train by three minutes and nineteen seconds.
    - superscript:
      - link "[7]":
        - /url: "#ref-7"
    - text: DORTS responded by stopping the work, strengthening training and site management, and circulating the resulting rules to joint-development investors.
    - superscript:
      - link "[7]":
        - /url: "#ref-7"
    - text: The architecture brief says the twelve-station section was delivered through a systematised, modular and standardised design because its design and tender schedule was compressed.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: That standard vocabulary used curved metal-composite roofs, metal and glass envelopes, transparent lifts and platform doors, while the platforms were not air-conditioned.
    - superscript:
      - link "[6]":
        - /url: "#ref-6"
    - text: DORTS describes the Muzha section’s base colour as light blue and notes that the repeated treatment could become monotonous across the section.
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
    - text: The same review links platform-edge railings to privacy and weather concerns where elevated platforms sit close to neighbouring buildings.
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
    - text: Its rubber-tyre concrete running surface also required later repair for cracking, roughness and noise, with epoxy mortar and emery used in night work.
    - superscript:
      - link "[11]":
        - /url: "#ref-11"

    - heading "References" [level=2]
    - paragraph: 12 of 12 sources on this page are primary — published by the operator, the builder or government.
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - link "Wenhu Line project and station table":
          - /url: https://www.dorts.gov.taipei/cp.aspx?n=DBAC040496EFAB94
        - text: "文山內湖線 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-17 The full project record supports the Neihu extension’s departure from Zhongshan Junior High tail tracks, its route toward Songshan Airport, and the airport-station siting decision. The original-language wording was checked on the linked page: the paragraph beginning 內湖線為銜接木柵線 and the sentence beginning 經評估以捷運內湖線於松山機場增設車站."
      - listitem:
        - 'link "High-elevated station architectural design: station packages"':
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page75.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full page identifies the four Muzha-section station-architecture packages and lists the engineering-era station numbers and platform lengths for the six stations in this batch. The original-language paragraph beginning 文湖線木柵段分為四個設計標 was checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - 'link "High-elevated station architectural design: design constraints"':
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page76.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full page describes the road-centre and single-column station forms, the route’s urban constraints, and the use of systematised, modular and standardised design for the twelve-station Muzha section. The original-language paragraphs beginning 車站型式 and 木柵線全線12座車站 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - 'link "High-elevated station architectural design: materials and public response"':
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page80.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full page describes the Muzha section’s aluminium-panel, laminated-glass, curved-roof and frame vocabulary, and records the author’s criticism that the final details did not achieve the intended lightweight transparency. The original-language paragraphs beginning 木柵線車站外觀 and 原設計理念 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - 'link "High-elevated station architectural design: colour and platform-edge treatment"':
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page82.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full page records the Muzha section’s light-blue base colour and discusses platform-edge railings, adjacent-building privacy, weather exposure and the later Neihu response. The original-language paragraphs beginning 木柵段車站基本色 and 月臺邊緣欄杆 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - 'link "High-elevated station architectural design: station form"':
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page84.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full page describes Muzha-section elevated side-platform stations, platform doors, the absence of air-conditioning, curved metal-composite roofs, metal-and-glass envelopes and transparent lifts. The original-language paragraph beginning 木柵段車站均為高架側式月臺 was checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Rapid-transit joint-development risk cases":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/JRTST/ebook/no45/files/basic-html/page143.html
        - text: 捷運土地開發風險管理案例 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full technical-journal page records a falling safety net from the Muzha joint-development site that delayed a train, and the Wanfang Community joint-development noise case that led to airtight-window requirements and a later DORTS control procedure. The original-language entries beginning 木柵線木柵站聯開工程 and 文湖線萬芳社區聯合開發大樓噪音案 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Wenhu Line completed land-development sites":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no19/files/basic-html/page124.html
        - text: 捷運土地開發實務 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full land-development volume records the investors, locations, completion dates, building forms and Taipei City property shares for the Wanfang Community, Muzha and Linguang development sites. The original-language entries beginning 萬芳社區站（交十二）, 木柵站（交十三） and 麟光站（交九） were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Basic design of rapid-transit development buildings":

        - text: 捷運開發大樓基本設計概要 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full page distinguishes co-constructed and separately constructed development buildings and names the Wanfang Community station site as a separate-structure example, including the construction-sequencing and worksite-safety implications. The original-language paragraph beginning 分構案例如 was checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Taipei rapid-transit property-cost record":
          - /url: https://www.laws.taipei.gov.tw/Law/LawSearch/LawArticleContent/FL013179?date=20060227
        - text: 臺北市政府捷運工程局辦理臺北都會區大眾捷運系統財產列計注意事項 primary Taipei City Legal Affairs Department accessed 2026-08-18 The full official legal-system page reproduces DORTS’s cost-allocation example for CC409 and its table of joint-development deductions for BR2, BR5 and BR6. The original-language table beginning 聯合開發應予扣除之費用 was checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Wenhu Line concrete running-surface maintenance":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/JRTST/ebook/no39/files/basic-html/page252.html
        - text: 文湖線膠輪混凝土軌道面維修實務 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full technical-journal page records the Muzha section’s concrete running-surface dimensions, early spalling, cracking, roughness and noise problems, and the repair method and maintenance-cost comparison. The original-language paragraphs beginning 木柵線膠輪軌道面 and 維修工法 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "TRTC station accessibility records":
          - /url: https://web.metro.taipei/pages/tw/stationdisabledinfo/
        - text: 車站無障礙設施查詢 primary Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation ( 臺北大眾捷運股份有限公司 ) accessed 2026-08-24 TRTC’s stationdisabledinfo API was fetched for all 121 station records returned by its station-label endpoint. The API publishes station-specific lift/ramp locations, accessible-toilet locations, tactile-paving and stair anti-slip fields. It does not publish nursing-room or platform-gap fields; those remain TBC here.

      - link "[12]":
        - /url: "#ref-12"
    - text: TRTC’s current page places the Wenhu and Bannan transfer corridor near Exit 2 and records separate paid-area facilities for the two lines.
    - superscript:
      - link "[13]":
        - /url: "#ref-13"
    - text: The joint-development site covers the southwest side of the Zhongxiao East Road Section 3 and Fuxing South Road intersection, with a total development area of 7,691 square metres.
    - superscript:
      - link "[10]":
        - /url: "#ref-10"
    - text: DORTS’s concept design joined the building’s first through third floors to the Wenhu facilities and its basement levels one through three to the Bannan entrances.
    - superscript:
      - link "[10]":
        - /url: "#ref-10"
    - text: The city published the development plan in November 1997, sought investors in March 1999, signed the investment contract in January 2000 and recorded completion and an occupancy permit in November 2006.
    - superscript:
      - link "[10]":
        - /url: "#ref-10"
    - text: The project was planned for retail and department-store use, with public paid parking and reserved connections to the rapid-transit facilities.
    - superscript:
      - link "[10]":
        - /url: "#ref-10"
    - text: DORTS later described the Zhongxiao Fuxing building as one of the larger city-managed development assets and recorded a unified-management model with investor Hongtong.
    - superscript:
      - link "[11]":
        - /url: "#ref-11"
    - text: The same management record says the original proposal had six basement levels and thirteen floors above ground, but the transit mezzanine was counted as an additional floor, producing a six-basement, fourteen-floor design.
    - superscript:
      - link "[11]":
        - /url: "#ref-11"
    - text: The common Muzha station design used curved roofs, aluminium panels, laminated glass, platform doors and transparent lifts, with no platform air-conditioning.
    - superscript:
      - link "[6]":
        - /url: "#ref-6"
    - text: DORTS later judged that the heavy outer frames reduced the intended lightweight transparency of the standardised station image.
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
    - text: The live TRTC log records a 2 August 2026 signalling anomaly in the Zhongxiao Fuxing section that briefly stopped trains for about two minutes while the rest of the line remained unaffected.
    - superscript:
      - link "[14]":
        - /url: "#ref-14"
    - text: The same log records a 5 August passenger medical emergency at the station; the system continued normal operation while station staff used an AED assessment and CPR before handing over to paramedics.
    - superscript:
      - link "[14]":
        - /url: "#ref-14"
    - text: The Muzha section opened on 28 March 1996 as Taiwan’s first driverless medium-capacity metro.
    - superscript:
      - link "[9]":
        - /url: "#ref-9"
    - text: The individual CC403 contractor, award date and final station-package value are not identified in the full primary pages checked here, so those fields remain TBC.
    - superscript:
      - link "[2]":
        - /url: "#ref-2"

        - text: "文山內湖線 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-17 The full project record supports the Neihu extension’s departure from Zhongshan Junior High tail tracks, its route toward Songshan Airport, and the airport-station siting decision.       - listitem:
        - 'link "High-elevated station architectural design: station packages"':
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page75.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full page identifies the four Muzha-section station-architecture packages and lists the engineering-era station numbers and platform lengths for the six stations in this batch. The original-language paragraph beginning 文湖線木柵段分為四個設計標 was checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - 'link "High-elevated station architectural design: design constraints"':
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page76.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full page describes the road-centre and single-column station forms, the route’s urban constraints, and the use of systematised, modular and standardised design for the twelve-station Muzha section. The original-language paragraphs beginning 車站型式 and 木柵線全線12座車站 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - 'link "High-elevated station architectural design: alignment history"':
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page78.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full page records the proposed Dunhua alignment, its change to Fuxing South and North Roads, and the design pressures of narrow streets and dense commercial and residential frontage. The original-language paragraphs beginning 原規劃路線 and 由於敦化南北路 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - 'link "High-elevated station architectural design: materials and public response"':

        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full page describes the Muzha section’s aluminium-panel, laminated-glass, curved-roof and frame vocabulary, and records the author’s criticism that the final details did not achieve the intended lightweight transparency. The original-language paragraphs beginning 木柵線車站外觀 and 原設計理念 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - 'link "High-elevated station architectural design: station form"':

        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full page describes Muzha-section elevated side-platform stations, platform doors, the absence of air-conditioning, curved metal-composite roofs, metal-and-glass envelopes and transparent lifts.   - heading "Station context" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: The Muzha project begins at the zoo and runs through Xinguang Road, Wanfang Road, Xinglong Road and Xinhai Road before turning toward the central city.
    - superscript:
      - link "[1]":
        - /url: "#ref-1"
    - text: DORTS placed the Muzha depot near the zoo exit on about 6.2 hectares, combining train storage, maintenance, control, washing, wayside maintenance and parts warehousing.
    - superscript:
      - link "[1]":
        - /url: "#ref-1"
    - text: That depot relationship made the zoo station the public-facing beginning of a line whose operating infrastructure was concentrated beside its southern terminus.
    - superscript:
      - link "[1]":
        - /url: "#ref-1"
    - text: The architecture volume says the first medium-capacity line had to fit stations into existing urban roads while limiting the visual and structural burden placed on neighbouring buildings.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: Its two station families used either a single-column cantilever arrangement or a conventional beam-and-column frame, selected according to the available site.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: Because all twelve Muzha stations had to be designed, tendered and built on a compressed schedule, DORTS adopted a systematised, modular and standardised design approach.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: The architecture package covering the southern three stations was CC414, whose engineering-era list gives the zoo station a 70-metre platform.
    - superscript:
      - link "[2]":
        - /url: "#ref-2"
    - text: The wider construction arrangement separated system turnkey work from domestically bid civil, architectural, tunnel and depot work, while the operating contract was a separate part of the project structure.
    - superscript:
      - link "[7]":
        - /url: "#ref-7"
    - text: The line’s rubber-tyre trains run on concrete running surfaces, so the station approaches share the section’s problems of spalling, cracking, roughness and noise that DORTS later addressed with night maintenance.
    - superscript:
      - link "[9]":
        - /url: "#ref-9"
    - text: The original station vocabulary used aluminium panels, laminated glass, curved roofs and structural frames to present a modern, lightweight image.
    - superscript:
      - link "[4]":
        - /url: "#ref-4"
    - text: DORTS later acknowledged that frame thickness and detail choices kept the built result from achieving the intended degree of visual transparency and drew less public acceptance than hoped.
    - superscript:
      - link "[4]":
        - /url: "#ref-4"
    - text: The Muzha stations were designed as elevated side-platform stations with platform doors, curved metal-composite roofs, metal-and-glass envelopes and transparent lifts, without air-conditioning on the platforms.
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
    - text: The line opened on 28 March 1996 as Taiwan’s first driverless medium-capacity metro, recording 42,548 rides on its first day.
    - superscript:
      - link "[6]":
        - /url: "#ref-6"
    - text: "Its opening landscaping was also treated as a project responsibility: DORTS was directed to fund and commission planting restoration along the route after the city’s landscape office selected the transplant sites."
    - superscript:
      - link "[6]":
        - /url: "#ref-6"

  - heading "Station context" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: "Songshan Airport was not part of the first Neihu alignment: the project record says the Ministry of Transportation ordered a feasibility study in ROC 89 (2000) for a station that would directly serve airport trips."
    - superscript:
      - link "[1]":
        - /url: "#ref-1"
    - text: DORTS reports that the evaluation found an airport station on the Neihu Line more feasible in engineering terms and compatible with the construction schedule, after which the route was adjusted and the station added.
    - superscript:
      - link "[1]":
        - /url: "#ref-1"
    - text: The same project record says the Executive Yuan agreed in principle in ROC 90 (2001), the Public Construction Commission agreed to the funding arrangement in ROC 91 (2002), and the revised project cost was NT$60.997 billion.
    - superscript:
      - link "[1]":
        - /url: "#ref-1"
    - text: The route leaves its elevated approach at Minzu East Road, enters the airport, and places the station beneath the surface car park in front of the terminal building.
    - superscript:
      - link "[1]":
        - /url: "#ref-1"
    - text: The project table identifies the airport station as BR1 in the Neihu engineering sequence, while the operating station is BR13 ; the two identifiers belong to different numbering systems.
    - superscript:
      - link "[1]":
        - /url: "#ref-1"
    - text: The CB420 section starts east of the station, uses shield tunnels below Songshan Airport, crosses the expressway and Keelung River, reaches Dazhi, and continues to the point where the line emerges for its elevated section.
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
    - text: That section is about 3,460 metres long, with separate airport tunnel drives of 1,241 metres and 1,286 metres for the down and up lines.
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
    - text: The two drives passed below the runway, apron and taxiway, and the published cover decreases from 27.8 metres near the Huajiang Street ventilation shaft to 18.8 metres at the airport-station end.
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
    - text: DORTS records the airport crossing as Taipei Basin K1 lake-deposit ground, with a 50-to-60-metre layer of very soft silty clay whose low self-support and sensitivity made settlement a central construction concern.
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
    - text: Because airport rules constrained when workers could enter and observe the site, the monitoring system combined automatic reading and transmission with manual observation during the night-time airport closure.
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
    - text: The down-line shield drive launched on 8 October 2003 and reached the station diaphragm wall on 30 June 2004; the up-line drive launched on 8 September 2004 and arrived on 7 September 2005.
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
    - text: DORTS’s architecture account calls the station’s design concept “A Story of Flight”, using spiral-wing steel roofs to link the entrances and accessible lift and to suggest a pair of wings waiting to depart.
    - superscript:
      - link "[2]":
        - /url: "#ref-2"
    - text: That account also describes a ground plaza, water feature and curved ventilation-shaft wall as a combined place for activity, rest and artistic work rather than treating the entrance as only a circulation object.
    - superscript:
      - link "[2]":
        - /url: "#ref-2"
    - text: The official art table records Great Age of Travel at Exit 3, Flight Plan on the concourse wall and Dream Flight in the platform void, completed in October 2008 through open selection.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: DORTS’s broader public-art record says Neihu works other than the donated Gangqian piece were funded through the Neihu Line construction budget, with DORTS handling selection and valuation and its eastern works office handling contracts, material subsidies and implementation.
    - superscript:
      - link "[4]":
        - /url: "#ref-4"
    - text: The checked CB420 and project pages identify the section and programme but do not publish an individual station contractor, award date or final station-package value, so those fields remain TBC.
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"

  - heading "Station context" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: Jiannan Road is the first elevated station in the Neihu section, positioned east of the Ziqiang Tunnel roundabout where the buried alignment has returned to the surface.
    - superscript:
      - link "[6]":
        - /url: "#ref-6"
    - text: The CB423 work-scope table assigns the B2–B5 station group and its connecting elevated bridge to one construction package under design package DB145.
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
    - text: The technical station record describes B2 as an east–west elevated side-platform station at the east side of the Beian Road and Ziqiang Tunnel intersection, with an approximately 99-metre station body and an 83-metre platform.
    - superscript:
      - link "[6]":
        - /url: "#ref-6"
    - text: The engineering volume also treats the B2 station’s western and eastern turnout areas as special bridge units, alongside the regular prestressed U-girder spans used between road crossings.
    - superscript:
      - link "[6]":
        - /url: "#ref-6"
    - text: DORTS places B2 through B5 in the Neihu corridor’s residential–rural landscape zone, a classification that includes some commercial activity but treats the surrounding character as the quieter part of the district.
    - superscript:
      - link "[8]":
        - /url: "#ref-8"
    - text: The architecture volume connects that zone to Neihu’s former agricultural landscape, its mountains and the Keelung River, and uses the shared “Lake-City Story” theme to link architecture, landscape and public art.
    - superscript:
      - link "[7]":
        - /url: "#ref-7"
    - text: For Jiannan Road specifically, the station theme is “Mountain Ridge” and the associated colour is rice-scent green, a deliberate reference to the local mountain and rural setting.
    - superscript:
      - link "[9]":
        - /url: "#ref-9"
    - text: The station-front plaza was planned as an open urban space for transfers, waiting, gathering and crossing, while also providing room for local activities rather than being only a forecourt.
    - superscript:
      - link "[12]":
        - /url: "#ref-12"
    - text: Its paving uses free curves to evoke mountain contours together with a gridded pattern recalling agricultural fields, and the design called for a public-art competition whose work would express Neihu’s natural and human history.
    - superscript:
      - link "[12]":
        - /url: "#ref-12"
    - text: The official art table records Frog’s Sky at the columns and ceiling beside Exit 2, completed in April 2009 by Chen Chien through open selection, with a listed cost of NT$6 million.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: The work’s recorded materials include stainless-steel cable, mirror-finished steel, transparent panels, mirror film, LED tube lights and stone, a material palette that extends the station’s designed relationship between structure and landscape.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: Across the elevated section, DORTS’s design system applies the route colour to platform-door and wayfinding elements while using station colours on columns, paving, wall panels, floors and doors.
    - superscript:
      - link "[10]":
        - /url: "#ref-10"
    - text: The station’s rounded raised arches were described as a mountain-city and gateway-to-Neihu image, while the internal lighting was intended to read like a lantern at night.
    - superscript:
      - link "[11]":
        - /url: "#ref-11"
    - text: The checked CB423 records establish the station group and structure but do not publish an individual station contractor, award date or final package value, so those fields remain TBC.
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"

    - heading "References" [level=2]
    - paragraph: 13 of 13 sources on this page are primary — published by the operator, the builder or government.
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - link "Wenhu Line project and station table":
          - /url: https://www.dorts.gov.taipei/cp.aspx?n=DBAC040496EFAB94
        - text: "文山內湖線 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-17 The full project record supports the Neihu extension’s departure from Zhongshan Junior High tail tracks, its route toward Songshan Airport, and the airport-station siting decision. The original-language wording was checked on the linked page: the paragraph beginning 內湖線為銜接木柵線 and the sentence beginning 經評估以捷運內湖線於松山機場增設車站."
      - listitem:
        - link "Wenhu Line station architecture":
          - /url: https://www.dorts.gov.taipei/cp.aspx?n=980C85299DA2890A&s=6B0F524CA1EB5C9F
        - text: "車站建築設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-17 The full architecture record explains the Muzha-section constraints illustrated by Zhongshan Junior High, identifies Dazhi as the Neihu section’s underground station, and documents the special station design treatment. The original-language wording was checked on the linked page: the paragraph beginning 文湖線初期路線(木柵段) and the sentence beginning 除大直站為地下車站外."
      - listitem:
        - link "Wenhu Line public-art table":
          - /url: https://www.dorts.gov.taipei/cp.aspx?n=EF3512A90C6BCFD2&s=E45C77C5F722B310
        - text: 公共藝術總表 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-17 The full official table supports the Wenhu entries for Songshan Airport, Jiannan Road, Xihu, Gangqian, Wende, Dahu Park, Donghu and Nangang Exhibition Center, including completion dates, locations, titles, authors, descriptions and selection methods. The original-language rows were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Neihu Line public-art selection and implementation":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no2/files/basic-html/page257.html
        - text: 捷運車站規劃與設計實務 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full page lists the Neihu station design-topic summary, records the executed-artwork selection methods, explains that the original wall-art installations at Gangqian and Huzhou were cancelled after design changes because the walls were incomplete, explains the later donated Gangqian work, and states how DORTS handled selection, material subsidy and implementation. The original-language paragraphs beginning 各站公共藝術之設置地點及徵選方式, 原擬於文德站、港墘站及葫洲站 and 港墘站之作品為捐贈 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "CB423 station and viaduct contract scope":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no32/files/basic-html/page22.html
        - text: 捷運高架橋梁結構設計與施工 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full technical volume’s work-scope table assigns B2–B5 stations and the connecting elevated bridge to CB423 under design package DB145. The original-language table beginning 文湖線內湖段各施工標工作範圍 was checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "CB423 station structures and sites":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no32/files/basic-html/page23.html
        - text: 捷運高架橋梁結構設計與施工 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full technical volume gives B2 as the first Neihu elevated station, gives the B2–B5 station orientations, platform forms and dimensions, the Xihu market and parking-site interface, and the CB423 bridge methods and spans. The original-language entries beginning 一、B2 劍南路站 and 二、B3 西湖站 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Neihu Line environmental and human context":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page88.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full architecture volume records Neihu’s mountains, Keelung River, former agricultural economy, later urbanisation, parks, community activities and the shared Lake-City Story theme used across architecture, landscape, interiors and public art. The original-language paragraphs beginning 內湖區位於臺北市地理位置 and 湖城故事 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Neihu Line corridor design zones":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page91.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full architecture volume places B2–B5 in the residential–rural landscape zone, describes the Xihu-area reclaimed land beside the river, and distinguishes B6–B9 as a commercial-recreation zone and B10–B11 as an industrial-technology zone. The original-language headings beginning 住宅城鄉風貌, 商業休閒環境 and 工業科技景觀 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Neihu Line station themes and colours":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page95.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full architecture volume’s station-theme table records the B2–B11 themes and associated colours, including B6’s Market/wine red, B7’s Recreation/sapphire blue, B8’s Dance/purple, B9’s Music/blue-grey, B10’s Digital/silver-grey and B11’s Light-and-shadow/silver-white. The original-language table beginning 各車站設計主題及色彩 was checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Neihu Line station form and environmental detailing":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page97.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full architecture volume explains how route colour and station colour are applied to columns, paving, wall panels, floors and doors, and illustrates the B2–B5 station forms. The original-language paragraphs beginning 各車站之色彩計畫 and 內湖段之車站為高架車站 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Neihu Line station forms and Jiannan Road landmark":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no2/files/basic-html/page177.html
        - text: 捷運車站規劃與設計實務 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full planning volume describes the Neihu elevated stations’ standard curved-column, metal-roof, glass-and-metal form, identifies Dahu Park’s mast-and-sail form beside the park, and identifies Jiannan Road’s raised round arches, mountain-city gateway image and lantern-like night lighting. The original-language paragraphs beginning 內湖線, 大湖公園站 and 劍南路站 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Jiannan Road station plaza landscape":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page156.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full architecture volume describes Jiannan Road’s station-front plaza, public open-space role, public-art competition, planting and paving that evokes mountain contours and agricultural grids. The original-language paragraphs beginning 劍南路站廣場景觀 and 為了表現本站山陵 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "TRTC station accessibility records":
          - /url: https://web.metro.taipei/pages/tw/stationdisabledinfo/
        - text: 車站無障礙設施查詢 primary Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation ( 臺北大眾捷運股份有限公司 ) accessed 2026-08-24 TRTC’s stationdisabledinfo API was fetched for all 121 station records returned by its station-label endpoint. The API publishes station-specific lift/ramp locations, accessible-toilet locations, tactile-paving and stair anti-slip fields. It does not publish nursing-room or platform-gap fields; those remain TBC here.

  - heading "Station context" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: The current DORTS project table maps Donghu to engineering station B9, and the CB424 record includes B9 in the four-station elevated package covering B6–B9.
    - superscript:
      - link "[1]":
        - /url: "#ref-1"
    - text: B9 is on 25-metre Kangning Road 3, near Lane 245, on transport land to the northeast.
    - superscript:
      - link "[2]":
        - /url: "#ref-2"
    - text: The technical record describes a northeast–southwest elevated side platform, a 93-metre station body 20.6 metres wide and an 83-metre platform.
    - superscript:
      - link "[2]":
        - /url: "#ref-2"
    - text: DORTS treats B9 as part of the commercial-and-recreation corridor along Chenggong and Kangning Roads, where the broader account also records Dahu Park’s recreational role and nearby infrastructure.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: B9’s theme is Music, with a blue-grey station colour and a design reference to the Keelung River and sky.
    - superscript:
      - link "[4]":
        - /url: "#ref-4"
    - text: The shared elevated-station design keeps circulation semi-open and uses glass, enamelled steel and natural ventilation to reduce the visual and structural heaviness of a station above the road.
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
    - text: B9 is among the side-platform stations for which DORTS documented rainwater falling from the platform edge onto metal cladding and prescribed flashing and maintenance procedures.
    - superscript:
      - link "[6]":
        - /url: "#ref-6"
    - text: "Lake Ripples at Exit 3 turns the wall into DORTS’s “lake city story”: wind and rain create overlapping ripples that stand for shared memory in a city with lakes."
    - superscript:
      - link "[9]":
        - /url: "#ref-9"
    - text: The official art table records the work in March 2009 on the exterior wall at Exit 3, by Wu Shui-yi and Yang De-yi, using ceramic with celadon glaze through open selection at a listed cost of NT$2,300,000.
    - superscript:
      - link "[9]":
        - /url: "#ref-9"
    - text: The public-art chapter’s executed list also records Donghu as an open-selection station, separate from the topic summary used to frame the line’s design themes.
    - superscript:
      - link "[8]":
        - /url: "#ref-8"
    - text: The station-colour plan separates the brown line colour used in platform-door and sign systems from each station’s own colour treatment across selected finishes.
    - superscript:
      - link "[7]":
        - /url: "#ref-7"
    - text: The fetched CB424 record identifies the station package and dimensions but does not publish an individual contractor, award date or final station-package value; those fields remain TBC.
    - superscript:
      - link "[2]":
        - /url: "#ref-2"

      - listitem:
        - link "Wenhu Line project and station table":
          - /url: https://www.dorts.gov.taipei/cp.aspx?n=DBAC040496EFAB94
        - text: "文山內湖線 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-17 The full project record supports the Neihu extension’s departure from Zhongshan Junior High tail tracks, its route toward Songshan Airport, and the airport-station siting decision. The original-language wording was checked on the linked page: the paragraph beginning 內湖線為銜接木柵線 and the sentence beginning 經評估以捷運內湖線於松山機場增設車站."
      - listitem:
        - link "CB424 and CB425 station structures and sites":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no32/files/basic-html/page24.html
        - text: 捷運高架橋梁結構設計與施工 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full technical volume gives B7, B8 and B9 station sites, orientations, platform forms and dimensions, describes the approximately 4 km CB424 bridge, and begins the CB425 records for B10 and B11. The original-language entries beginning B7大湖公園站 and B10南港軟體園區站 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Neihu Line corridor design zones":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page91.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full architecture volume places B2–B5 in the residential–rural landscape zone, describes the Xihu-area reclaimed land beside the river, and distinguishes B6–B9 as a commercial-recreation zone and B10–B11 as an industrial-technology zone. The original-language headings beginning 住宅城鄉風貌, 商業休閒環境 and 工業科技景觀 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Neihu Line station themes and colours":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page95.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full architecture volume’s station-theme table records the B2–B11 themes and associated colours, including B6’s Market/wine red, B7’s Recreation/sapphire blue, B8’s Dance/purple, B9’s Music/blue-grey, B10’s Digital/silver-grey and B11’s Light-and-shadow/silver-white. The original-language table beginning 各車站設計主題及色彩 was checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Neihu Line elevated-station design principles":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page93.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full architecture volume describes the shared materials, platform-space form, overpass, semi-open edges, natural ventilation and “same within difference” approach of the elevated Neihu stations. The original-language paragraphs beginning 特殊站在建築語彙上 and 車站穿透與輕巧之構想 were checked on the linked page.

  - heading "Station context" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: The current DORTS project table maps Taipei Nangang Exhibition Center to engineering station B11, and the CB425 record identifies it as the southern station of the Nangang package.
    - superscript:
      - link "[1]":
        - /url: "#ref-1"
    - text: The station sits on the north side of Nangang Road at the southern end of the Nangang Economic and Trade Park, across a 30-metre road from the park and beside commercial land.
    - superscript:
      - link "[2]":
        - /url: "#ref-2"
    - text: It is recorded as an east–west elevated island-platform interchange station with east and west entrances; the station body is 128 metres long and 18.6 metres wide, with an 83-metre platform.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: The technical record also describes a parallel stacked structural exchange with future BL18 , one emergency exit, and an underground passage level connecting toward BL18 and the exhibition-centre underground walkway.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: The associated CB425 viaduct is recorded at approximately 1.9 kilometres and crosses the Keelung River, the Zhongshan Expressway and Jingmao 1 Road.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: DORTS places B11 in the industrial-and-technology landscape zone and describes the surrounding economic-and-trade park as important to Nangang’s development and urban economic potential.
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
    - text: DORTS’s local design brief ties the station to Nangang Software Park, Nangang Economic and Trade Park, and Academia Sinica, setting the theme “digital space, e-station” to express the surrounding technology landscape.
    - superscript:
      - link "[4]":
        - /url: "#ref-4"
    - text: The same brief uses dawn blue and light, thin, transparent materials, with barcode imagery, to make the station read as an urban technology landmark.
    - superscript:
      - link "[4]":
        - /url: "#ref-4"
    - text: The broader station-theme table names B11 Light and Shadow, uses silver-white, and links the treatment to technological feeling and the transparency of light.
    - superscript:
      - link "[6]":
        - /url: "#ref-6"
    - text: Unlike the eight side-platform stations, B11 is one of the two island-platform stations excluded from DORTS’s platform-edge water-stain problem.
    - superscript:
      - link "[8]":
        - /url: "#ref-8"
    - text: "The official art table treats Light Gaps, Glimpses, and River in the Sky as a three-work ensemble: entrance columns form a visual landmark, the wall interacts with moving passengers, and the platform skylight carries water, light, and motion."
    - superscript:
      - link "[10]":
        - /url: "#ref-10"
    - text: DORTS records the ensemble in October 2008 at the west-plaza columns, south outdoor pool and platform skylight, with ceramic panels, mosaic, stainless steel and painted acrylic glass, a listed cost of NT$5,999,868, and open selection.
    - superscript:
      - link "[10]":
        - /url: "#ref-10"
    - text: The fetched CB425 pages identify the interchange and viaduct context but do not publish an individual station contractor, award date or final station-package value; those fields remain TBC.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"

    - heading "References" [level=2]
    - paragraph: 11 of 11 sources on this page are primary — published by the operator, the builder or government.
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - link "Wenhu Line project and station table":
          - /url: https://www.dorts.gov.taipei/cp.aspx?n=DBAC040496EFAB94
        - text: "文山內湖線 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-17 The full project record supports the Neihu extension’s departure from Zhongshan Junior High tail tracks, its route toward Songshan Airport, and the airport-station siting decision. The original-language wording was checked on the linked page: the paragraph beginning 內湖線為銜接木柵線 and the sentence beginning 經評估以捷運內湖線於松山機場增設車站."
      - listitem:
        - link "CB424 and CB425 station structures and sites":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no32/files/basic-html/page24.html
        - text: 捷運高架橋梁結構設計與施工 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full technical volume gives B7, B8 and B9 station sites, orientations, platform forms and dimensions, describes the approximately 4 km CB424 bridge, and begins the CB425 records for B10 and B11. The original-language entries beginning B7大湖公園站 and B10南港軟體園區站 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "CB425 Nangang station structures and viaduct":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no32/files/basic-html/page25.html
        - text: 捷運高架橋梁結構設計與施工 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full technical volume completes the B11 record with its emergency exit, underground mechanical and passage levels, BL18 and exhibition-centre walkway connections, body dimensions and platform length, and describes the approximately 1.9 km CB425 bridge and its crossings. The original-language paragraphs beginning B11南港展覽館站 and CB425標高架橋工程 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Nangang Exhibition Center Station architecture":
          - /url: https://www.dorts.gov.taipei/cp.aspx?n=980C85299DA2890A&s=30FCACCAB334BFA2
        - text: 南港展覽館站 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-17 The full station architecture record supports the station’s technology-park context, its digital-space theme, its dawn-blue palette, its light and transparent materials, and its barcode imagery. The original-language paragraphs were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Neihu Line corridor design zones":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page91.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full architecture volume places B2–B5 in the residential–rural landscape zone, describes the Xihu-area reclaimed land beside the river, and distinguishes B6–B9 as a commercial-recreation zone and B10–B11 as an industrial-technology zone. The original-language headings beginning 住宅城鄉風貌, 商業休閒環境 and 工業科技景觀 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Neihu Line station themes and colours":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page95.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full architecture volume’s station-theme table records the B2–B11 themes and associated colours, including B6’s Market/wine red, B7’s Recreation/sapphire blue, B8’s Dance/purple, B9’s Music/blue-grey, B10’s Digital/silver-grey and B11’s Light-and-shadow/silver-white. The original-language table beginning 各車站設計主題及色彩 was checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Neihu Line elevated-station design principles":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page93.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full architecture volume describes the shared materials, platform-space form, overpass, semi-open edges, natural ventilation and “same within difference” approach of the elevated Neihu stations. The original-language paragraphs beginning 特殊站在建築語彙上 and 車站穿透與輕巧之構想 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Neihu Line platform-edge design review":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page131.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full architecture volume distinguishes the Xihu and Nangang Exhibition Center island-platform stations from the eight side-platform stations and records the platform-edge rain-stain and glass-cover design review. The original-language paragraph beginning 除了西湖站及南港展覽館站 was checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Neihu Line station form and environmental detailing":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no34/files/basic-html/page97.html
        - text: 捷運高架車站建築造型設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-18 The full architecture volume explains how route colour and station colour are applied to columns, paving, wall panels, floors and doors, and illustrates the B2–B5 station forms. The original-language paragraphs beginning 各車站之色彩計畫 and 內湖段之車站為高架車站 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Wenhu Line public-art table":
          - /url: https://www.dorts.gov.taipei/cp.aspx?n=EF3512A90C6BCFD2&s=E45C77C5F722B310
        - text: 公共藝術總表 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems accessed 2026-08-17 The full official table supports the Wenhu entries for Songshan Airport, Jiannan Road, Xihu, Gangqian, Wende, Dahu Park, Donghu and Nangang Exhibition Center, including completion dates, locations, titles, authors, descriptions and selection methods. The original-language rows were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "TRTC station accessibility records":
          - /url: https://web.metro.taipei/pages/tw/stationdisabledinfo/
        - text: 車站無障礙設施查詢 primary Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation ( 臺北大眾捷運股份有限公司 ) accessed 2026-08-24 TRTC’s stationdisabledinfo API was fetched for all 121 station records returned by its station-label endpoint. The API publishes station-specific lift/ramp locations, accessible-toilet locations, tactile-paving and stair anti-slip fields. It does not publish nursing-room or platform-gap fields; those remain TBC here.

    - text: Station order is the operator’s published LB01–LB12 sequence. Coordinates come from the official New Taipei landmark records, converted from their published TWD97 fields to WGS84 for display.

  - heading "Station context" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: "At LB01 , DORTS presents A Beautiful Journey as an interchange walk: wall lighting and mosaic ceramic panels linked to train information turn the passage into a flowing river of light."
    - superscript:
      - link "[8]":
        - /url: "#ref-8"
    - text: The project route record places LB01 in Tucheng’s Central Road Section 4 and identifies the station as the Sanying Line’s connection to the existing Bannan Line Dingpu station.
    - superscript:
      - link "[7]":
        - /url: "#ref-7"
    - text: DORTS describes the Sanying platform as ground-level three while the Bannan platform is underground three, making this a vertically stacked interchange rather than a same-level transfer.
    - superscript:
      - link "[11]":
        - /url: "#ref-11"
    - text: The same interchange announcement records eight direct escalators, arranged as four up and four down, and two lifts serving the direct connection between the lines.
    - superscript:
      - link "[11]":
        - /url: "#ref-11"
    - text: That announcement states a transfer time of under two minutes for the direct route, while the operator’s actual passenger walking time is not independently established here.
    - superscript:
      - link "[11]":
        - /url: "#ref-11"
    - text: A 2024 construction notice records that the transfer facility was still being built between the two systems and temporarily closed Bannan exit 3 while the work proceeded.
    - superscript:
      - link "[12]":
        - /url: "#ref-12"
    - text: The notice describes the construction path from the Bannan station’s underground level three by escalator or lift to Sanying’s ground-level three, which explains why the public route is distinct from a street transfer.
    - superscript:
      - link "[12]":
        - /url: "#ref-12"
    - text: DORTS’ station-design record describes an elevated side platform closely integrated with the existing Dingpu station and shared entrances.
    - superscript:
      - link "[13]":
        - /url: "#ref-13"
    - text: It frames the station as an urban greenhouse, using planting, a long-span structure, a semi-transparent expanded-metal façade, daylight and natural ventilation as parts of the design brief.
    - superscript:
      - link "[13]":
        - /url: "#ref-13"
    - text: The line’s public-art index describes the wider project as 14.29 kilometres with 12 elevated stations, placing LB01 ’s interchange work inside a line-wide rather than underground station programme.
    - superscript:
      - link "[9]":
        - /url: "#ref-9"
    - text: The builder’s engineering documentary says the elevated alignment crosses national and railway infrastructure, the Dahan and Sanxia rivers and Yingge Creek.
    - superscript:
      - link "[10]":
        - /url: "#ref-10"
    - text: For railway crossings, it records a fish-fin bridge, protective base plates, railway supervision and a night operation with a TRA power-off section.
    - superscript:
      - link "[10]":
        - /url: "#ref-10"
    - text: Those controls describe line-level construction risk and should not be read as evidence that a particular LB01 structural incident occurred.
    - superscript:
      - link "[10]":
        - /url: "#ref-10"
    - text: The public-art record establishes the artists and the interchange-passage media for A Beautiful Journey, but the fetched records do not establish a separate LB01 art cost or a civil construction contract value.
    - superscript:
      - link "[8]":
        - /url: "#ref-8"
    - text: No fetched primary record in this batch establishes an LB01 rename, a separate station architect, or a station-specific feeder-bus stop-ID join, so those fields remain TBC.
    - superscript:
      - link "[7]":
        - /url: "#ref-7"

    - text: That article gives seven minutes as the planned walking time from the station toward the museum, which is a design target rather than a measured current journey time.
    - superscript:
      - link "[13]":
        - /url: "#ref-13"
    - text: The builder public-art index places Yingge within the 14.29-kilometre, 12-station elevated Sanying project.
    - superscript:
      - link "[8]":
        - /url: "#ref-8"
    - text: The engineering documentary says the elevated line crosses national and railway infrastructure and the Dahan, Sanxia and Yingge waterways.
    - superscript:
      - link "[11]":
        - /url: "#ref-11"
    - text: Its railway-crossing account records a fish-fin bridge, a protective base plate, railway supervision and a night TRA power-off operation.
    - superscript:
      - link "[11]":
        - /url: "#ref-11"
    - text: These are line-level construction controls and do not establish an LB08 -specific structural incident.
    - superscript:
      - link "[11]":
        - /url: "#ref-11"
    - text: The individual LB08 art record names Tao Xiang and describes a practical lighting installation on the institutional corridors, while also identifying Yingge ceramic and kiln context.
    - superscript:
      - link "[12]":
        - /url: "#ref-12"
    - text: The full 2025 public-art announcement instead lists Reed Flower Street Lamp for LB08 in its station-by-station assignment.
    - superscript:
      - link "[9]":
        - /url: "#ref-9"
    - text: That same individual LB08 record separately places Flower Street Lamp on the corridor toward the New Taipei Art Museum, so the records describe both Tao Xiang and a street-lamp work in the LB08 -area programme.
    - superscript:
      - link "[12]":
        - /url: "#ref-12"
    - text: The 2026 announcement omits LB08 from its station-by-station sentence while calling the programme 12 works, so it does not resolve the earlier LB08 assignment difference.
    - superscript:
      - link "[10]":
        - /url: "#ref-10"
    - text: These are conflicting official public-art assignments and descriptions, not values to average or silently reconcile.
    - superscript:
      - link "[9]":
        - /url: "#ref-9"
    - text: The fetched primary records do not establish a separate LB08 civil contract value, final account, individual architect, complete art cost, rename gazette or confirmed feeder-bus stop-ID join.
    - superscript:
      - link "[7]":
        - /url: "#ref-7"
    - text: The unresolved station-level fields remain TBC; the planned weather-corridor time remains distinct from an observed transfer time.
    - superscript:
      - link "[13]":
        - /url: "#ref-13"
    - text: DORTS’s full LB08 art record presents “陶鄉” as a ceramic- and kiln-firing-inspired landmark and practical lighting installation for the corridors linking Yingge’s local institutions.
    - superscript:
      - link "[12]":
        - /url: "#ref-12"
    - text: A DORTS builder article from September 2022 describes the planned weather corridor linking LB08 to TRA Yingge and, by a bridge, the New Taipei Art Museum; it says the walk to the museum was planned at seven minutes.
    - superscript:
      - link "[13]":
        - /url: "#ref-13"

  - heading "Station context" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: DORTS identifies O21 as the Xinzhuang Line terminal at the boundary between Xinzhuang Depot and Zhongzheng Road.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: Because the road structure needed at least 4.5 metres of cover, parts of the concourse and platform plans had to be staggered rather than aligned in a single rectangle.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: The street arrangement places two northern entrances, an emergency exit and ventilation facilities along Zhongzheng Road, with a southern entrance and shaft reached through a crossing route.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: The concourse is divided into paid, unpaid and administrative areas, while the west end houses traction-power, mechanical, environmental-control and other service rooms.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: DORTS gives the concourse a length of about 260 metres and a width of 19.55 metres, and the island platform about 251.5 metres.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: The western non-public area includes a driver dispatch centre with staff facilities, while the eastern end contains signalling, communications, battery and uninterruptible-power equipment.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: The station entrances and depot entrances are arranged together along Zhongzheng Road, so their colours and forms were planned as one visible frontage.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: The depot palette is described as light pink and grey-white, while the station entrances retain their own visibility, transparency and liveliness.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: To reduce surface clutter, DORTS places a cooling tower above a ventilation shaft and reserves street-level land for planting, paving and public art.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: Transfer parking is also reserved at the street edge, making the terminal a depot interface and a local access point rather than only a platform below ground.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: The Control Yuan investigation records that the depot site was selected at the Losheng Sanatorium after an earlier plan for land east of Fu Jen University could not provide enough land.
    - superscript:
      - link "[8]":
        - /url: "#ref-8"
    - text: The same investigation records a 2002 construction start, resident-relocation arrangements and cracking near the work area during excavation.
    - superscript:
      - link "[8]":
        - /url: "#ref-8"
    - text: It also records partial stoppage from July 2004 while the authorities dealt with the new hospital, cultural-preservation dispute and site handover.
    - superscript:
      - link "[8]":
        - /url: "#ref-8"
    - text: The Control Yuan reported an estimated 37.5-month delay and about NT$7.3 billion in added and claim-related costs; those are investigation estimates, not a final station account.
    - superscript:
      - link "[8]":
        - /url: "#ref-8"
    - text: A separate Control Yuan correction found that the depot siting, land handover, slope risk and damage to some sanatorium buildings involved administrative failings and construction consequences.
    - superscript:
      - link "[7]":
        - /url: "#ref-7"
    - text: The New Taipei gazette records Losheng as a historical building on 7 September 2009 at Zhongzheng Road 794, with the registration covering the historic-building scope stated there.
    - superscript:
      - link "[9]":
        - /url: "#ref-9"
    - text: DORTS later recorded the depot entering operation on 4 January 2021 after the preservation-related configuration changes, while the entrance-landscape project was handled separately.
    - superscript:
      - link "[2]":
        - /url: "#ref-2"
    - text: Its FAQ states that the depot was operating even while the entrance project was suspended and that any later work had to be coordinated around depot operations.
    - superscript:
      - link "[6]":
        - /url: "#ref-6"
    - text: A geotechnical book labels the fault-protection comparison as source-era O59 for Huilong and O60 for Danfeng; the current station pages use O21 and O20 .
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"
    - text: The two code sets measure project-era engineering labels and current operating codes, so both remain visible in the station history.
    - superscript:
      - link "[2]":
        - /url: "#ref-2"
    - text: The fetched primary pages do not establish O21 civil contract value, final account, architect, rename gazette, complete current art inventory or a full transfer classification.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: Those fields remain TBC rather than being inferred from the depot dispute or the terminal layout.
    - superscript:
      - link "[10]":
        - /url: "#ref-10"
    - text: O21 ’s road-cover constraint required at least 4.5 metres of overburden, so DORTS staggered parts of the concourse and platform plans; depot and station entrances are coordinated along Zhongzheng Road, with street land reserved for landscape, art and transfer parking.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"

      - listitem:
        - link "Xinzhuang Depot and the Losheng entrance project":
          - /url: https://www.dorts.gov.taipei/News_Content.aspx?n=2A66A485FACB0D5B&s=602D327B2B353759
        - text: 有關衛福部目前所採行之樂生療養院入口意象方案，因樂生保留自救會與青年樂生聯盟反對，以致遲遲無法施作，是否會連帶影響捷運新莊機廠營運？ primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems ( 臺北市政府捷運工程局 ) accessed 2026-08-18 The full DORTS FAQ records that the depot was already operating, the entrance-landscape project had been suspended after a court order, and future works were to be coordinated so depot operations were not affected.
      - listitem:
        - link "Control Yuan correction on the Losheng preservation dispute":
          - /url: https://www.cy.gov.tw/CyBsBoxContent.aspx?n=134&s=3612
        - text: 臺北都會區大眾捷運系統新莊線新莊機廠選址不當糾正案文 primary Control Yuan ( 監察院 ) accessed 2026-08-18 The full Control Yuan correction records the dispute over the depot site, delayed land handover and resident relocation, slope and building damage, and the resulting construction delay.
      - listitem:
        - link "Control Yuan investigation report on Losheng and the Xinzhuang Depot":
          - /url: https://cybsbox.cy.gov.tw/CYBSBoxSSL/edoc/download/54397
        - text: 調查報告：樂生療養院及新莊機廠工程 primary Control Yuan ( 監察院 ) accessed 2026-08-18 The full investigation report records the original depot-site decision, the 2002 start, land and resident-relocation arrangements, cracking near the works, partial stoppage, and the reported delay and added-cost estimates.
      - listitem:
        - link "Losheng Sanatorium historical-building registration gazette":
          - /url: https://web.law.ntpc.gov.tw/Scripts/FLAWDOC03.aspx?ecase=%E5%8C%97%E5%BA%9C%E6%96%87%E8%B3%87&ecode=H00000&eno=09800123211&rtype=E
        - text: 公告「新莊樂生療養院」登錄為本縣歷史建築 primary Taipei County Government / New Taipei City Government ( 臺北縣政府／新北市政府 ) accessed 2026-08-18 The full gazette record gives the 7 September 2009 registration, the Zhongzheng Road address and the historical-building reasons and scope.
      - listitem:
        - link "MRT station architectural design principles":
          - /url: https://www.dorts.gov.taipei/cp.aspx?n=980C85299DA2890A
        - text: 車站建築設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems ( 臺北市政府捷運工程局 ) accessed 2026-08-18 The full DORTS architecture page explains function-first circulation, modular planning, local station themes, public-art integration and the requirement to reduce the visual mass of surface structures.
      - listitem:
        - link "TRTC station accessibility records":
          - /url: https://web.metro.taipei/pages/tw/stationdisabledinfo/
        - text: 車站無障礙設施查詢 primary Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation ( 臺北大眾捷運股份有限公司 ) accessed 2026-08-24 TRTC’s stationdisabledinfo API was fetched for all 121 station records returned by its station-label endpoint. The API publishes station-specific lift/ramp locations, accessible-toilet locations, tactile-paving and stair anti-slip fields. It does not publish nursing-room or platform-gap fields; those remain TBC here.

  - heading "Station context" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: The current DORTS station table identifies Xiangshan as R02 with engineering code R5 , while the DR148 design article uses the construction-era label R05 for the same station.
    - superscript:
      - link "[3]":
        - /url: "#ref-3"
    - text: That article places the station east of Songren Road and west of the Xinyi branch exit of the National Freeway, at the foot of Xiangshan beside Zhongqiang Park.
    - superscript:
      - link "[8]":
        - /url: "#ref-8"
    - text: It records an underground two-level island-platform station with three entrances, and describes Zhongqiang Park as a mature recreational landscape with trees, sports facilities and morning runners.
    - superscript:
      - link "[6]":
        - /url: "#ref-6"
    - text: "The park setting also brought a specific ecological constraint: the Taipei tree frog breeds in the area, so the design treated existing trees and the park’s dense woodland as a protective screen."
    - superscript:
      - link "[8]":
        - /url: "#ref-8"
    - text: CR580B’s station record gives the R05 construction label a body about 220 metres long and 21.8 metres wide, with a 22.4-metre excavation, three entrances and two ventilation shafts.
    - superscript:
      - link "[7]":
        - /url: "#ref-7"
    - text: The contract article records CR580B as a 16-subcontract section awarded on 23 May 2005 to the Taiwan Obayashi–Mutual Construction joint venture for NT$8.272 billion, opened on 1 July 2005 and completed with the line on 23 November 2013.
    - superscript:
      - link "[7]":
        - /url: "#ref-7"
    - text: To reduce the impact on the frog habitat, the ventilation shafts, cooling tower and small underground-substation lifting opening were concentrated in a planted landscape strip on the north side of Xinyi Road instead of being scattered through the park.
    - superscript:
      - link "[9]":
        - /url: "#ref-9"
    - text: Entrances A and D were designed with reduced visual mass and continuous planting, while entrance B sits inside Zhongqiang Park with a shaded waiting plaza, seats and an underground passage beneath the Xinyi branch.
    - superscript:
      - link "[10]":
        - /url: "#ref-10"
    - text: The entrance language uses curved, lightweight transparent glass so daylight reaches the passage by day and the entrance becomes an urban light form at night.
    - superscript:
      - link "[9]":
        - /url: "#ref-9"
    - text: Inside, the station’s main colour plan is a rainbow, with tree-frog ceramic wall panels and an environmental-education display linking the underground space to the protected habitat outside.
    - superscript:
      - link "[11]":
        - /url: "#ref-11"
    - text: The interior programme separates the urban imagery toward the city from frog, butterfly and child imagery toward the park, and carries the same distinction to the platform-level art walls.
    - superscript:
      - link "[11]":
        - /url: "#ref-11"
    - text: DORTS describes Xiangshan’s work as a tree-frog and childhood-memory composition that represents the richness of the local natural environment and invites visitors to experience its distinctive ecology.
    - superscript:
      - link "[5]":
        - /url: "#ref-5"

    - paragraph: 12 of 12 sources on this page are primary — published by the operator, the builder or government.
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - link "R02 Xiangshan station information":
          - /url: https://web.metro.taipei/pages2026/WebStation/099/1
        - text: 車站資訊查詢：R02 象山 primary Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation ( 臺北大眾捷運股份有限公司 ) accessed 2026-08-14 The operator’s full station page publishes the current station address, accessibility facilities, toilets, bicycle access, exit count and numbered exit locations.
      - listitem:
        - link "Tamsui–Xinyi Line route and stations":
          - /url: https://www.dorts.gov.taipei/cp.aspx?n=0AC527D5FC9E596A&s=A60BB323F07BC768
        - text: 淡水信義線 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems ( 臺北市政府捷運工程局 ) accessed 2026-08-14 The builder’s full route page publishes the line’s mixed guideway, station sequence, station table, interchanges and opening chronology.
      - listitem:
        - link "Xinyi Line extension project":
          - /url: https://www.dorts.gov.taipei/cp.aspx?n=0ac527d5fc9e596a&s=CB7BC86DBDA1E44D
        - text: 信義線東延段 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems ( 臺北市政府捷運工程局 ) accessed 2026-08-14 The project page says the CKS Memorial Hall–Xiangshan section has seven underground stations and opened on 24 November 2013.
      - listitem:
        - link "Tamsui–Xinyi Line depot planning":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/ebook/no27/files/basic-html/page27.html
        - text: 捷運工程叢書 精進版－27 捷運機廠規劃與設計 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems ( 臺北市政府捷運工程局 ) accessed 2026-08-14 The full engineering-book page identifies Beitou Depot as the line’s main depot and gives its location in northern Beitou.
      - listitem:
        - link "Xiangshan station public art":
          - /url: https://www.dorts.gov.taipei/cp.aspx?n=2E32DBDC65CAA983&s=E09DC8AE77E47420
        - text: 心蛙朵朵開 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems ( 臺北市政府捷運工程局 ) accessed 2026-08-14 The official public-art page identifies 心蛙朵朵開 by 江洋輝 and 麻粒國際文化試驗股份有限公司, its stainless-steel and epoxy-resin medium, location and 28 June 2013 completion date.
      - listitem:
        - link "Xinyi Line DR148 station design overview":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/JRTST/ebook/no51/files/basic-html/page65.html
        - text: 都會組曲－信義線DR148標建築設計理念 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems ( 臺北市政府捷運工程局 ) accessed 2026-08-18 The full technical-journal page gives the Xinyi Line’s six-station corridor context, construction-era R05 – R10 labels, underground island-platform forms, station sites and the “Metro Suite” design concept. The original-language passages beginning 臺北捷運信義線自羅斯福路 and 信義線整體建築設計構想 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "CR580B Xinyi Line section contract and station works":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/JRTST/ebook/no51/files/basic-html/page100.html
        - text: 捷運信義線土建施工－CR580B區段標之特殊施工及障礙處理 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems ( 臺北市政府捷運工程局 ) accessed 2026-08-18 The full technical-journal page records CR580B’s 16 subcontracts, the joint-venture award, value, dates, R07 / R06 / R05 station construction scales, and the distinction between Taipei 101 structural work and later fit-out. The original-language passages beginning 捷運信義線CR580B區段標 and 二、車站工程規模 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Xiangshan station site and design concept":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/JRTST/ebook/no51/files/basic-html/page73.html
        - text: 都會組曲－信義線DR148標建築設計理念 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems ( 臺北市政府捷運工程局 ) accessed 2026-08-18 The full technical-journal page describes the Xiangshan site beside Zhongqiang Park, the park’s mature trees and facilities, Taipei tree-frog ecology, and the “Song of the Tree Frog” design concept. The original-language passages beginning 象山站( R05 )位於信義路五段 and 因位處四獸山系象山山腳 were checked on the linked page.
      - listitem:
        - link "Xiangshan station landscape protection and entrances":
          - /url: https://ebook.dorts.gov.taipei/JRTST/ebook/no51/files/basic-html/page74.html
        - text: 都會組曲－信義線DR148標建築設計理念 primary Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit Systems ( 臺北市政府捷運工程局 ) accessed 2026-08-18 The full technical-journal page records the retreat of above-ground facilities into a planted north landscape strip to protect tree-frog habitat, and describes the transparent entrance forms. The original-language passages beginning 台北樹蛙是中強公園地區的特色 and 出入口在設計手法上 were checked on the linked page.

    - paragraph:
      - text: Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation (TRTC) is the operating company behind the Taipei Metro. Its own network material describes train formations and service characteristics, while the line pages in this guide keep government construction records separate from the operator's operating record.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: "That distinction matters: a company can publish how a railway runs without being the agency that selected the alignment, let the civil contracts or accepted the works."
    - heading "Operations and fleet responsibility" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: TRTC's
      - link "Wenhu Line":
        - /url: /rail/metro/lines/wenhu-line/
      - text: introduction describes two pairs coupled as a four-car train, an 80 km/h maximum and approximately 420 passengers at the stated standing-density assumption.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
      - text: Those figures belong to that line's published vehicle description; they should not be copied across the high-capacity fleet, whose car lengths, formations and refurbishment histories differ. The rolling-stock pages therefore name their own contracts and technical sources rather than treating “Taipei Metro” as one uniform vehicle family.
      - superscript:
        - link "[1]":
          - /url: "#ref-1"
    - paragraph:
      - text: The operator's vehicle-plant page assigns rolling stock, depot equipment and track-maintenance vehicles by line responsibility. It associates Tamsui–Xinyi work with Vehicle Plant One and
      - link "Beitou":
        - /url: /rail/metro/stations/r22/
      - text: workshop management, for example.
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: "That is a maintenance-organisation statement, not a current overnight-stabling inventory: the cited page does not establish how many sets are parked at each depot on a given night."
      - superscript:
        - link "[2]":
          - /url: "#ref-2"
      - text: The gap is left explicit rather than inferred from the line map.
